issues.title: `GRAPH.UDF LOAD REPLACE` is not atomic: concurrent queries fail with `Unknown function`
issues.body:
### Summary

While a library is being replaced with `GRAPH.UDF LOAD REPLACE`, queries that call its functions can fail with
`Unknown function '<lib>.<fn>'`, even when the new code defines the same functions.

### Reproduction

1. `GRAPH.UDF LOAD repro "function recency(d, a, h) { ... } falkor.register('recency', recency);"`
2. `GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1, 2000) AS i CREATE (:N {dates: ['2025-01-01','2025-06-01']})"`
3. Client A loops on `GRAPH.UDF LOAD REPLACE repro "<same code>"`.
4. Clients B to G loop on `GRAPH.RO_QUERY g "MATCH (n:N) RETURN sum(repro.recency(n.dates, '2026-10-16', 180))"`.

Over 60 s on a fresh container: 28,168 replaces and 32,227 queries, 3 of which failed with
`Unknown function 'repro.recency'` (timestamps in the attached transcript). It is intermittent: across four runs we saw between 1 and 6 failures per minute. A self-contained script that reproduces it is attached (`udf_replace_race.py`: starts a throwaway container, runs the loops, prints a transcript, removes the container).

### Expected

A replace is atomic: a query sees either the old library or the new one.

### Environment

`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` (module ver 60002), `redis_version:8.10.2`.

### Evidence

Reproduced on a fresh `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` container with a self-contained script that starts a throwaway container, runs every step, prints the transcript below and removes the container: [`udf_replace_race.py`](https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/lineage/blob/main/docs/upstream/repro/udf_replace_race.py).

![udf_replace_race](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/lineage/main/docs/upstream/evidence/udf_replace_race.jpg)

<details><summary>Full transcript</summary>

```
# Environment (2026-10-16T11:50:57+00:00)
image: falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2
redis_version: 8.10.2
graph module: 60002

# Setup
$ GRAPH.UDF LOAD repro "<library defining repro.recency>"
  OK
$ GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1, 2000) AS i CREATE (:N {dates: ['2025-01-01','2025-06-01','2026-01-01']})"
$ GRAPH.RO_QUERY g "MATCH (n:N) RETURN sum(repro.recency(n.dates, '2026-10-16', 180))"
  1110.94192323542

# For 60 s: 1 client replaces the library with the SAME code in a loop; 6 clients run the query in a loop
replaces: 28,168
successful queries: 32,224
failed queries: 3
  3 x  Unknown function 'repro.recency'
first failures:
  2026-10-16T11:51:06.218+00:00  Unknown function 'repro.recency'
  2026-10-16T11:51:10.894+00:00  Unknown function 'repro.recency'
  2026-10-16T11:51:43.102+00:00  Unknown function 'repro.recency'

Expected: 0 failed queries (a replace with identical code should be atomic).

# Done: throwaway container removed
```

</details>

issues.title: Read-only graph ACLs from the docs (`%R~pattern`) refuse `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` on 6.0.2
issues.body:
### Summary

The ACL page (https://docs.falkordb.com/commands/acl) describes `%R~<pattern>` as read-only access to a graph, with two examples: `+@all ~app1:* %R~app2:*` and `ACL SETUSER reader on >pass +GRAPH.RO_QUERY %R~*`. On 6.0.2 both refuse a plain `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` with `NOPERM No permissions to access a key`. Graph commands seem to declare their key as read-write, so a read-only key pattern never matches.

### Reproduction

```
GRAPH.QUERY app2:users "CREATE (:U)"
ACL SETUSER reader_doc on >pass +GRAPH.RO_QUERY %R~*
AUTH reader_doc pass
GRAPH.RO_QUERY app2:users "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)"
-> NOPERM No permissions to access a key
```

Same result for `ACL SETUSER rw_doc on >pass +@all ~app1:* %R~app2:*` reading `app2:users`.
`ACL LOG` shows `reason: key`, `object: app2:users`.

### Expected

`GRAPH.RO_QUERY` succeeds; `GRAPH.QUERY` with a write clause is refused.

### Workaround that works on 6.0.2

```
ACL SETUSER agent on >pass resetkeys -@all +@connection +INFO \
    ~app1:* +GRAPH.QUERY +GRAPH.RO_QUERY \
    (~app2:* +GRAPH.RO_QUERY)
```

Reads of `app2:*` succeed, `GRAPH.QUERY app2:users "CREATE ..."` is refused, and a write sent through
`GRAPH.RO_QUERY` is rejected by the engine. `+INFO` is needed because clients call `INFO` on connect.
`ACL DRYRUN <user> GRAPH.RO_QUERY app2:users ...` checks a rule set safely.

### Environment

`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` (module ver 60002), `redis_version:8.10.2`.

### Suggestion

Either declare a read-only key spec for `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` (and the other read commands) so `%R~` works as documented, or show the selector form on the ACL page. Happy to open a docs PR with the selector example.

### Evidence

Reproduced on a fresh `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` container with a self-contained script that starts a throwaway container, runs every step, prints the transcript below and removes the container: [`acl_readonly.sh`](https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/lineage/blob/main/docs/upstream/repro/acl_readonly.sh).

![acl_readonly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/lineage/main/docs/upstream/evidence/acl_readonly.jpg)

<details><summary>Full transcript</summary>

```

# Environment (2026-10-16T11:49:15Z)
image: falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2
redis_version:8.10.2
graph module: 60002

# A graph to read
$ GRAPH.QUERY app2:users "CREATE (:U)"
Labels added: 1

# Docs example 1 (docs.falkordb.com/commands/acl): read-only user
$ ACL SETUSER reader_doc on >pass +GRAPH.RO_QUERY %R~*
OK
$ (as reader_doc) GRAPH.RO_QUERY app2:users "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)"
NOPERM No permissions to access a key


# Docs example 2: full access to app1:*, read-only access to app2:*
$ ACL SETUSER rw_doc on >pass +@all ~app1:* %R~app2:*
OK
$ (as rw_doc) GRAPH.RO_QUERY app2:users "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)"
NOPERM No permissions to access a key


# Why: the ACL log says the key was refused
$ ACL LOG 1
reason key
context toplevel
object app2:users
username rw_doc

# Workaround: a Redis ACL selector that grants only GRAPH.RO_QUERY on the read-only pattern
$ ACL SETUSER agent on >pass resetkeys -@all +@connection +INFO ~app1:* +GRAPH.QUERY +GRAPH.RO_QUERY (~app2:* +GRAPH.RO_QUERY)
OK
$ (as agent) GRAPH.RO_QUERY app2:users "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)"   # read: allowed
count(n)
1
$ (as agent) GRAPH.QUERY app2:users "CREATE (:Hacked)"             # write: refused
NOPERM No permissions to access a key
$ (as agent) GRAPH.QUERY app1:own "CREATE (:Mine)"                 # own graph: allowed
Labels added: 1
$ GRAPH.RO_QUERY app2:users "MATCH (h:Hacked) RETURN count(h)"     # nothing was written
0

# Done: throwaway container removed
```

</details>

issues.title: The IN operator fails to perform value-based equality checks for nested lists (tuples), silently evaluating to false
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
According to the openCypher specification, equality and list inclusion checks (such as the IN operator) must perform value-based deep equality for complex types like lists/arrays.

When evaluating whether a dynamically constructed list exists within an aggregated list of lists (e.g., [a.id, b.id] IN [[1, 2], [2, 3]]), the evaluator should return true if the elements match. However, FalkorDB silently evaluates this to false and drops all rows. This strongly suggests that the scalar expression evaluator is incorrectly performing pointer/reference equality rather than deep value comparisons for nested lists.


**To Reproduce**
```
// 1. Setup a simple 3-node, 2-edge graph
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_tuple_in "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_tuple_in "CREATE (v1:V {id: 1}), (v2:V {id: 2}), (v3:V {id: 3}), (v1)-[:E]->(v2), (v2)-[:E]->(v3)"

// 2. Direct pattern match (Returns 2 as expected)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_tuple_in "MATCH (a:V)-[:E]->(b:V) RETURN count(*) AS match_direct"
1) 1) "match_direct"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 2

// 3. Tuple filtering via IN operator (BUG: Returns 0)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_tuple_in "MATCH (x:V)-[:E]->(y:V) WITH collect([x.id, y.id]) AS valid_pairs MATCH (a:V), (b:V) WHERE [a.id, b.id] IN valid_pairs RETURN count(*) AS match_via_tuple_in"
1) 1) "match_via_tuple_in"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 0

```

**Expected Behavior**
The IN operator must evaluate nested lists by comparing their values, not their memory references. The second query is logically equivalent to the first and must return 2.

Verification on other openCypher engines:
Neo4j 5.x: Returns 2
Memgraph 3.x: Returns 2

**Actual Behavior**
FalkorDB returns 0. The IN operator fails to match identical lists when evaluating [a.id, b.id] IN [[1, 2], [2, 3]], breaking all queries that rely on composite key filtering or tuple-based subset assertions.

**Cross-engine comparison**

```

issues.title: Relationship isomorphism (edge uniqueness) is erroneously dropped in a single MATCH clause when relationship variables are anonymous
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
According to the openCypher specification's Relationship Isomorphism rule, a single MATCH pattern cannot traverse the exact same physical relationship twice. In a simple graph without parallel edges, a pattern that loops back via the same edge, such as MATCH (u)-[:INC]->(e)<-[:INC]-(u), must return 0.However, FalkorDB drops this isomorphism constraint when the relationship variables are omitted (anonymous). In such cases, the query planner appears to degrade the pattern into an unconstrained matrix multiplication (evaluating the trace of the incidence matrix product $B \cdot B^T$), incorrectly returning 6 instead of 0.This AST/Planner inconsistency is proven by the fact that simply naming the variables (-[r1:INC]-> ... <-[r2:INC]-) restores the expected isomorphism check and correctly returns 0.

**To Reproduce**
```
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
1) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.132911 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 1"

// 1. Create a simple bipartite incidence graph (6 physical edges total)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (v1:V {id: 1}), (v2:V {id: 2}), (v3:V {id: 3}), (e1:Edge), (e2:Edge), (e3:Edge), (v1)-[:INC]->(e1)<-[:INC]-(v2), (v2)-[:INC]->(e2)<-[:INC]-(v3), (v3)-[:INC]->(e3)<-[:INC]-(v1)"
1) 1) "Labels added: 2"
   2) "Nodes created: 6"
   3) "Properties set: 3"
   4) "Relationships created: 6"

// 2. Query with ANONYMOUS edges (BUG: Returns 6)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (u:V)-[:INC]->(e:Edge)<-[:INC]-(u:V) RETURN count(*) AS iso_implicit"
1) 1) "iso_implicit"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 6

// 3. Query with NAMED edges (Correct: Returns 0)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (u:V)-[r1:INC]->(e:Edge)<-[r2:INC]-(u:V) RETURN count(*) AS iso_named"
1) 1) "iso_named"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 0

// 4. Query with explicit inequality (Correct: Returns 0)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (u:V)-[r1:INC]->(e:Edge), (u)-[r2:INC]->(e) WHERE r1 <> r2 RETURN count(*) AS iso_explicit"
1) 1) "iso_explicit"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 0

```

**Expected Behavior**
The pattern MATCH (u:V)-[:INC]->(e:Edge)<-[:INC]-(u:V) contains a single graph pattern (one isomorphism scope). Regardless of whether relationship variables are explicitly named or left anonymous, the engine must enforce relationship uniqueness and not traverse the same physical edge twice. It must return 0.

**Actual Behavior**
The query with anonymous relationships returns 6. It bypasses the isomorphism constraint, allowing the engine to traverse the same physical edge twice (out and then in), treating the operation as a pure linear algebra inner product rather than a strictly isomorphic graph pattern match.

**Cross-engine comparison**
```
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
1) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.132911 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 1"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (v1:V {id: 1}), (v2:V {id: 2}), (v3:V {id: 3}), (e1:Edge), (e2:Edge), (e3:Edge), (v1)-[:INC]->(e1)<-[:INC]-(v2), (v2)-[:INC]->(e2)<-[:INC]-(v3), (v3)-[:INC]->(e3)<-[:INC]-(v1)"
1) 1) "Labels added: 2"
   2) "Nodes created: 6"
   3) "Properties set: 3"
   4) "Relationships created: 6"
   5) "Cached execution: 0"
   6) "Query internal execution time: 1.072989 milliseconds"
   7) "Graph version: 2"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (u:V)-[:INC]->(e:Edge)<-[:INC]-(u:V) RETURN count(*) AS iso_implicit"
1) 1) "iso_implicit"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 6
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 1.700622 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 2"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (u:V)-[r1:INC]->(e:Edge)<-[r2:INC]-(u:V) RETURN count(*) AS iso_named"
1) 1) "iso_named"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 0
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"

127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (u:V)-[r1:INC]->(e:Edge), (u)-[r2:INC]->(e) WHERE r1 <> r2 RETURN count(*) AS iso_explicit"

issues.title: `MATCH (n) WHERE id(n) = 0` returns a node on an empty graph
issues.body:
## Summary

On a graph that has never had a node, looking up a node by id 0 returns a node that does not
exist. It has no labels and no properties. Trying to delete it fails with an internal error that
asks for the bug to be reported. Expected: no rows.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN 1"                                    // create an empty graph
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)"                    // 0
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) WHERE id(n) = 0 RETURN id(n), labels(n), properties(n)"
// 0, [], {}   <- one row is returned (expected: no rows)
```

- The plan is `Project <- NodeByIdSeek`. The seek does not seem to check whether id 0 was ever
  allocated.
- The range form of the seek has the same problem: `WHERE id(n) >= 0` and `WHERE id(n) < 3` also
  return id 0.
- Writing to that phantom node fails: `MATCH (n) WHERE id(n) = 0 DELETE n` answers
  `internal error in the node id space: 0 was never allocated here. No part of this write was
  applied. This is a bug in FalkorDB rather than a problem with the query  please report it`.
- These cases work correctly (no rows):
  - `id(n) = 5` on the empty graph
  - `id(n) IN [0, 1]` on the empty graph
  - `MATCH (n) RETURN id(n)` on the empty graph
  - a deleted id on a non-empty graph
  - id 0 after a node was created and then deleted
- So the problem only appears for id 0 in a graph that has never allocated a node.

## Environment

- FalkorDB 6.0.2 (`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` Docker image, module version 60002)
- Redis 8.10.2
- Reproduced with `redis-cli`, no client library involved

issues.title: 6.0.2 regression: OPTIONAL MATCH with WHERE after an aggregating WITH returns null (works in 4.22.0)
issues.body:
## What happens

On FalkorDB 6.0.2, an `OPTIONAL MATCH ... WHERE` that comes right after an aggregating `WITH` returns null, even though a matching node exists. There's no error, just missing data.

The same query works on 4.22.0.

## Environment

- FalkorDB 6.0.2 (module version 60002), Docker image `falkordb/falkordb:latest` built 2026-10-08
- Reproduced with `redis-cli`, and also through the `falkordb` npm client 6.8.0
- Works on the Docker image `falkordb/falkordb:v4.22.0`

## Steps to reproduce

```cypher
CREATE (p:Person {email:'x'}),
       (r:Rule {status:'revoked', decided_at: 123})-[:SCOPED_TO]->(p)
```

```cypher
MATCH (p:Person)
OPTIONAL MATCH (r0:Rule)-[:SCOPED_TO]->(p)
WITH p, count(r0) AS n
OPTIONAL MATCH (r:Rule)-[:SCOPED_TO]->(p)
WHERE r.status = 'revoked'
RETURN n, r.decided_at AS e
```

**Expected:** `n = 1, e = 123`
**Actual on 6.0.2:** `n = 1, e = null`
**On 4.22.0:** `n = 1, e = 123`

## When it happens

All three of these have to be true:

1. There are two MATCH clauses before an aggregating `WITH`. The first one can be a plain `MATCH` or an `OPTIONAL MATCH`.
2. An `OPTIONAL MATCH` comes right after that `WITH`.
3. That `OPTIONAL MATCH` filters on its new variable, either with `WHERE r.status = ...` or an inline map like `{status:'revoked'}`.

Each of these changes makes the query return the right answer:

- removing the `WHERE`
- filtering on `p` instead of `r`
- having only one MATCH before the `WITH`
- using a `WITH` that doesn't aggregate
- adding an extra `WITH p, n` after the aggregation
- changing the second clause to a mandatory `MATCH`

## Query plan

The filter seems to run before `r` is bound, so it never matches.

6.0.2 (wrong):

```text
Project
    Apply
        Aggregate
            Apply
                Node By Label Scan | (p:Person)
                Optional
                    Conditional Traverse | (r0)->(p:Person)
                        Argument
        Optional
            Conditional Traverse | (r)->(p:Person)
                Filter
                    Argument
```

4.22.0 (correct):

```text
Results
    Project
        Apply
            Aggregate
                Optional Conditional Traverse | (p)->(r0:Rule)
                    Node By Label Scan | (p:Person)
            Optional
                Filter
                    Conditional Traverse | (p)->(r:Rule)
                        Argument
```

On 6.0.2, `Filter` sits below the traverse. On 4.22.0 it sits above it.

## Workaround

Add a plain `WITH` after the aggregation:

```cypher
WITH p, count(r0) AS n
WITH p, n
OPTIONAL MATCH (r:Rule)-[:SCOPED_TO]->(p)
WHERE r.status = 'revoked'
```

## Possibly related

#3351 is also about missing rows on 6.0.2 after an aggregating `WITH`. That one needs a `WHERE` on the `WITH` and a mandatory `MATCH` after it. Here, a mandatory `MATCH` works and only `OPTIONAL MATCH` fails. They may have the same root cause.

issues.title: 6.0.2: after `OPTIONAL MATCH ... WITH n, count(...) AS c WHERE ...`, a filter on a node bound by the next MATCH drops every row (4.22 returns it)
issues.body:
Found while writing a "decisions that only one person wrote" query for Graph Hacks; our two-engine test matrix caught it.

Graph: `CREATE (:P {name: 'ana'})-[:D {v: 5}]->(:Dec {id: 'd1'})`

```cypher
MATCH (d:Dec {id: 'd1'})
OPTIONAL MATCH (:Dec)-[s:S]->(d)
WITH d, count(s) AS c WHERE c = 0
MATCH (x)-[r:D]->(d) WHERE x.name = 'ana'
RETURN count(r)
```

| Variant | 6.0.2 | 4.22.0 |
|---|---|---|
| filter on the new node `x.name = 'ana'` (above) | 0 | 1 |
| `x.name IS NOT NULL` | 0 | 1 |
| filter on the new edge instead, `r.v > 0` | 1 | 1 |
| no `WHERE` after the `WITH` | 1 | 1 |
| `WITH d, count(*) AS c WHERE c = 1`, no `OPTIONAL MATCH` | 1 | 1 |
| filter moved to a later `WITH x, r WHERE x.name = 'ana'` | 1 | 1 |

Expected: 1 on both. It looks like `x` is seen as null by the `WHERE` that follows the next `MATCH`, only when the previous `WITH` has a `WHERE` and follows an `OPTIONAL MATCH` with an aggregate.
Script with all six variants: https://github.com/retailbox-automation/what-leaves-with-them/blob/main/spike/with_where_repro.py

issues.title: Variable-length bound passed as a parameter (`*1..$depth`) fails with "Encountered unhandled type in inlined properties"
issues.body:
Hi! We hit this while building for Graph Hacks.

A variable-length upper bound passed as a query parameter fails on both 4.22.0 and 6.0.2, and the error points at inlined properties, so it took a while to see what was wrong. The blast-radius query in the hackathon guide ("How to Build an Agent That Reasons Over a Graph") uses this form, so other participants will probably run into it too.

Repro (falkordb-py 1.8.0, images falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2 and falkordb/falkordb:v4.22.0, same result on both):

```python
g.query("CREATE (:S {n:'a'})-[:D]->(:S {n:'b'})-[:D]->(:S {n:'c'})")

g.query("MATCH (x:S {n:'a'})-[:D*1..$d]->(y) RETURN y.n", {"d": 3})
# ResponseError: Encountered unhandled type in inlined properties.

g.query("MATCH (x:S {n:'a'})-[:D*1..3]->(y) RETURN y.n")   # [['b'], ['c']]
g.query("MATCH (x:S {n:$n}) RETURN x.n", {"n": "a"})       # [['a']], parameters work elsewhere
```

Expected: the bound accepts an integer parameter, or the error says that variable-length bounds must be literals.
Our workaround: validate the depth as an integer from 1 to 4 in code and format it into the pattern.
Related, but not the same: #1916 (same error text when a parameter is used as inlined pattern properties).

issues.title: algo.WCC and algo.pageRank fail with `-1000` when the nodeLabels projection holds exactly one node (6.0.2)
issues.body:
### Summary

`algo.WCC({nodeLabels: [...]})` and `algo.pageRank('<label>', null)` return an error instead of a result when exactly one node matches the label. This happens however many other nodes the graph has. With zero labelled nodes see #3056 (`-6`). With two or more nodes, both procedures answer correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:Node {id:'a'}), (:Other {id:'b'}), (:Other {id:'c'})"

GRAPH.RO_QUERY g "CALL algo.WCC({nodeLabels:['Node']}) YIELD node, componentId RETURN node.id, componentId"
(error) LAGr_ConnectedComponents failed: -1000

GRAPH.RO_QUERY g "CALL algo.pageRank('Node', null) YIELD node, score RETURN node.id, score"
(error) LAGr_PageRank failed: -1000
```

Controls on 6.0.2:

| query | result |
|---|---|
| same graph, `algo.labelPropagation({nodeLabels:['Node']})` | `a, 0` (correct) |
| same graph, `algo.WCC({relationshipTypes:['R']})` (no label filter) | `a 0`, `b 1`, `c 2` (correct) |
| graph with a single `(:Node {id:'a'})`, `algo.WCC(null)` or `algo.WCC({})` | `a, 0` (correct) |
| graph with a single `(:Node {id:'a'})`, `algo.WCC({nodeLabels:['Node']})` | `-1000` |
| two `:Node` nodes, no relationships, `algo.WCC({nodeLabels:['Node']})` | `a 0`, `b 1` (correct) |

### Expected

One row: `a` in its own component (WCC) and one row with its score (pageRank), as `labelPropagation` already returns.

### Notes

This looks like the 1x1 case of the compact matrix built for a `nodeLabels` projection. #3056 is the 0x0 case and #3029 covers ids under `nodeLabels`. Our case comes up naturally when the projected set is computed per request (for example, a time window that holds a single alert).

### Workaround

Add one isolated anchor node with the label, so the projection always holds at least two nodes, and drop it from the results.

### Environment

`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` @ `sha256:107455e862a824e45e8e9f5a7fbfdf5e00a08b14e13eae2577c72fd9e3f59ba6` (graph module 60002), default config, Docker on Linux x86_64.

Found while building Faultline (github.com/Prashant-thakur77/Faultline), an on-call agent on FalkorDB.

issues.title: SIGSEGV in QueryNode_AddChildren when an IN list on an indexed property contains a full-text stopword
issues.body:
## Summary

A read-only query crashes the server (SIGSEGV, exit code 139) when an `IN` list on an indexed node property contains a string that is a stopword of the label's full-text index.

## Environment

- `falkordb/falkordb:latest`, image config digest `sha256:620a4bff89fe089f9218886696a523f5b4bf033e0603ffb534255c8d4bf66525` (FalkorDB 4.18.11, Redis 8.6.3)
- Seen in production through graphiti-core 0.28.2, which creates full-text indexes on `Episodic`/`Entity`/`Community` with a stopword list

## Minimal reproduction

```
GRAPH.QUERY t "CALL db.idx.fulltext.createNodeIndex({label:'L', stopwords:['a']}, 'x')"
GRAPH.QUERY t "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.u)"
GRAPH.QUERY t "CREATE (:L {u:'a'}), (:L {u:'b'})"
GRAPH.RO_QUERY t "MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.u IN ['b'] RETURN n.u"   -- works
GRAPH.RO_QUERY t "MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.u IN ['a'] RETURN n.u"   -- server crashes
```

Reproduced on a fresh container on 2026-10-15: the last query ends the process with exit code 139 (not OOM).

## Crash report (production, two occurrences)

```
signal 11 (SIGSEGV), si_code 1, address 0x20
QueryNode_AddChildren+0xf4
QueryNode_AddChild
Index_BuildQueryTree
ExecutionPlan_Execute
```

The query at the time was of the form `MATCH (e:Episodic) WHERE e.uuid IN [..., 'a', ...] OR e.created_at >= '...' RETURN ...`.

## Analysis (from source, not verified with a debugger)

- In `src/index/index_query.c`, `_FilterTreeToMultiValQueryNode` (for `prop IN [strings]`), and `_FilterTreePredicateToQueryNode` for string `=` inside an OR, create a token node per value with `RediSearch_CreateTokenNode(...)` and attach it to a TAG node without a NULL check.
- `RediSearch_CreateTokenNode` returns `NULL` when the token is a stopword of the index (case-insensitive).
- `QueryNode_AddChildren` then dereferences `child->type`, which matches the fault address 0x20.
- Range predicates in an AND context go through `_compose_ranges` and do not crash.
- The code path looks unchanged in v4.20.7, v4.22.0 and master. We did not test 6.0.x.

## Suggested fix

Skip, or treat as a literal match, a `NULL` child returned by `RediSearch_CreateTokenNode` in both code paths, instead of passing it to `QueryNode_AddChildren`.

## Workaround

Wrap the property, e.g. `toString(n.u) IN [...]`, so the planner does not build index token nodes. Alternatively, filter out values that are stopwords.

issues.title: Consecutive MATCH clauses are illegally fused into a single isomorphism scope, erroneously enforcing relationship uniqueness across separate MATCH clauses
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
According to the openCypher specification, relationship uniqueness (isomorphism) is scoped strictly per MATCH clause: while a single clause MATCH (a)-[r1:E]->(b), (a)-[r2:E]->(b) requires r1 <> r2, two separate clauses MATCH (a)-[r1:E]->(b) MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) evaluate their relationship uniqueness independently and join on the bound nodes a and b. Consequently, separating two MATCH clauses with a pass-through WITH a, b, r1 is a pure relational identity transformation.

However, FalkorDB erroneously merges consecutive MATCH clauses into a single relationship uniqueness scope when no WITH clause separates them. On a graph with a single edge (1)-[:E]->(2), MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) enforces r1 <> r2 across clauses and returns 0, whereas the semantically equivalent query with WITH a, b, r1 (as well as Neo4j and Memgraph on both queries) correctly returns 1.

**To Reproduce**

```
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_fusion_mre "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
1) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.147782 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 1"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_fusion_mre "CREATE (:V {id: 1})-[:E]->(:V {id: 2})"
1) 1) "Labels added: 1"
   2) "Nodes created: 2"
   3) "Properties set: 2"
   4) "Relationships created: 1"
   5) "Cached execution: 0"
   6) "Query internal execution time: 1.073790 milliseconds"
   7) "Graph version: 2"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_fusion_mre "MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) WITH a, b, r1 MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) RETURN count(r1) AS cnt_with_barrier"
1) 1) "cnt_with_barrier"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 1
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.420409 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 2"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_fusion_mre "MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) RETURN count(r1) AS cnt_multi_match"
1) 1) "cnt_multi_match"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 0
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.317277 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 2"
```

**Expected Behavior**
Both queries are semantically equivalent under openCypher relationship uniqueness rules and must return 1 (as verified in Neo4j and Memgraph). Relationship uniqueness must only be enforced within each individual MATCH clause, not across separate MATCH clauses.

**Actual Behavior**
FalkorDB fuses the two consecutive MATCH clauses into a single isomorphism scope and enforces r1 <> r2, causing cnt_multi_match to return 0 instead of 1.


**Cross-engine comparison**
```
memgraph> MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n;
Empty set (round trip in 0.001 sec)
5 nodes have been deleted.
7 relationships have been deleted.
memgraph> CREATE (:V {id: 1})-[:E]->(:V {id: 2});
Empty set (round trip in 0.001 sec)
2 labels have been created.
2 nodes have been created.
1 relationships have been created.
memgraph> MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) WITH a, b, r1 MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) RETURN count(r1) AS cnt_with_barrier;
+------------------+
| cnt_with_barrier |
+------------------+
| 1                |
+------------------+
1 row in set (round trip in 0.001 sec)
INFO: Sequential scan will be used on symbol `a` although there is a filter on labels :V. Consider creating a label index.
memgraph> MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) RETURN count(r1) AS cnt_multi_match;
+-----------------+
| cnt_multi_match |
+-----------------+
| 1               |
+-----------------+
1 row in set (round trip in 0.001 sec)
INFO: Sequential scan will be used on symbol `a` although there is a filter on labels :V. Consider creating a label index.

===

neo4j@neo4j>  MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n;
0 rows
ready to start consuming query after 2 ms, results consumed after another 0 ms
Deleted 5 nodes, deleted 7 relationships
neo4j@neo4j> CREATE (:V {id: 1})-[:E]->(:V {id: 2});
0 rows
ready to start consuming query after 29 ms, results consumed after another 0 ms
Created 2 nodes, created 1 relationship, set 2 properties, added 2 labels
neo4j@neo4j> MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) WITH a, b, r1 MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) RETURN count(r1) AS cnt_with_barrier;
+------------------+
| cnt_with_barrier |
+------------------+
| 1                |
+------------------+

1 row
ready to start consuming query after 48 ms, results consumed after another 1 ms
neo4j@neo4j> MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) RETURN count(r1) AS cnt_multi_match;
+-----------------+
| cnt_multi_match |
+-----------------+
| 1               |
+-----------------+

1 row
ready to start consuming query after 42 ms, results consumed after another 1 ms
```

issues.title: accept index trimmed values
issues.body: Resolve: #3345 --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a server crash when a UNIQUE constraint's value is empty, whitespace-only, or trimmed by RediSearch (for example `" abc"`). Resolves #3345. The commit-time duplicate check looks the value up in the TAG index, but such values don't round-trip, so the lookup returns NULL; the code dereferenced it, and the guard was compiled out in release builds. - The constraint is now treated as satisfied for values that can't be looked up, so they're accepted without duplicate detection. - Genuine duplicates with normal values are still rejected. - Adds regression tests for sync and async constraint creation. Written for commit fb6bc957915eb323df7afcce407f2741b5cde0c5. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: Segfault (NULL deref) in EnforceUniqueEntity when a UNIQUE-constrained string value is empty or whitespace-padded
issues.body:
Creating or updating a node/edge whose UNIQUE-constrained string property is empty, all-whitespace, or has leading/trailing whitespace crashes the server with a segmentation fault during write-commit constraint enforcement.

These values don't round-trip through the RediSearch TAG index (it trims surrounding whitespace and can't store an empty token), so the "find myself in the index" lookup in EnforceUniqueEntity returns NULL and the result is dereferenced.

The guarding ASSERT is compiled out in release builds, so production hits the raw NULL deref.

There is now a single config for enabling 64-bit time_t: libc_unstable_time64. This can be set unconditionally; it opts in to 64-bit time_t on the following platforms that use 32-bit by default:

  • 32-bit Linux-GNU
  • 32-bit Linux-uClibc
  • 32-bit Linux-musl. Note that setting this flag also enables some other changes that happend in musl v1.2.

RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=libc_unstable_time64' cargo ...

issues.title: UNWIND before MATCH ... WHERE ... MATCH is dropped from the plan, query silently returns 0 rows
issues.body:
### Summary

When an `UNWIND` variable is used in the `WHERE` of a node-only `MATCH`, and a second `MATCH` then expands from that node, the planner drops the `Unwind` operation. The filter is kept but reads a variable nothing produces, so the query returns 0 rows with no error.

Seen on `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` (`sha256:107455e8…`) and on today's `falkordb/falkordb:edge` (`sha256:a8f008dc…`).

### Steps to reproduce

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:Fact {id: 'billing-v1'})<-[:PREMISE]-(:Link {id: 'l1'})"
```

| query | expected | got |
|---|---|---|
| `UNWIND ['billing-v1'] AS x MATCH (n:Fact) WHERE n.id = x MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)` | 1 | **0** |
| `UNWIND [0] AS nid MATCH (n) WHERE id(n) = nid MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)` | 1 | **0** |
| same as the first, with `WITH n` between the two matches | 1 | 1 |
| `UNWIND ['billing-v1'] AS x MATCH (n:Fact {id: x}) MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)` | 1 | 1 |
| `MATCH (n:Fact) WHERE n.id = 'billing-v1' MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)` | 1 | 1 |

The plan for the first query has no `Unwind` at all:

```
GRAPH.EXPLAIN g "UNWIND ['billing-v1'] AS x MATCH (n:Fact) WHERE n.id = x MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)"
Aggregate
    Filter
        Conditional Traverse | (n)<-(l)
            Node By Label Scan | (n:Fact)
```

With `WITH n` in between, the plan keeps it (`... Project / NodeByIdSeek / Unwind` for the `id()` form) and the count is right.

### Expected

`Unwind` stays under the scan and the filter, and the query returns 1, the same as the `WITH` and inline-map forms.

### Why it bites

This is the usual batch shape, `UNWIND $ids AS x MATCH (n) WHERE ... MATCH (n)-[...]-(m)`, and it fails silently. We hit it in a frontier expansion that kept coming back empty.

### Related

Looks like the same clause-merge rewrite as #3188 and #2972, where the `WHERE` was dropped instead. On edge that case now returns the right count, but a preceding `UNWIND` still gets lost. #2557 is a different `UNWIND` scoping bug, where the unwound value is the traversal anchor.

### Workarounds

A `WITH n` between the matches, an inline property map (`MATCH (n:Fact {id: x})`), or `WHERE id(n) IN $ids` without the `UNWIND`.

issues.title: fix: start a correlated multi-hop OPTIONAL MATCH / pattern predicate from the bound node
issues.body: Closes #3332 ## Problem `MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o:O) RETURN count(o)` was planned from the labelled far end: ``` Optional Conditional Traverse | (_anon_1)<-(p:P) Records produced: 1 Conditional Traverse | (o)<-(_anon_1) Records produced: 20000 Argument ``` The planner tapped the outer row into the OPTIONAL MATCH sub-plan with an opaque `Argument(None)` (`add_argument_to_leaves(&mut match_plan, None)`). `select_scan_node` only scores an endpoint as *bound* (score 3) when the child operator says it binds it, and `Argument(None)` says nothing, so `p` scored 0 and the labelled `o:O` (score 1) won. Without the label the two tied and `p` won only on the position tiebreak, which is why the issue's table shows the label as the trigger. Pattern predicates (`WHERE (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(:O)`, SemiApply) and pattern comprehensions had the same opaque `Argument` and the same plan; `CALL { WITH p OPTIONAL MATCH ... }` hits it through the inner OPTIONAL MATCH. ## Fix Pass the variables visited so far (read before the pattern is planned) to the `Argument` for OPTIONAL MATCH, pattern predicates (SemiApply/AntiSemiApply) and pattern comprehensions, the same way MERGE already does (`Argument(Some(bound))`). `select_scan_node` then sees `p` as bound and starts the chain there, so the existing scoring rule (bound endpoint beats any label) applies inside correlated branches too. No optimizer change; no other pass looks at the `Argument` payload (runtime, `push_filters_down`, `references`, `fuse_optional_traverse` all match `Argument(_)`). When nothing in the pattern is bound by the outer row, the `Argument` is now provably "transparent" and the branch still starts from the best label scan, as before (covered by the test). Plans (issue graph: 20,000 `:P`, 200 `:O`, 20,000 `:M`): | query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | issue (OPTIONAL, label, 2 hops) | `(o)<-(_anon_1)` 20,000 records, then `(_anon_1)<-(p)` | `(p)->(_anon_1) (+1 fused hop)`, 1 record | `Optional Conditional Traverse (p)->(o:O)`, 1 record | | same in `CALL { WITH p ... }` | from `o`, 20,000 records | from `p`, 1 record | from `p`, 1 record | | 3 hops | from `o`, 2 × 20,000 records | from `p` (+2 fused hops), 1 record | from `p`, 1 record | | `WHERE (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(:O)` | from the far end, 20,000 records | from `p`, 1 record | from `p`, 1 record | | `[(p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o:O) \| o]` | from `o`, 20,000 records | from `p`, 1 record | from `p`, 1 record | | no label / non-optional / one pattern / one hop | from `p` | from `p` (unchanged) | from `p` | Latency, `GRAPH.RO_QUERY`, release builds, macOS arm64 (p50 / p99 ms; 500 iterations on the 20k graph, 200 on the 130k one): | query | graph | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---|---| | issue | 20k `:M` into `:O` | 2.593 / 2.718 | 0.212 / 0.286 | 0.225 / 0.278 | | CALL form | 20k | 2.600 / 2.868 | 0.215 / 0.240 | 0.227 / 0.245 | | 3 hops | 20k | 4.488 / 4.852 | 0.212 / 0.235 | 0.226 / 0.244 | | issue | 130k `:M` into `:O` | 15.158 / 16.260 | 0.202 / 0.242 | 0.225 / 0.246 | | CALL form | 130k | 15.153 / 16.111 | 0.217 / 0.283 | 0.227 / 0.255 | | 3 hops | 130k | 27.580 / 29.495 | 0.212 / 0.246 | 0.226 / 0.242 | | no label / non-optional / one pattern / one hop | both | 0.20–0.23 / ≤0.29 | 0.20–0.21 / ≤0.25 | 0.22 / ≤0.28 | Before the fix the cost grew with the relationships into `:O` (2.6 ms → 15 ms); after it is flat and at or below C. ## Tests New flow test `test_optional_match.py::test29_correlated_multi_hop_starts_from_bound_node`: for the issue's query, the `CALL { WITH p ... }` form, a 3-hop variant, a variant whose far node lacks the label (result 0, so the label is still enforced), a pattern predicate, a pattern comprehension, and the four table rows that already worked, it asserts the result, that the first traversal starts at `(p)->`, that no traversal is transposed (`<-`), and that `:O` is never label-scanned. It also checks that an OPTIONAL MATCH with no outer-bound node still starts from `Node By Label Scan | (o:O)`. - Before the fix (main @ 66d4d9d40): fails — e.g. `Conditional Traverse | (_anon_1)<-(p:P)` / `Conditional Traverse | (o)<-(_anon_1)` for the issue's query, the CALL form, 3 hops, the unlabelled-far-node variant and the pattern predicate. - After: passes. Also run on this branch: all 126 files in `flow_tests_done.txt` (1638 tests, 0 failures, incl. test_optional_match, test_call_subquery, test_optimizations_plan, test_path_filter, test_traversal_construction, test_multi_pattern, test_index_scans, test_graph_merge, test_comprehension_functions); TCK done list (2456 scenarios passed, 0 failed); `tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py` (131 passed); `cargo test -p graph --lib` (501 passed; the one failure is the known macOS `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, #2922); `cargo fmt --check`; clippy clean on touched code. ## Interaction with open PRs No textual overlap with #3046, #3099 (both `select_scan_node.rs` only) or #3100, #2981 (other parts of `planner/mod.rs`). Semantically, #3046 changes what `select_scan_node` treats as bound when it keeps an outer child; with this PR the kept child inside correlated branches is more often an `Argument(Some(..))` that binds the chosen start, which is the case #3046 is about, so it is worth re-running its tests after either merges. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the planner so correlated multi-hop patterns (OPTIONAL MATCH, pattern predicates, pattern comprehensions) start from the node bound by the outer row instead of from a labelled far endpoint. - Previously the sub-plan received an opaque `Argument(None)`, so the bound endpoint scored 0 and the labelled one won, walking every relationship into it. - Now the `Argument` carries the variables visited so far, so `select_scan_node` sees the bound endpoint and starts the chain there, matching the existing scoring rule. - Adds a flow test verifying the plan starts at the bound node for the issue's query, the `CALL { WITH p ... }` form, a 3-hop variant, pattern predicates, and pattern comprehensions, and that unlabelled far endpoints still filter correctly. Closes #3332. Written for commit e21cd04173746b0b5baddcf2163e2af4580f5303. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Corrected multi-hop pattern matching in `OPTIONAL MATCH`, subqueries, pattern predicates, and comprehensions when a pattern starts from a node already bound by an outer query. Traversal now starts from that bound node rather than searching backward from the far endpoint, improving result accuracy. * Patterns without an outer-bound starting node can still begin from a labeled endpoint, preserving label-based matching.

issues.title: fix: bound value nesting on RDB/RESTORE decode, property writes and bulk insert
issues.body: Closes #3338 ## Problem `GRAPH.RESTORE` decodes nested `T_ARRAY` values recursively (`Value::decode` in `graph/src/runtime/value.rs`) with no depth limit. A crafted payload with ~60,000 nested arrays exhausts the stack and aborts the server (SIGSEGV). Reproduced on a release build of `main` (8a66c01e5): depth 1,000 restores, depth 60,000 kills the server. ## Fix A shared constant `MAX_VALUE_NESTING = 4096` (plus `value_nesting_error()`) in `graph/src/runtime/value.rs`, enforced where a nested value enters storage: - **RDB / GRAPH.RESTORE decode**: `decode_value(r, depth)` counts depth and, on entry, returns a decode error for a value inside more than 4,096 arrays. Nothing recurses past 4,097 frames. - **Property writes** (`validate_list_property` in `pending.rs`): a list property nested past the cap is refused with `Property values can only be nested up to 4096 levels deep`. Lists can be built arbitrarily deep at runtime (e.g. `reduce(a = 1, i IN range(1, n) | [a])`), so this is checked when a value is stored, not at parse time. Every stored value can therefore always be saved and loaded back. This also covers the stored-value side of public issue #2722. - **GRAPH.BULK INSERT** (`read_property`): the iterative array reader refuses arrays past the cap. The values it built were otherwise walked recursively everywhere else. The effects (replication) decoder stays iterative and uncapped, as its comment explains. Its 5,000-level unit test is unchanged and passes. **Known trade-off:** an existing RDB that already holds a list property nested deeper than 4,096 levels will be refused on load. ## Choosing the cap On a release build, building and then freeing a nested list on a 2 MiB thread (the query pool's stack) survives about 25,900 levels (measured). 4,096 is a wide margin below that and far beyond any nesting real data uses. The new tests run the decoder, encoder, property validation and drop at exactly 4,096 levels on a thread spawned with a 2 MiB stack. ## Tests - Unit (`value.rs` `nesting_tests`): - decode at 4,096 succeeds and 4,097 errors; - a 60,000-deep payload returns an error; - an encode → decode round trip at 4,096, including drop, runs on a 2 MiB-stack thread. - Unit (`pending.rs` `property_nesting_tests`): a property at 4,096 is valid, 4,097 is refused, and the existing errors are unchanged. - Flow (`tests/flow/test_rdb_load.py`): - a real `GRAPH.RESTORE` payload, captured from `GRAPH.COPY`, with the property spliced to depth 10 / 4,096 restores; - 4,097 and 60,000 return an error, the key is not created, and the server answers PING; - nested list properties survive `DEBUG RELOAD`; - a list built to 4,096 levels with `reduce` is stored on a node and a relationship and survives `DEBUG RELOAD`; one level deeper is refused by CREATE and SET on both. **Before (origin/main + the new tests):** - `rdb_decode_refuses_one_past_the_cap` and `a_property_past_the_cap_is_refused` fail: the value is accepted. - `rdb_decode_refuses_the_advisory_payload` aborts the test process: the stack overflows. - Flow `test_restore_refuses_nesting_past_the_cap` fails: the payload restored and the key exists. The crashing inputs were not run against an unfixed server. **After:** - All new unit tests pass. - `test_rdb_load` 6/6 (2 existing + 4 new), `test_encode_decode` 19/19, `test_persistency` 11/11, `test_bulk_insertion` 14/14 and `test_replication` 2/2 pass. - e2e + functions: 131 passed. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 504 passed, 1 failed (`batched_result_emitter::cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, which fails identically on origin/main and is unrelated). - fmt is clean; clippy reports no new warnings in touched code. ## Bench `DEBUG RELOAD NOSAVE` of 1,000,000 nodes, each with list properties (`tags: [..3 strings]`, `v: [i, 2i, [i, 'x'], 1.5]`), release build, 7 runs per side, two alternating rounds: | | median | min | |---|---|---| | base round 1 | 679 ms | 671 ms | | fix round 1 | 659 ms | 653 ms | | base round 2 | 647 ms | 644 ms | | fix round 2 | 681 ms | 653 ms | The difference is within run-to-run noise. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a stack overflow in `GRAPH.RESTORE` and RDB loading where a crafted payload with ~60,000 nested arrays crashed the server. Adds a shared `MAX_VALUE_NESTING` (4096) cap, enforced wherever a nested value enters storage, so values deeper than the cap are refused with an error instead of recursing into a crash. - RDB/`GRAPH.RESTORE` decode, property writes, and `GRAPH.BULK INSERT` now reject values nested deeper than 4,096 levels. - Runtime-built lists that exceed the cap are refused by `CREATE`/`SET`, and the limit matches what the RDB encoder/decoder supports, so every accepted value round-trips. - Existing RDB files containing list properties nested deeper than 4,096 levels will fail to load. **Tests** - Unit and flow tests cover the cap boundary, the 60,000-deep crash payload, and where runtime-built nesting is accepted or refused. - The flow test that captures a real `GRAPH.RESTORE` payload now connects to the server the test actually uses, so it passes in CI where the server runs in a service container. Written for commit 8c2609fdc11687269333751ebd4394d22692c533. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Node and relationship properties support recursively nested lists up to 4,096 levels deep, including after saving and reloading data. * **Bug Fixes** * Values exceeding the nesting limit are rejected during property creation, updates, and data loading. The server remains responsive when handling excessively nested values. * Lists continue to reject NULL elements and non-primitive values, while top-level NULL properties remain valid.

issues.title: UDF value conversion recurses without a depth limit
issues.body:
Converting values between the engine and a UDF (`js_to_value` / `value_to_js` in `graph/src/udf/type_convert.rs`) recursed once per nesting level with no limit. A UDF returning a deeply nested array or object, or an array that contains itself, exhausted the query thread's stack and crashed the server.

Expected: a value nested past a fixed depth is a query error, and the server keeps running.

Tracked as GHSA-frmf-ffvc-mxx5.

issues.title: fix: bound the nesting depth of UDF value conversion
issues.body:
Closes #3337

Fixes uncontrolled recursion in UDF value conversion (GHSA-frmf-ffvc-mxx5).

## Problem

`js_to_value` (UDF result → engine value) and `value_to_js` (engine value → UDF argument) recursed once per nesting level with no limit. A UDF can build an arbitrarily deep array or object in a loop, or an array that contains itself. Converting it exhausted the query thread's stack and the server aborted with SIGSEGV. A UDF returning a 300,000-level array kills the server on `main`.

## Fix

Both conversions now carry a depth and return a query error past `MAX_UDF_VALUE_NESTING`:

```
UDF value nesting exceeds the maximum depth of 1024
```

The check covers arrays, plain objects (maps) and the path members in `js_to_value`, and lists and maps in `value_to_js`. A self-containing array hits the limit and errors instead of recursing forever.

**Why 1,024, and why the stack also grows:** 1,024 is far beyond any nesting real data uses. The cap alone does not keep every build within a 2 MiB worker stack, because each level holds QuickJS handles and an `rquickjs` frame. Measured on a 2 MiB thread with the cap lifted:

| Build | Deepest JS → engine | Deepest engine → JS | Stack per level |
|---|---|---|---|
| release | 2,344 | 3,984 | ~0.9 KB |
| ASAN (CI's debug profile, `opt-level = 2`) | 354 | 354 | ~6 KB |

So each conversion level also runs through `stacker::maybe_grow`, which moves onto a fresh 1 MiB heap segment when less than 128 KB of stack is left. The cap bounds the work; the stack growth means no build's frame size can turn the cap into an overflow.


| Query | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| UDF returning a 300,000-level array | server crashes | query error, server up |
| UDF returning a 300,000-level object | server crashes | query error, server up |
| UDF returning a self-containing array | server crashes | query error, server up |
| UDF returning a 1,024-level array | works | works |

## Tests

- New unit tests in `udf::type_convert::nesting_tests`, run on a 1 MiB thread:
  - array and object at the limit convert, and one level past it is an error;
  - `value_to_js` at the limit converts and round-trips, and one past is an error;
  - the advisory's 300,000-level array and a self-containing array are errors;
  - ordinary nesting round-trips.
- With the guard disabled, the three past-the-limit tests fail on their assertions (they get a value instead of an error). The 300,000-level case isn't run against unguarded code.
- New flow test `test_udf.py::test_deeply_nested_result_is_an_error`: 300,000-level array and object, a 1,025-level array and a self-containing array each return the error, the server answers PING after each, and depth 1,024 plus ordinary nested results still work. `test_udf` passes 47/47 on this branch.
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; clippy clean in the touched file; `cargo test -p graph --lib` 504 passed (the one failure, `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, fails the same way on `main`, #2922); `tests/test_e2e.py` + `tests/test_functions.py` 131 passed.

## Bench

UDF calls converting a small nested value, release builds, 16 clients, 20,000 queries, 3 alternating rounds (p50 / p99 ms):

| Query | `main` (8a66c01e5) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `RETURN b.out()`, a small nested result | 0.207 / 0.575–0.679 | 0.207–0.215 / 0.607–0.615 |
| `RETURN b.id([1,[2,3],{a:[4,5]},'s'])`, nested argument and result | 0.207 / 0.535–0.599 | 0.207–0.223 / 0.575–0.639 |

Within run-to-run noise and redis-benchmark's latency-bucket resolution.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
