issues.title: fix: a parenthesised WHERE uses the index and NodeByIdSeek again
issues.body: Closes #3331 Closes #3187 ## Problem Parentheses around a `WHERE` predicate, or around one of its conjuncts, turn off index and id lookups. Results are correct; only the plan is worse: - `WHERE (n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1)` and `WHERE (n.k = 7) AND n.s = 1` use **Node By Label Scan** instead of **Node By Index Scan** (#3331), with literals or parameters. - `WHERE (id(n) = 42)` uses **All Node Scan + Filter** instead of **NodeByIdSeek**, and `MATCH (a), (b) WHERE ((id(a) = 1) AND (id(b) = 2))` becomes a **Cartesian Product of two All Node Scans** (#3187). The parser keeps an `ExprIR::Paren` node for `( ... )`, which it needs while parsing (`(a < b) < c` is not a chain, `SET (n).x` must open with `(`, `((x))` collapses). The binder copied that node into the bound tree. The optimizer passes (`utilize_index`, `utilize_node_by_id`, filter push-down, Cartesian-to-hash-join) match on the filter root and on the children of a top-level `And`, so a `Paren` hid the predicate from all of them. ## Fix Fixed once in the binder (`graph/src/planner/binder.rs`), so no optimizer pass has to know about parentheses: - The binder drops the `Paren` wrapper. The tree shape already carries the grouping, so `(x)` binds to the same IR as `x`. - The binder merges a nested `And`/`Or` into a parent of the same operator. Both are associative, and operand order is kept, so `(a AND b) AND c` splits into all three conjuncts. Unchanged: column names (they come from the source text, so `RETURN (1 + 2)` is still named `(1 + 2)`), chained comparisons (the parser decides those), `NOT (NOT x)`, and `(a - b) - c` vs `a - (b - c)`. These were checked live against C and match. On a graph of 100k `:A` nodes with an index on `k` (#3331 repro), plus a graph of 1000 nodes for the id cases: | Query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `WHERE n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1` | Node By Index Scan | Node By Index Scan | Node By Index Scan | | `WHERE (n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1)` | Node By Label Scan | **Node By Index Scan** | Node By Index Scan | | `WHERE (n.k = 7) AND n.s = 1` | Node By Label Scan | **Node By Index Scan** | Node By Index Scan | | `WHERE ((n.k = 7) AND (n.s = 1))` | Node By Label Scan | **Node By Index Scan** | Node By Index Scan | | `WHERE (n.k = $k AND n.s = $s)` | Node By Label Scan | **Node By Index Scan** | Node By Index Scan | | `WHERE (id(n) = 42)` | Filter ← All Node Scan | **NodeByIdSeek** | NodeByIdSeek | | `MATCH (a), (b) WHERE ((id(a) = 1) AND (id(b) = 2))` | Filter ← Cartesian(All Node Scan ×2) | **Cartesian(NodeByIdSeek ×2)** | Cartesian(NodeByIdSeek ×2) | Every result is the same in all three columns. ### Benchmark The #3331 repro (100k nodes), `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` latency in ms over 3000 runs after 100 warm-up runs, two rounds, macOS arm64 release build: | `MATCH (n:A) WHERE (n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1) RETURN count(n)` | p50 | p99 | |---|---|---| | Rust before | 1.935 / 1.935 | 2.098 / 2.129 | | Rust after | 0.221 / 0.221 | 0.251 / 0.258 | | C | 0.211 / 0.213 | 0.255 / 0.239 | Rust after is within run-to-run noise of C; the unparenthesised form measures 0.218–0.222 / 0.242–0.253 on both Rust builds. `GRAPH.MEMORY USAGE` is the same on all three (16 MB). ## Tests - **Unit** (`planner::binder::tests`): `parentheses_bind_to_the_same_ir` checks that parenthesised and plain forms bind to identical IR. It covers nested parens, parameters, `(a AND b) AND c`, `OR` groups, `NOT (x IN ([..]))`, the two-id Cartesian case, a parenthesised pattern predicate `WHERE ((a)-->())`, and a `SET` expression. `parentheses_that_regroup_still_bind_differently` checks that grouping which changes meaning is kept: `(a OR b) AND c`, `a - (b - c)`, `(a < b) < c`. The first test fails with the fix removed; the second passes either way. - **Flow**: `test_index_scans.py::test_42_parenthesised_predicates_use_the_index` (literals, parameters, nested parens, `IN`) and `test_node_by_id.py::test_parenthesised_id_predicates` (single id, nested, range, the #3187 two-id Cartesian, with parameters) assert both the plan and the results. - On `main`: both fail, for example `'Aggregate\n Filter\n Node By Label Scan | (n:A)' should contain 'Node By Index Scan'` and `'Project\n Filter\n All Node Scan | (n)' should not contain 'All Node Scan'`. - With this PR: both pass. They also pass on the C module. - Related flow suites all pass: `test_index_scans` (39), `test_edge_index_scans` (30), `test_node_by_id` (4), `test_optimizations_plan` (32), `test_path_filter` (19), `test_query_validation` (51), `test_params` (13), `test_filters` (9), `test_graph_merge` (38), `test_bidirectional_traversals` (12). - TCK done list: 10140 steps passed, 0 failed. `test_e2e.py` + `test_functions.py`: 131 passed. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 503 passed. The one failure, `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, already fails on macOS (#2922). - `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy reports no warnings in `binder.rs`. #3327 (test-only) has reproductions for these two issues. Once this merges, they can move into the suites. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #3331 and #3187: parenthesized WHERE predicates no longer disable index scans and node-by-id seeks. The binder now strips the parser's `Paren` wrapper and splices nested `And`/`Or` into a parent of the same operator, so `(n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1)` and `(id(n) = 42)` bind to the same IR as their unparenthesised forms. A new `ExprIR::and_of`/`or_of` builds flat AND/OR trees across planner and optimizer passes, so filters stay flat after every rewrite. Paren handling is removed from the runtime and vectorised evaluator. - Parenthesized predicates now use the index and NodeByIdSeek. - Column names and chained comparisons are unchanged. - Added unit and flow tests covering literals, parameters, and nested forms. Written for commit d46f80088dc15c5489b71f83036506aedc230d4e. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Parenthesized predicates now behave consistently with equivalent unparenthesized expressions, including when using indexes and node ID lookups. * Nested conjunctions and disjunctions are handled consistently, while parentheses that change expression grouping continue to preserve that grouping. * Predicates combined from pattern attributes and `WHERE` clauses can still use indexes. * **Tests** * Added coverage for parenthesized index scans and node ID predicates, including parameterized queries, range conditions, and merged filters.

issues.title: fix: enforce unique constraints by index lookup, not a label scan per entity (#3330)
issues.body: Fixes #3330. ## Cause `Pending::check_node_constraint` / `check_edge_constraint` rebuilt a hash of every key in the label **once per written entity**, so a commit cost O(written × label size). A single `CREATE` cost O(label), and a bulk insert was quadratic. ## Fix The check now looks each written entity's values up in the constraint's supporting index, as C's `EnforceUniqueEntity` does: - Each `Commit` publishes its index documents before the next one runs (`commit_deferred_indexes`), so the index lags only the commit being checked. - Written entities are compared among themselves through a key set. - Index hits are re-verified against the private graph. An entity that was deleted, lost the label, or was re-valued in this commit does not count. Hits that are themselves written in this commit are skipped, since the key set already covers them. - Without an operational index, or for a value the index can't match exactly (arrays, ints that lose f64 precision, NaN, empty strings), the label is scanned **once for the whole commit**, not once per entity. Semantics are unchanged: the key is still `build_composite_key`, and NULL or absent properties still opt out. ## Numbers These are local release builds on Apple M-series, against the C module (`master`). The first table is the issue's repro. | | C | Rust before | Rust after | |---|---:|---:|---:| | nodes 1–5,000 | 56 ms | 3,101 ms | 16 ms | | nodes 5,001–10,000 | 71 ms | 6,408 ms | 12 ms | | nodes 10,001–20,000 | 148 ms | 26,047 ms | 20 ms | | single `CREATE` at 20k, p50 / p99 | 91 / 152 µs | 2,855 / 3,144 µs | 81 / 174 µs | At 200k nodes (20 batches of 10k, then 5,000 single-row queries each): | | C int | Rust int | C string | Rust string | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | load 200k | 3,269 ms | 335 ms | 408 ms | 369 ms | | `CREATE`, p50 / p99 | 90 / 161 µs | 81 / 159 µs | 73 / 130 µs | 81 / 160 µs | | `MERGE … SET` new, p50 / p99 | 1,019 / 1,238 µs | 93 / 154 µs | 982 / 1,172 µs | 93 / 153 µs | | `SET id` on existing, p50 / p99 | 114 / 148 µs | 91 / 154 µs | 89 / 129 µs | 84 / 150 µs | On Rust the constraint now costs nothing measurable. String `CREATE` with no constraint is 80 / 156 µs, the same as with one. The small remaining p99 gap to C on single string writes, and the memory difference, also show up with no constraint, so they are not part of this issue. The fix adds no persistent state, so memory is unchanged. ## Tests `tests/flow/test_constraint.py::testUniqueConstraintLookup` covers: - a bulk-insert time bound: 35 s before the fix, about 30 ms after, against a 10 s bound - SET onto an existing value, and swapping two values - delete or remove-label followed by re-create in the same query, plus re-adding the label - a duplicate created in an earlier commit of the same query - values that take the scan fallback - composite keys - edges The six semantic tests pass on both the old and the new module; only the timing test fails on the old one. The existing `test_constraint` flow tests (26) and `cargo test -p graph` pass. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the quadratic unique-constraint check: commits previously rebuilt a hash of every key in the label once per written entity, so a commit cost O(written × label size). Unique checks now look each written entity's values up in the constraint's supporting index, as C's `EnforceUniqueEntity` does. **Details** - Written entities are compared among themselves via a key set, and index hits are re-verified against the graph so deleted, unlabelled, or re-valued entities don't count. - Without an operational index, or for values it can't match exactly (arrays, ints that lose f64 precision, NaN, empty strings), the label is scanned once per commit rather than once per entity. Strings containing NUL use the index, since the tag encoding escapes them. - Semantics are unchanged: the key is still `build_composite_key`, and NULL or absent properties still opt out. No persistent state is added. **Benchmarks and tests** - Inserting 10k nodes into a 10k-node label drops from ~26s to ~20ms; a single `CREATE` at 20k goes from ~3.1ms p99 to ~170µs, on par with C. - New flow tests cover duplicates within and across commits, SET collisions and value swaps, delete/remove-label reuse, scan-fallback values, composite keys, and edges. Written for commit aa7663b6f521f6ae5764e252322cecab60afe6ba. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Unique constraints are enforced consistently during bulk inserts, updates, value swaps, and changes involving deleted or relabeled entities. * Composite keys, relationship constraints, and values that require scan-based checks are handled correctly. * Mandatory-constraint checks apply only to affected entities that match the constrained label or relationship type. * **Performance** * Uniqueness checks can run more efficiently when supporting indexes are available.

issues.title: Splitting a path pattern with an aggregating WITH clause loses bound node bindings and returns an empty result
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
On a simple 4-node linear path (1)-[:R]->(2)-[:R]->(3)-[:R]->(4), matching the full 3-hop pattern (a:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(x:V)-[:R]->(m:V)-[r:R]->(b:V {id: 4}) and aggregating count(*) grouped by m.id and b.id is semantically equivalent to matching the first two hops, aggregating WITH m, count(*) AS c1, and then matching the final single hop MATCH (m)-[r:R]->(b:V {id: 4}).

However, while FalkorDB evaluates the full 3-hop query to [3, 1, 4], splitting the pattern with WITH m, count(*) AS c1 causes the subsequent MATCH clause to lose the node binding for m and erroneously return (empty array).

**To Reproduce**

```
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_mre "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
1) 1) "Nodes deleted: 4"
   2) "Relationships deleted: 3"
   3) "Cached execution: 1"
   4) "Query internal execution time: 5.191300 milliseconds"
   5) "Graph version: 3"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_mre "CREATE (:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(:V {id: 2})-[:R]->(:V {id: 3})-[:R]->(:V {id: 4})"
1) 1) "Nodes created: 4"
   2) "Properties set: 4"
   3) "Relationships created: 3"
   4) "Cached execution: 1"
   5) "Query internal execution time: 0.690766 milliseconds"
   6) "Graph version: 4"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_mre "MATCH (a:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(x:V)-[:R]->(m:V)-[r:R]->(b:V {id: 4}) RETURN m.id AS mid, count(*) AS c1, b.id AS bid"
1) 1) "mid"
   2) "c1"
   3) "bid"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 3
      2) (integer) 1
      3) (integer) 4
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.578910 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 4"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_mre "MATCH (a:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(x:V)-[:R]->(m:V) WITH m, count(*) AS c1 MATCH (m)-[r:R]->(b:V {id: 4}) RETURN m.id AS mid, c1, b.id AS bid"
1) 1) "mid"
   2) "c1"
   3) "bid"
2) (empty array)
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 1.705505 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 4"
```

**Expected Behavior**
Both queries are semantically equivalent on this linear path topology and must return the exact same 1-row result:

```
1) 1) "mid"
   2) "c1"
   3) "bid"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 3
      2) (integer) 1
      3) (integer) 4
```

**Actual Behavior**
The second query returns 2) (empty array) (0 rows) after transitioning from WITH m, count(*) AS c1 into MATCH (m)-[r:R]->(b:V {id: 4}).

**Cross-engine comparison**
```
neo4j@neo4j> MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n;
0 rows
ready to start consuming query after 1 ms, results consumed after another 0 ms
Deleted 8 nodes, deleted 6 relationships
neo4j@neo4j> CREATE (:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(:V {id: 2})-[:R]->(:V {id: 3})-[:R]->(:V {id: 4});
0 rows
ready to start consuming query after 1 ms, results consumed after another 0 ms
Created 4 nodes, created 3 relationships, set 4 properties, added 4 labels
neo4j@neo4j> MATCH (a:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(x:V)-[:R]->(m:V)-[r:R]->(b:V {id: 4}) RETURN m.id AS mid, count(*) AS c1, b.id AS bid;
+----------------+
| mid | c1 | bid |
+----------------+
| 3   | 1  | 4   |
+----------------+

1 row
ready to start consuming query after 92 ms, results consumed after another 1 ms
neo4j@neo4j> MATCH (a:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(x:V)-[:R]->(m:V) WITH m, count(*) AS c1 MATCH (m)-[r:R]->(b:V {id: 4}) RETURN m.id AS mid, c1, b.id AS bid;
+----------------+
| mid | c1 | bid |
+----------------+
| 3   | 1  | 4   |
+----------------+

1 row
ready to start consuming query after 81 ms, results consumed after another 1 ms

===

memgraph>  MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n;
Empty set (round trip in 0.001 sec)
4 nodes have been deleted.
3 relationships have been deleted.
memgraph> CREATE (:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(:V {id: 2})-[:R]->(:V {id: 3})-[:R]->(:V {id: 4});
Empty set (round trip in 0.001 sec)
4 labels have been created.
4 nodes have been created.
3 relationships have been created.
memgraph> MATCH (a:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(x:V)-[:R]->(m:V)-[r:R]->(b:V {id: 4}) RETURN m.id AS mid, count(*) AS c1, b.id AS bid;
+-----+-----+-----+
| mid | c1  | bid |
+-----+-----+-----+
| 3   | 1   | 4   |
+-----+-----+-----+
1 row in set (round trip in 0.001 sec)
memgraph> MATCH (a:V {id: 1})-[:R]->(x:V)-[:R]->(m:V) WITH m, count(*) AS c1 MATCH (m)-[r:R]->(b:V {id: 4}) RETURN m.id AS mid, c1, b.id AS bid;
+-----+-----+-----+
| mid | c1  | bid |
+-----+-----+-----+
| 3   | 1   | 4   |
+-----+-----+-----+
1 row in set (round trip in 0.001 sec)
```

issues.title: 6.0.0 regression: OPTIONAL MATCH of two hops from a bound node is planned from the labelled far end
issues.body:
On 6.0.0, an `OPTIONAL MATCH` of two hops that starts from a node already bound, and names a label on the node it ends at, is planned from the far end: it walks every relationship into nodes of that label and only then joins back to the bound node. 4.20.7 traverses outward from the bound node.

### Repro

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (p:P) ON (p.id)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (o:O) ON (o.id)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0,19999) AS i CREATE (:P {id: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0,199) AS i CREATE (:O {id: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0,19999) AS i MATCH (p:P {id: i}) MATCH (o:O {id: i % 200}) CREATE (p)-[:M]->(o)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0,19999) AS i MATCH (p:P {id: i}) MATCH (f:P {id: (i + 1) % 20000}) CREATE (p)-[:F]->(f)"

GRAPH.PROFILE g "MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o:O) RETURN count(o)"
```

### 6.0.0

```
Node By Index Scan | (p:P) | Records produced: 1, Execution time: 0.04 ms
    Conditional Traverse | (_anon_1)<-(p:P) | Records produced: 1, Execution time: 2.35 ms
        Conditional Traverse | (o)<-(_anon_1) | Records produced: 20000, Execution time: 2.55 ms
```

All 20,000 `M` relationships are read to find one.

### 4.20.7

```
Optional Conditional Traverse | (p)->(o:O) | Records produced: 1, Execution time: 0.26 ms
    Node By Index Scan | (p:P) | Records produced: 1
```

### What does and does not trigger it on 6.0.0

| query | plan |
|---|---|
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o:O)` | from the far end, 20,000 records |
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o)` (no label on `o`) | from `p`, 1 record |
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) MATCH (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o:O)` (not optional) | from `p`, 1 record |
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7})-[:F]->(:P)-[:M]->(o:O)` (one pattern) | from `p`, 1 record |
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:M]->(o:O)` (one hop) | from `p`, 1 record |

The same happens when the `OPTIONAL MATCH` is inside `CALL { WITH p ... }`. The answers are right in every case.

### Impact

The cost grows with the number of relationships into the far label and not with what the bound node reaches. On a graph with 130,000 relationships into the far label, a lookup that takes 0.07 ms without the label takes 44 ms with it.

### Versions

Graph module 60000 (`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0`, also `latest`) against 42007 (`falkordb/falkordb:v4.20.7`).

issues.title: 6.0.0 regression: a parenthesised WHERE is answered by a label scan where the index was used
issues.body:
On 6.0.0, a `WHERE` whose conditions are wrapped in parentheses is answered by a label scan, where the same conditions without the parentheses use the index. 4.20.7 uses the index either way.

### Repro

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:A) ON (n.k)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1,100000) AS i CREATE (:A {k: i % 1000, s: i % 3})"

GRAPH.PROFILE g "MATCH (n:A) WHERE n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1 RETURN count(n)"
GRAPH.PROFILE g "MATCH (n:A) WHERE (n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1) RETURN count(n)"
GRAPH.PROFILE g "MATCH (n:A) WHERE (n.k = 7) AND n.s = 1 RETURN count(n)"
```

### 6.0.0

```
-- WHERE n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1
Aggregate | Records produced: 1
    Filter | Records produced: 34
        Node By Index Scan | (n:A) | Records produced: 100

-- WHERE (n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1)
Aggregate | Records produced: 1
    Filter | Records produced: 34
        Node By Label Scan | (n:A) | Records produced: 100000

-- WHERE (n.k = 7) AND n.s = 1
Aggregate | Records produced: 1
    Filter | Records produced: 34
        Node By Label Scan | (n:A) | Records produced: 100000
```

### 4.20.7

All three forms give `Node By Index Scan | (n:A) | Records produced: 100`.

The answers are right in every case; only the plan changes. Parameters in place of the literals behave the same way.

### Impact

Query builders commonly parenthesise a group of conditions, so a generated filter on an indexed property scans the label. On a label of 250,000 nodes that is about 24 ms for a lookup that takes 0.3 ms with the index.

### Versions

Graph module 60000 (`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0`, also `latest`) against 42007 (`falkordb/falkordb:v4.20.7`).

issues.title: 6.0.0 regression: node inserts under a unique constraint are 35-120x slower than 4.20.7 and scale quadratically
issues.body:
Creating nodes of a label that has a unique constraint is far slower on 6.0.0 than on 4.20.7, and the cost per node grows with the number of nodes already in the label.

### Repro

Fresh container, `redis-cli`:

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:A) ON (n.id)"
GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE g UNIQUE NODE A PROPERTIES 1 id
# wait for db.constraints() to report OPERATIONAL
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1,5000) AS i CREATE (:A {id: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(5001,10000) AS i CREATE (:A {id: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(10001,20000) AS i CREATE (:A {id: i})"
```

### Timings

Wall clock, same machine, Docker on an Apple M2 Max:

| statement | `falkordb/falkordb:v4.20.7` | `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0` |
|---|---:|---:|
| nodes 1 to 5,000 | 118 ms | 4,300 ms |
| nodes 5,001 to 10,000 | 155 ms | 8,878 ms |
| nodes 10,001 to 20,000 | 307 ms | 36,280 ms |
| 20,000 nodes, same label, no constraint | 11 ms | 26 ms |

On 6.0.0 the second 5,000 take twice as long as the first, and the next 10,000 take four times as long again, so each insert appears to cost time proportional to the nodes already in the label. On 4.20.7 the cost per node stays roughly flat.

The constraint is `OPERATIONAL` before the inserts on both versions, and both reject a duplicate afterwards (`unique constraint violation on node of type A`). String ids behave the same way as integers.

### Impact

A bulk load into a constrained label is impractical. Loading 750,000 nodes this way did not get past the first few tens of thousands; with a plain range index in place of the constraint, the same 1.1M-node load takes about 10 seconds.

### Versions

Graph module 60000 (`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0`, also `latest`) against 42007 (`falkordb/falkordb:v4.20.7`).

issues.title: support RDB decode short read
issues.body: Resolve: #3140 --- ## Summary by cubic Makes RDB decoding fail cleanly on truncated or corrupt payloads instead of crashing, allocating huge buffers, or looping on garbage counts. - Adds `TryRead*` decoder APIs that latch short reads and jump to an abort handler that tears down the partial graph; the unarmed (offload/RESTORE/COPY) path now frees that graph instead of leaking it. - Enforces hard bounds on counts read from untrusted payloads, so excessive values fail the decode instead of driving huge allocations. - Consolidates all version decoders behind a single `RdbLoadGraph` dispatcher and centralizes the duplicated malformed-payload diagnostics into shared messages. - v14 decoders now reject vector index fields, which that version's wire format predates. - Regenerates baked RESTORE test payloads that were saved in the removed v10 encoding. **Migration** - Drops decode support for encoding versions 10-13 (RedisGraph 2.8-2.12); the oldest loadable payload is now version 14 (FalkorDB v4.0). Written for commit a5579417119bf190a6a3fdf204b030bb26ac1a7d. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: fix: parse module-load arguments like C (case-insensitive, validated, refused on bad input)
issues.body: Closes #3268 ## Problem Module-load arguments (`--loadmodule falkordb.so NAME VALUE ...`) were read by two parsers. redismodule-rs's `module_args_as_configuration` handled the fields registered in `redis_module!`, with case-sensitive names and `value == "yes"` for booleans. An ad-hoc loop in `graph_init` handled the rest, with no `ASYNC_DELETE` arm, plain `parse::()` and no rejection of unknown names or a trailing odd argument. So `CMD_INFO YES` turned telemetry off, `cache_size 10` and `ASYNC_DELETE no` were ignored, and invalid or unknown arguments loaded where C refuses to start. ## Fix There is now one parser, as in C's `Config_Init` (option (a) in the issue, plus Dvir's points): - `module_args_as_configuration` is off. `apply_module_args` (`src/commands/config_cmd.rs`) parses every pair in `graph_init`. Names are ASCII case-insensitive. - Run-time fields go through the same `validate_config_set` + `apply_config_set` as `GRAPH.CONFIG SET`, one pair at a time like C, with the same timeout cross-checks. - Load-only fields get C's `Config_Option_set` rules: - `CACHE_SIZE`, `THREAD_COUNT`, `OMP_THREAD_COUNT`: positive integer. - `NODE_CREATION_BUFFER`: non-negative integer. - `INDEX_WORKER_THREADS` (Rust-only): non-negative integer. - `IMPORT_FOLDER`: any string. - `TEMP_FOLDER`: must exist, be a directory and be writable, with C's messages. - A bad argument refuses the load. The reason is logged at `warning` level using C's texts: - `Encountered unknown configuration field 'FOO'` - `FalkorDB received N arguments, all configurations should be key-value pairs` - `Failed setting field 'X' with error: ...` - `The TIMEOUT configuration parameter should be removed when specifying TIMEOUT_DEFAULT and/or TIMEOUT_MAX` - **Deprecated but accepted.** The engine has no behaviour yet for these C configs: `ASYNC_DELETE`, `DELAY_INDEXING`, `DELTA_MAX_PENDING_CHANGES`, `EFFECTS_THRESHOLD`. They are validated, stored and reported by `GRAPH.CONFIG GET`. They also log `configuration field 'X' is deprecated and has no effect in this version; the value 'V' is accepted and ignored`. - **`BOLT_PORT`** is out of scope, as agreed. It is accepted and unused, as before, with no validation added. - `GRAPH.CONFIG GET/SET` is unchanged. The `graph.*` Redis module configs are still registered, so `graph.X` lines in redis.conf and `CONFIG GET/SET graph.X` still work. Each row starts a fresh `redis-server --loadmodule `, then runs `GRAPH.CONFIG GET`. C is `bin/macos-arm64v8-release/falkordb.so`. | Load args | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `CMD_INFO YES` | `0` | `1` | `1` | | `CMD_INFO garbage` | loads, `0` | refuses | refuses | | `DELAY_INDEXING YES` | `0` | `1` | `1` | | `cache_size 10` | `25` (ignored) | `10` | `10` | | `ASYNC_DELETE no` / `async_delete no` | `1` (ignored) | `0` | `0` | | `timeout_max 7` | `7` | `7` | `7` | | `CACHE_SIZE 0` | loads, `0` | refuses | refuses | | `CACHE_SIZE 5000` | `5000` | `5000` | `5000` | | `THREAD_COUNT 0` | loads, auto (`11`) | refuses | refuses | | `MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES 0` | loads, `0` | refuses | refuses | | `FOO 1` | loads, ignored | refuses: `Encountered unknown configuration field 'FOO'` | refuses (same message) | | `CACHE_SIZE` (odd count) | loads, `25` | refuses: `FalkorDB received 1 arguments, all configurations should be key-value pairs` | refuses (same message) | ### Behaviour changes (need a release note) 1. **Stricter start-up.** The following now stop the server from starting, as they do on C: - a non-yes/no boolean - `CACHE_SIZE 0`, `THREAD_COUNT 0`, `OMP_THREAD_COUNT 0`, `MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES 0` - negative values for non-negative fields (e.g. `EFFECTS_COMPRESSION -1`) - `JS_HEAP_SIZE`/`JS_STACK_SIZE` below 1MB - an unknown name - an odd argument count `THREAD_COUNT 0` used to mean "auto". Leaving `THREAD_COUNT` out still gives the default, one thread per core. Rust's names are a superset of C's, so nothing valid on C is refused. 2. **Module arguments now win over `graph.*` in redis.conf.** I checked with `loadmodule CACHE_SIZE 10` plus `graph.CACHE_SIZE 5` in the same redis.conf: - Before: `GRAPH.CONFIG GET CACHE_SIZE` returned `5`. - After: it returns `10`, and so does `CONFIG GET graph.CACHE_SIZE`. A `graph.*` line with no matching module argument still applies (`5`). Runtime `CONFIG SET graph.VKEY_MAX_ENTITY_COUNT 88` still works. C has no `graph.*` configs, so this affects only Rust-only setups. This changes start-up only, so no runtime benchmark was run. ## Tests New `tests/flow/test_module_args.py` (spawn bucket in CI; added to `flow_tests_done.txt`): - `test01_defaults`: with no arguments, every config keeps its default. - `test02_accepted`: all accepted rows from the table, plus mixed-case names (`Thread_Count 3`, `max_queued_queries 5`, `node_creation_buffer 600` → 1024, `Vkey_Max_Entity_Count 0`, and a valid `TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`/`TIMEOUT_MAX` pair). - `test03_refused`: every refused row, plus `DELAY_INDEXING 1`, `OMP_THREAD_COUNT 0`, `JS_HEAP_SIZE 5`, a 3-argument odd count and the three TIMEOUT conflicts. `Env()` must fail to start. Locally, the test also starts `redis-server --port 0` directly and asserts that the server exits, that the log has the expected message, and that it has `initialization failed. Module not loaded`. - `test04_ignored_configs_logged`: the four ignored configs are accepted and stored, and each logs the deprecation line. Results: - New test on `main`: fails. The 9 mismatched accepted rows, every refused row (all loaded) and the missing deprecation log lines are all reported. - New test with this PR: 4/4 pass. - Existing flow suites with module args, all passing: `test_config` 20/20, `test_timeout` 14/14, `test_cache` 15/15, `test_pending_queries_limit` 3/3, `test_graph_info` 15/15, `test_load_csv` 18/18, `test_encode_decode` 19/19, `test_multi_writer` 2/2, `test_rdb_load` 2/2, `test_replication_states` 1/1. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 499 passed. The one failure is the known `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922, macOS). - `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` are clean on the touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Parses module-load arguments (`--loadmodule falkordb.so NAME VALUE ...`) the way C's `Config_Init` does, closing #3268. Names are now ASCII case-insensitive, values get the same validation as `GRAPH.CONFIG SET`, and an invalid value, unknown name, or odd argument count refuses the load instead of being silently ignored. The parse happens once in `graph_init`, via `apply_module_args` in `src/config.rs`; `config_cmd.rs` shares its validators and setter with `GRAPH.CONFIG SET`. All pairs are validated before any are applied, so a refused load leaves no partial configuration, and pairs are checked in order with the same timeout cross-constraints as C's one-pair-at-a-time `Config_Init`. **Behavior changes** - The server now refuses to start, as in C, on non-yes/no booleans, `CACHE_SIZE 0`, `THREAD_COUNT 0`, `OMP_THREAD_COUNT 0`, `MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES 0`, negative values, unknown names, and odd argument counts. - Module arguments now win over `graph.*` lines in redis.conf, since they are applied after them. - Deprecated C configs (`ASYNC_DELETE`, `DELAY_INDEXING`, `DELTA_MAX_PENDING_CHANGES`, `EFFECTS_THRESHOLD`) are accepted and stored, with a deprecation log line. - New flow test `tests/flow/test_module_args.py` covers accepted, refused, and deprecated arguments. Written for commit 7dfde9b16c64085a1e9be0cbbd538f68baade48a. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Module-load configuration arguments are applied after `graph.*` settings from `redis.conf`, so they take precedence. * Argument names are case-insensitive, and supported settings are validated when the module loads. * **Bug Fixes** * Invalid values, unknown settings, malformed argument lists, and incompatible timeout combinations now cause module loading to fail with an error. * Selected deprecated settings are accepted but ignored, with a notice logged.

issues.title: test: reproduce open Rust-engine issues (S1 and externally reported)
issues.body:
Adds reproduction tests for two sets of open Rust-engine issues, and records how each one behaves on the latest C release:
- each open **S1 (critical)** issue that hits only the Rust engine
- every open Rust-engine bug **reported by someone outside the FalkorDB team**

Closes #3326

<!-- status:start -->
## Status

**Current (2026-10-15):** open, waiting on a rebase. The PR has a merge conflict with `main` and has had no changes since 2026-10-13 11:10 UTC. No human reviewer is assigned yet. 528 CI checks pass; `codecov/patch` fails because the PR adds only test files that CI does not run.

**Next:** rebase onto `main`; remove `testIssue3013` (#3013 is fixed and closed); re-check the #3237 unit test against the new CowBTree fixes; re-run the 18 flow classes on a fresh `edge` image and refresh the results table below; request a reviewer.

**Status page with timelines** (FalkorDB org members only): https://claude.ai/artifact/XMdVaXgD6XnNojmFnB1zGW

### Progress log

| Date (UTC) | PR | `main` since PR base | In-scope issues fixed on `main` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-13 | Opened. 3 commits, +3,632 lines. 13 of 13 review threads resolved. | 0 | 0 |
| 2026-10-15 | No change since 10-13 11:10. Merge conflict with `main`. | 9 commits | 1 (#3013) |
<!-- status:end -->

**Full triage page** (FalkorDB org members only): https://claude.ai/artifact/1ZajBCKvAvnYJz8KKq8rMw. It covers all 727 open issues by engine (Rust v6+, C, or both) and estimated severity, and shows these tests' results on Rust and C.

## What's in it

- **`tests/flow/test_open_rust_s1_issues.py`**: 18 flow-test classes, one per issue (`testIssue<N>`). Each docstring links its issue and names the trigger. Each test asserts the **correct** behaviour, so it fails on today's Rust engine and passes once the issue is fixed.
- **`graph/src/index/falkordb/data_structures/cow_btree/tests.rs`**: one `#[ignore]`d unit test for #3237. A client can't trigger that bug without millions of index entries, so it is tested at small fan-out.

**CI does not run any of these tests.** Several of them crash or hang the server, so the flow file is deliberately left out of `flow_tests_done.txt`, and the unit test is `#[ignore]`d. When an issue is fixed, move its class into the suite that covers the feature (and into CI), and delete it from this file.

**Three issues already had tests on `main`, so they got no new test.** The existing tests pass on both engines, which suggests these bugs are fixed and the issues can be closed:
- **#2749:** `tests/flow/test_constraint.py` `testConstraintSchemaRegistration.test01_a_constraint_on_an_unused_property_survives_a_reload`
- **#2772:** `tests/flow/test_encode_decode.py` `test_encode_decode_rename.test_01_renamed_multi_key_graph_round_trips`
- **#2770:** `tests/flow/test_create_clause.py` `testCreateClause.test19_id_pool_never_reissues_a_live_id` (plus test16–test18, from #2797)

I've commented the test names on each of those issues.

**#3284 has no test.** The virtual-key name collision depends on nanosecond timing (`a = t ^ seq` in `uuid_v4`), so a client can't trigger it reliably. A deterministic unit test would first need `uuid_v4` refactored to take `t` and `seq` as inputs.

## Results

Every test was run against two images, each in a fresh container per class with the CI service config (`FALKORDB_ARGS=""`, `--enable-debug-command yes`):
- **Rust:** `falkordb/falkordb-server:edge` (main, 2026-10-12)
- **C:** `falkordb/falkordb-server:v4.22.0` (latest C release)

| Issue | Opened by | What breaks (severity reason) | Test | Rust `edge` | C `v4.22.0` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #3304 | AviAvni (team) | stack overflow crash | `testIssue3304` | ❌ fails: 2000 chained UNWINDs: stack overflow, raw SIGSEGV, container exit 139, no log line; 300 OPTIONAL MATCH...WHERE also SIGSEGVs (manual probe) | ✅ passes: both chains return [[1]] (2000 UNWINDs in 0.6s, 300 OPTIONAL MATCH in 0.4s) |
| #3284 | AviAvni (team) | RDB save drops graph slice | none | n/a: uuid_v4 (src/redis_type.rs:799) sets a = t ^ seq; not injective, so two virtual keys can share a name and one graph slice is dropped on save | n/a: C names virtual keys with a random UUID_New; cannot collide this way |
| #3279 | AviAvni (team) | trailing MATCH crashes server | `testIssue3279` | ❌ fails: trailing MATCH: panic utilize_node_by_id.rs:106:75, server down (exit 1); UNWIND/OPTIONAL MATCH run; CREATE/MERGE [:R\|S] accepted (wrong result) | ✅ passes: 'Query cannot conclude with ...' and 'Exactly one relationship type must be specified ...' errors |
| #3266 | AviAvni (team) | memory blowup from payload | `testIssue3266` | ❌ fails: 128KB nested-list GRAPH.EFFECT drives used_memory_peak to 4.15 GB before rejection (quadratic reservation); server stays up | n/a: C has no v3 effects decoder; the payload trips C divergence shutdown instead (unrelated) |
| #3237 | AviAvni (team) | panic in CowBTree | `cow_btree/tests.rs` `remove_batch_keeps_non_root_branches_at_least_half_full` (ignored) | ❌ fails: check_invariants panics: 'branch must have >= 2 children … : 1' (cargo test -- --ignored) | n/a: C has no CowBTree; no client-visible trigger at small scale |
| #3150 | andynski (external) | server panics | `testIssue3150` | ❌ fails: server exits (container exit 1); log: FalkorDB panic at src/reply.rs:655:58 Option::unwrap() on None. test02 (collect), test03 (missing property) same. | ✅ passes: all 3 methods pass: [[None,1]], [[None,[1]]], [['b',None,1]] |
| #3031 | AviAvni (team) | panic, graph cannot be saved | `testIssue3031` | ❌ fails: GRAPH.RESTORE of a payload with an orphan multi-edge row -> edge_count panic 'multi exceeds the effective pattern' tensor.rs:1243, container exit 1, server down | n/a: C uses a different RESTORE format; the Rust-format payload just hangs the C client (server stays up) |
| #3013 | AviAvni (team) | server hangs when queue full | `testIssue3013` | ❌ fails: 1200 concurrent heavy writes over 16 graphs deadlock the Redis main thread; PING stops answering until the container is killed | ✅ passes: server completes the flood and keeps answering PING |
| #3003 | AviAvni (team) | parser hang forever | `testIssue3003` | ❌ fails: 'RETURN shortestPath((a)-[{' never answers (30s client socket timeout); worker spins; server still answers PING | ✅ passes: all 5 inputs return 'Invalid input ...' syntax errors promptly |
| #2994 | AviAvni (team) | corrupt RESTORE crashes server | `testIssue2994` | ❌ fails: GRAPH.RESTORE of a truncated multi-edge blob -> decode_blob assert 'GxB_Vector_deserialize failed: GrB_INVALID_OBJECT' vector.rs:222, container exit 1, server down | n/a: C uses a different RESTORE format; the Rust-format payload just hangs the C client (server stays up) |
| #2974 | AviAvni (team) | UDF forgery crashes server | `testIssue2974` | ❌ fails: test01: CREATE accepts forged node 7, dangling edge (2 edges). test02: panic graph/src/graph/graph.rs:3365, SIGABRT, container exit 133 | ✅ passes: both queries rejected with type errors (forged object is a Map); server alive |
| #2972 | AviAvni (team) | WHERE dropped, deletes unmatched data | `testIssue2972` | ❌ fails: var-length shape: WHERE a.v=99 ... DETACH DELETE b deletes 3 nodes/3 rels (expected 0). test02-04 also fail (UNWIND lost 2!=4, x unbound [] vs [[7,2]], varlen rows). | ✅ passes: all 5 methods pass |
| #2946 | AviAvni (team) | replication/AOF load failure, divergence | `testIssue2946` | ❌ fails: replica refuses the next GRAPH.EFFECT ('assigns label B id 1, replica would assign 0'), forced full resync, replica missing the B node | ✅ passes: replica converges, no forced resync |
| #2930 | AviAvni (team) | panic crashes server | `testIssue2930` | ❌ fails: week:1e10 panics temporal.rs:83:29, server down; dayOfQuarter:200 returns 2021-07-19; 'W1é' (temporal.rs:258) and chrono TimeDelta panics in probes | ✅ passes: 'Invalid value for week/dayOfQuarter (valid values ...)', 'Failed to parse date' |
| #2895 | AviAvni (team) | crash bypassing depth guard | `testIssue2895` | ❌ fails: SET n.a x5000 = 1: stack overflow, SIGSEGV, container exit 139; REMOVE chain and 500 nested FOREACH also SIGSEGV (manual probes) | ✅ passes: SET/REMOVE chains rejected with errors; 500 nested FOREACH runs, Nodes created: 1 |
| #2894 | AviAvni (team) | hang or panic | `testIssue2894` | ❌ fails: query runs until its 10s per-query TIMEOUT: 'Query timed out' (expected count 2); test02/test03 same; server stays up. | ✅ passes: all 4 methods pass (2, 2, [..800,..803,..806], 0) |
| #2782 | gkorland (team) | kills server or write-locks | `testIssue2782` | ❌ fails: same graph name in db0 and db1: db0 becomes write-locked ('graph was deleted or replaced while the query was running'); server stays up (release build) | ✅ passes: both databases' graphs stay independently readable and writable |
| #2772 | gkorland (team) | data loss on RDB load | `tests/flow/test_encode_decode.py` `test_encode_decode_rename.test_01_renamed_multi_key_graph_round_trips` | ✅ passes: renamed multi-key (VKEY_MAX_ENTITY_COUNT 10) graph survives SAVE + restart; 200 nodes recovered under the new key | ✅ passes: same, survives round-trip |
| #2770 | gkorland (team) | node id aliasing corruption | `tests/flow/test_create_clause.py` `testCreateClause.test19_id_pool_never_reissues_a_live_id (also test16–test18)` | ✅ passes: does not reproduce on edge; fixed by #2797, which added these tests | ✅ passes: passes |
| #2769 | gkorland (team) | server panic | `testIssue2769` | ❌ fails: server exits (container exit 1); log: FalkorDB panic at graph/src/graph/graph.rs:3365:9 'relationship 0 not found'. indegree variant (test02) same. | ✅ passes: returns [[0]] for outdegree and indegree; server alive |
| #2749 | DvirDukhan (team) | constraint lost in RDB | `tests/flow/test_constraint.py` `testConstraintSchemaRegistration.test01_a_constraint_on_an_unused_property_survives_a_reload` | ✅ passes: MANDATORY constraint on an unregistered property survives DEBUG RELOAD unchanged (not rewritten to attribute id 0) | ✅ passes: survives unchanged |
| #2653 | gkorland (team) | replica divergence | `testIssue2653` | ❌ fails: non-UTF-8 key \xc3\x28bin replicates to a mangled U+FFFD key; real key absent on replica (EXISTS=0) | ✅ passes: replica holds the byte-exact key and answers the query |
| #2537 | gkorland (team) | SIGSEGV on RESTORE | `testIssue2537` | ❌ fails: GRAPH.RESTORE key "" -> SIGSEGV, container exit 139, server down (null RedisModuleIO deref in BufferedReader stream-refill) | ❌ fails: C aborts too: "Guru Meditation: Redis aborting for OUT OF MEMORY", exit 133 |

**Summary:**
- **Rust:** all 19 new tests fail on `edge`, by crash or panic, hang, data loss or replica divergence, a write-lock, or memory blow-up.
- **C v4.22.0:** passes every test it can run, except #2537, where an empty `GRAPH.RESTORE` payload crashes C too (OOM abort). #2537 is really a both-engines bug.
- **n/a on C:** for #2994, #3031 and #3266 the payload format is Rust-specific. #3237 is a Rust data structure.

## Externally reported Rust-engine issues

I checked every open issue opened by someone outside the FalkorDB team (author not in the org) that the triage marks as affecting the Rust engine, 100 issues in all. #3150 is already covered by the S1 file, and #2670 and #2668 are devcontainer build issues, which leaves **97**.

Where no test existed, I added one to **`tests/flow/test_open_rust_external_issues.py`**. It's one `testIssue<N>` class per issue, also kept out of `flow_tests_done.txt`. Every class was run in a fresh container against `falkordb/falkordb-server:edge` and `falkordb/falkordb-server:v4.22.0`.

| Result | Issues |
|---|---|
| New test, **fails on Rust** | 86, of which **62 also fail on C** (so not Rust-only) and 24 pass on C |
| **Already fixed on Rust**, new test kept as a regression test | 5: #627, #2098, #2099, #2179, #2733 |
| **Existing test** | 3: #2006 (`test_query_validation.py` test51, passes on Rust); #3168 (#2537's test for the empty payload, plus a new regression class for the truncated payload, which `edge` already handles); #3188 (#2972's test) |
| Not testable or not an engine bug | 3: #978 (memory ratio report), #1492 (performance only), #1826 (the 1000 ms timeout is the Docker image's `FALKORDB_ARGS`, not the module default) |

I commented on #2006, #3168 and #3188 with the test locations.

### Needs a decision before fixing

These tests assert the openCypher or expected behaviour, but an **existing test on `main` asserts the current behaviour**. A fix would have to change both:
- **#1393, #1946** (reading properties of deleted entities): `tests/flow/test_access_del_entity.py`, `test_access_del_edge.py`
- **#1315** (`exists(pattern)`): `tests/flow/test_union.py` test10
- **#2607** (`*..0`): `tests/flow/test_relation_patterns.py` `test12_lt_zero_hop_traversals`
- **#2222** (month-end duration arithmetic): `tests/flow/test_temporal.py` `test_month_end_duration_arithmetic`
- **#2007** (parallel edges in an anonymous pattern): `tests/flow/test_inline_pattern_attributes.py` test12
- **#2213, #3199** (`sum()` of integers returns a float): the TCK `Aggregation3.feature` was edited to expect a float

Two more are product decisions:
- **#2724:** `prev()` was dropped from the Rust engine on purpose.
- **#946:** the test accepts either an error or a non-null key.

### Notes from the runs

- **#2725, #2727, #2737, #2744** have one likely root cause: a single-node named path over a variable bound before `WITH` or `CALL`.
- **#2728 and #2742** are probably both fixed by open PR #3281.
- **Other open PRs with fixes:** #3223 for #3226, #2513 for #2441, #3071 for #2659.
- **#2283:** its test uncovered a separate Rust-only bug. After nodes are created earlier in the same query, `MATCH (a:N),(b:N) WHERE a.id < b.id` drops every row (`testIssue2283.test03`). It may need its own issue.
- **DoS classes (#1482, #1483, #1485, #1486):** each ends with the reporter's query on the default config. That query OOM-kills both engines, so run these classes in a memory-capped container.

## Running the tests

Each class is self-contained. Because some of them take the server down, run them one class at a time, each against its own server, for example:

```bash
docker run -d -p 6390:6379 -e FALKORDB_ARGS= -e REDIS_ARGS="--enable-debug-command yes" falkordb/falkordb-server:edge
cd tests/flow && FALKORDB_TEST_IMAGE=falkordb/falkordb-server:edge FALKORDB_USE_SERVICE=1 \
  FALKORDB_HOST=localhost FALKORDB_PORT=6390 \
  RLTest -t test_open_rust_s1_issues:testIssue3150 --env existing-env --existing-env-addr localhost:6390 \
  --parallelism 1 --enable-debug-command --enable-protected-configs
```

- **Replica tests:** #2946 and #2653 need a replica. Start a second container with `REDIS_ARGS="--replicaof <master> 6379"` on the same docker network, and set `FALKORDB_REPLICA_HOST` and `FALKORDB_REPLICA_PORT`.
- **#3237 unit test:** `cargo test -p graph -- --ignored remove_batch_keeps_non_root_branches_at_least_half_full`

## How the issues were selected

The 23 issues come from an engine triage of all 727 open issues in this repo. Each issue was classified from its text, labels and triage comments as Rust-only, C-only or both. Severity was then estimated: S1 means a crash, panic, data loss or corruption, a hang, or a security problem.

These are the issues classified as **Rust-only and S1**. The "What breaks" column above is that triage's severity reason, and "Opened by" shows whether the opener is in the FalkorDB GitHub org.

issues.title: Add reproduction tests for the open Rust-only S1 issues
issues.body:
Add a reproduction test for every open S1 (critical) issue that affects only the Rust engine, and record how the latest C release behaves on the same test.

Scope: the 23 open issues classified as Rust-only and S1 (crash, panic, data loss or corruption, hang, security) in an engine triage of all open issues: #3304, #3284, #3279, #3266, #3237, #3150, #3031, #3013, #3003, #2994, #2974, #2972, #2946, #2930, #2895, #2894, #2782, #2772, #2770, #2769, #2749, #2653, #2537.

- **No existing test:** add one that asserts the correct behaviour, so it fails today and passes once the issue is fixed. Keep these tests out of CI until their issue is fixed, since several of them crash or hang the server.
- **Existing test on `main`:** add no new test. Comment the test's name and path on the issue instead.
- **Every test:** run it against `falkordb/falkordb-server:edge` (Rust) and `falkordb/falkordb-server:v4.22.0` (C), and record both results in the PR.


**Extended scope:** every open Rust-engine bug reported by someone outside the FalkorDB team, 97 issues after excluding #3150 (already covered) and the two devcontainer issues, #2670 and #2668. The same rule applies: add a test if none exists, otherwise comment the existing test's location on the issue. The new tests are in `tests/flow/test_open_rust_external_issues.py`.

**Full triage page** (FalkorDB org members only): https://claude.ai/artifact/1ZajBCKvAvnYJz8KKq8rMw. It covers all 727 open issues by engine (Rust v6+, C, or both) and estimated severity, and shows these tests' results on Rust and C.

issues.title: `WITH c WHERE r IS NOT NULL` fails with an internal alias lookup error after `OPTIONAL MATCH`
issues.body:
## Description

FalkorDB's C-based engine fails to execute a valid Cypher query when a `WITH`-associated `WHERE` clause references a relationship variable that is not included in the `WITH` projection.

The query is taken from the openCypher TCK `TriadicSelection1` scenario. It fails on **FalkorDB 4.20.1 and 4.22.0**, while FalkorDB 6.0.2 and Neo4j 2026.09 execute it successfully.

This report describes a distinct, reproducible query form. It does not claim that the underlying root cause is independent of previously reported filtered-alias issues.

## Versions

- FalkorDB 4.20.1 (C engine): affected; reproduced once.
- FalkorDB 4.22.0 (C engine): affected; reproduced in three consecutive runs.
- FalkorDB 6.0.2 (Rust engine): not reproduced.
- Neo4j 2026.09: executes successfully as a reference.

## Steps to reproduce

Run the following statements on a fresh graph.

**1. Create the graph**

```cypher
CREATE (a:A {name:'a'})-[:KNOWS]->(b:X {name:'b'}),
       (b)-[:NEXT]->(c:Y {name:'c'});
```

**2. Run the query**

```cypher
MATCH (a:A)-[:KNOWS]->(b:X)-->(c:Y)
OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[r:KNOWS]->(c)
WITH c WHERE r IS NOT NULL
RETURN c.name;
```

## Expected behavior

The query should execute successfully and return **zero rows**.

The graph contains the two-hop path `a → b → c`, but no direct `KNOWS` relationship from `a` to `c`. Therefore, the `OPTIONAL MATCH` binds `r` to `null`, and the `WHERE r IS NOT NULL` filter eliminates the row.

According to Cypher's `WITH` semantics, its associated `WHERE` may reference a variable from the incoming scope even when that variable is not retained for subsequent clauses.

Reference: https://neo4j.com/docs/cypher-manual/current/clauses/with/

## Actual behavior

FalkorDB 4.20.1 and 4.22.0 return:

```text
_AR_EXP_UpdateEntityIdx: Unable to locate a value with alias r within the record
```

The same query returns zero rows on FalkorDB 6.0.2 and Neo4j 2026.09.

## Additional controls

**Control A — Retain `r` in the projection**

```cypher
MATCH (a:A)-[:KNOWS]->(b:X)-->(c:Y)
OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[r:KNOWS]->(c)
WITH c, r WHERE r IS NOT NULL
RETURN c.name;
```

**Control B — Filter before projecting `r` away**

```cypher
MATCH (a:A)-[:KNOWS]->(b:X)-->(c:Y)
OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[r:KNOWS]->(c)
WITH c, r
WHERE r IS NOT NULL
WITH c
RETURN c.name;
```

Both controls return zero rows on FalkorDB 4.22.0.

The failure is therefore sensitive to how the relationship variable `r` is handled across the `WITH` projection and its associated filter.

## Execution plan

`GRAPH.EXPLAIN` for the failing query on FalkorDB 4.22.0 reports:

```text
Results
  Project
    Filter
      Project
        Apply
          Conditional Traverse | (a)->(c:Y)
            Node By Label Scan | (a:A)
          Optional
            Expand Into | (a)-[r:KNOWS]->(c)
              Argument
```

This plan, together with the passing controls, suggests a possible interaction between projection and alias availability during filter evaluation.

However, the plan does not expose record-slot contents, so this is a hypothesis rather than a confirmed internal root cause.

## openCypher TCK source

- Feature: `useCases/triadicSelection/TriadicSelection1.feature`
- Scenario: `[17] Handling triadic friend of a friend that is a friend with different labels`
- Case ID: `tck-3f5d297f04e92acb`
- Fixture: `binary-tree-2` (13 nodes, 16 relationships)

The original TCK query also fails on FalkorDB 4.22.0, with the same error. FalkorDB 6.0.2 returns the expected empty result.

## Related issues

Potentially related prior reports include:

- #1300 — filtered-alias resolution after `OPTIONAL MATCH`
- #1301 — filtered-alias resolution across `WITH`
- #1949 — errors when re-matching variables carried through `WITH`
- #2004 — cross-scope alias filtering
- #2010 — incorrect filtering after `OPTIONAL MATCH`

PR #2455 added regression tests for several related reports but did not change production code. The existing regression cases do not establish coverage of this exact TCK query.

Importantly, the present reproducer also fails on **C 4.20.1**, even though maintainers previously reported the original #1300/#1301 reproducers as no longer reproducible on that version. This does not establish a regression between C 4.20.1 and 4.22.0.

**Could maintainers confirm whether this query is covered by an existing underlying defect, or whether it exposes an additional alias-resolution problem in the C engine?**

The minimal reproducer and cross-version results are provided above to facilitate independent triage.

issues.title: Add CCH Phase 3: bidirectional upward query and path unpacking
issues.body: `Cch::query(src, dst)` returns the cheapest weight and the node sequence. Both halves of the search only climb rank over the upward graph (forward reading the upward weights, backward the downward ones) and meet at the rank minimising the two distances; the shortcut arcs on the route are expanded through their recorded mids into original edges. It is stateless, so queries run in parallel against one hierarchy. `None` for an unreachable target or a node outside the hierarchy; `src == dst` is the single-node path of weight 0; ties break on the lowest meeting rank, so results are deterministic. A path that repeats a node (possible only with a zero-weight cycle) has its cycles cut, which leaves the weight unchanged. Stacked on #3209 (customization) and the PRs below it. Tested: 119 `index::cch` tests: every pair on grids, random, parallel-edge, self-loop, zero-weight, disconnected and isolated-node graphs against the oracle's weight, with a path validity check (each hop is a real edge, the sum matches) and a check that the path is simple; 40 random graphs with half their edges at weight 0 (these fail without the cycle cut). Full `cargo test -p graph`: 618 pass, plus the macOS-only failure noted on #3321. Known limits: weights must be finite and `>= 0`, so zero-weight cycles are legal and are what the cycle cut handles. No benchmark against the C module or `algo.SPpaths` yet. Part of #3134. Closes #3210 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Implements CCH Phase 3, so `Cch::query(src, dst)` returns the cheapest weight and the node sequence. Both search halves only climb rank over the upward graph and meet at the rank minimizing the two distances; the shortcut arcs on the route then expand through their recorded mids back into original edges. The query is stateless, so any number of queries can run against one hierarchy in parallel, and unpacking is iterative rather than recursive. `None` for an unreachable target or a node outside the hierarchy; `src == dst` is the single-node path of weight 0, and ties break on the lowest meeting rank so results are deterministic. A path that repeats a node (only possible with a zero-weight cycle) has its cycles cut, which leaves the weight unchanged. A drifted index logs once per process, and memory usage now counts the shared topology and weight arrays. Written for commit 88f71dad5a9f4f95d35c4aabbc15096af9acd355. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added route queries that return the lowest-cost path between nodes, including a zero-cost path when the start and destination are the same. * **Bug Fixes** * Queries return no route for unreachable or out-of-range nodes, and when a route cannot be reconstructed. * Invalid or mismatched routing weights are treated as internal errors. * **Improvements** * Memory usage reports account for the hierarchy, shared topology, and weight arrays.

issues.title: Add CCH Phase 2: customization and WeightArr
issues.body: Phase 2 writes one concrete metric into the structure Phase 1 built. `Cch` now holds the shared `Topology` and a `Metric` of four per-arc arrays (upward/downward weight and the apex rank each routes through); `Cch::build` runs Phase 1 then Phase 2, and `Cch::customize` recomputes the metric on the same structure (nothing is written on error). `seed` scatters the original edges into infinity-filled arrays, so each edge is touched once; `relax` is one forward sweep over the lower triangles in increasing rank order, which suffices because the chordal supergraph holds every top arc and the two lower arcs are final when read. Negative, infinite and NaN weights are `InvalidWeight`, and the layout (id spaces, arc ids, the four arrays, why one sweep is enough) is documented at the top of `customize.rs`. `WeightArr` hides the storage behind the surface a copy-on-write array would need. `customize` refuses weights shaped for another graph (a different node count, offsets that do not start at zero or decrease, or an edge the hierarchy has no arc for) with `Internal` instead of silently dropping them or panicking; self-loops in the weights are ignored. Tested with shape-mismatch cases that leave the previous metric untouched. Stacked on #3321 (Phase 1), #3320 and #3319. Tested: 99 `index::cch` tests, including every arc compared with an independent exact oracle (`lower_rank_distances`) over grids, random, parallel-edge, self-loop, zero-weight, disconnected and isolated-node graphs, the boundary of both size ceilings, and the rejection of negative, infinite and NaN weights. Full `cargo test -p graph` passes except the macOS-only failure noted on #3321. `seed` timing (600x600 grid, 1.4M entries, best of 15): 13.3 ms with `WeightCsr::entries`, 13.4 ms with the previous index loop. Known limits: sequential. `seed` has disjoint writes and is parallelisable; `relax` writes the same arc from different apexes, so it needs a different loop to parallelise (both noted in the code). No benchmark against the C module yet. Not run on Linux locally. Part of #3134. Closes #3209 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Implements Phase 2 of the CCH index: `Cch` now holds the shared `Topology` from Phase 1 plus a `Metric` of four per-arc arrays — upward/downward weight and the apex rank each routes through. `Cch::build` runs both phases, and `Cch::customize` recomputes only the metric on the same topology, writing nothing on error. - Original edges are scattered into infinity-filled arrays so each is touched once; `relax` is a single forward sweep over lower triangles in increasing rank order. - Negative, infinite, and NaN weights are rejected as `InvalidWeight` before any write. - `WeightArr` hides the storage behind the surface a copy-on-write array would need, and the internal layout is documented at the top of `customize.rs`. Written for commit 82336e0ee45554f34b5bfdb506fdc5f8babf133e. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added support for building and customizing Contraction Hierarchies with weighted routes. * Update route weights without rebuilding the hierarchy. * **Bug Fixes** * Invalid weights are rejected, and failed customization leaves the existing hierarchy unchanged. * Correctly calculates shortcut weights and their unpacking paths.

issues.title: Add CCH Phase 1: elimination ordering and chordal triangulation
issues.body:
Phase 1 reads the undirected skeleton of a `CchInput`, never a weight, and builds the
metric-independent half of the hierarchy that every later customization reuses: a nested-dissection
elimination order (pure-Rust `feral-metis`, new dependency, behind an `Ordering` trait), the elimination
tree by union-find, and the chordal supergraph as one flat upward CSR with a mirrored downward CSR in
rank space. Ported from `CCH_EliminationOrder` / `CCH_ChordalTriangulation` (`src/algorithms/cch.c` on
`master`). An ordering-backend failure is a hard error, not a fallback to the identity order.

Stacked on #3207 (test kit) and #3206.

Tested: 79 `index::cch` tests, including structural invariants (rank/permutation inverses, sorted
up/down rows, up and down as exact inverses, every skeleton edge present) on grids, random,
disconnected, star, path, parallel-edge and self-loop graphs, with the Metis and identity orders; and a
test that a skeleton with self-loops and duplicates gives the same permutation and hierarchy as a clean
one, and the same permutation on a second run. A backend failure and a non-permutation are `CchError::Internal`
(tested), never `GraphTooLarge` and never a silent identity order. Full `cargo test -p graph`: 578 pass, 1
fails on macOS (`batched_result_emitter::tests::cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, which passes in the
Linux CI run of this PR's base).

Known limits: more than `MAX_NODES` nodes or `MAX_SKELETON_ENTRIES` skeleton entries is
`GraphTooLarge` (the entry limit is `i32::MAX`, at most 1,073,741,823 connected node pairs). Tested on
macOS only; not run against Linux CI. No benchmark against the C module yet.

Part of #3134. Closes #3208

issues.title: Add the CCH path index contract skeleton
issues.body:
Adds the types, signatures and reserved fields for the Customizable Contraction Hierarchies path
index (`index::cch`), with every body unimplemented, so the implementation changes can be written
and reviewed against a fixed contract. Nothing in the engine calls into it: a graph with no CCH
index behaves exactly as before (`Graph::cch_indexes` is an empty `Vec`; `Pending::cch_dirty` stays
`Default`).

- `new_version` clones one `Arc<Cch>` per index, so MVCC versions share the hierarchy.
- `check_size` enforces two limits: `MAX_NODES` (`i32::MAX` nodes) and `MAX_SKELETON_ENTRIES`
  (`i32::MAX` skeleton entries).
- `CchError` derives `thiserror::Error` like the crate's other errors; `InvalidWeight` covers negative,
  infinite and NaN.

Tested: 8 unit tests, including `check_size` at both ceilings and one past (no huge allocation),
`Csr::row`, and `new_version_shares_the_hierarchy` (fails if `cch_indexes` is dropped or the hierarchy is
deep-copied).

Known limits: the entry limit is the one a large graph reaches first. The skeleton is symmetric, so
it allows at most 1,073,741,823 connected node pairs (parallel and bidirectional edges count once;
self-loops not at all). It is the ordering backend's `i32` index width, not a `Csr` limit. Both limits
are ceilings, not promises: memory stops a graph earlier.
