issues.title: [Rust] Clauses after CALL … YIELD are not validated: a trailing MATCH crashes the server, CREATE accepts two relationship types
issues.body:
### Summary

Clauses that follow a procedure call (`CALL proc() YIELD …`) are never validated. A query that ends with `MATCH` after a `CALL` crashes the server. A query that ends with `UNWIND` or `OPTIONAL MATCH` after a `CALL` runs, and `CREATE` or `MERGE` with two relationship types runs too. C rejects all of these.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:N)"
```

| query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `CALL db.labels() YIELD label MATCH (n)` | **server crash** (panic `utilize_node_by_id.rs:106:75`, `parent().unwrap()` on `None`) | `Query cannot conclude with MATCH (…)` |
| `CALL db.labels() YIELD label WITH label MATCH (n)` | **server crash** (same panic) | `Query cannot conclude with MATCH (…)` |
| `CALL db.labels() YIELD label OPTIONAL MATCH (n)` | runs, empty result | `Query cannot conclude with MATCH (…)` |
| `CALL db.labels() YIELD label UNWIND [1] AS x` | runs, empty result | `Query cannot conclude with UNWIND (…)` |
| `CALL db.labels() YIELD label CREATE (a)-[:R\|S]->(b)` | `Nodes created: 2, Relationships created: 1` | `Exactly one relationship type must be specified for each relation in a CREATE pattern.` |
| `CALL db.labels() YIELD label MERGE (a)-[:R\|S]->(b)` | runs | `Exactly one relationship type must be specified for each relation in a MERGE pattern.` |

The panic log:
```
FalkorDB panic: panicked at graph/src/planner/optimizer/utilize_node_by_id.rs:106:75:
called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
  graph::planner::optimizer::utilize_node_by_id::utilize_node_by_id
  graph::planner::optimizer::optimize
```

### Mechanism

`QueryIR::inner_validate` (`graph/src/parser/ast.rs:1166-1206`): the `Call` arm checks the procedure's own arguments and then returns `Ok(())` without calling `inner_validate` on the remaining clauses. Every other clause arm continues with `iter.next().map_or(…, |first| first.inner_validate(iter))`. So no check runs after a `CALL`: the clause-ending checks (`MATCH`/`UNWIND`/`WITH` must not end the query), the single-relationship-type check for `CREATE`/`MERGE`, the inline-property and `SET`/`REMOVE` checks.

The crash happens because a trailing `MATCH` reaches the planner as the plan root, and `utilize_node_by_id` assumes every scan has a parent.

### Expected

The same errors as C. The validation should behave the same whether or not a `CALL` comes first.

### Suggested fix

End the `Call` arm with `iter.next().map_or(Ok(()), |first| first.inner_validate(iter))`, as the other arms do. The `parent().unwrap()` in `utilize_node_by_id` then cannot be reached from a validated query.

### Notes

C crashes (SIGSEGV) on `CALL db.labels() YIELD label MATCH (n) RETURN n`, which is a valid query. That bug is C-only. In Rust the same query returns one row per label and node.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the AST validator (`proofs/`, ledger entry W4-plan-4).

issues.title: fix: effects payloads of 4 GiB or more ship uncompressed instead of with a truncated length
issues.body: Closes #3276 ## Problem `maybe_compress` wrote the frame's `plain_len` and `comp_len` with `as u32`. With `EFFECTS_COMPRESSION` enabled, a payload of 4 GiB or more declared a truncated length, for example 5 for 4 GiB + 5. The replica uses that length as the ceiling for `zstd::bulk::decompress`, so it rejected the frame, never applied the write, and looped on forced resyncs. ## Fix The 12-byte prefix is now built by `frame_prefix`, which narrows both lengths with `u32::try_from` and returns `None` when either does not fit. `maybe_compress` then leaves the payload uncompressed, and an uncompressed payload has no length field to overflow. It also returns early when the plaintext alone is already too long, so a 4 GiB payload is not compressed only to be discarded. Payloads under 4 GiB produce the same bytes as before. | plaintext | Rust `main` | this PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | < 4 GiB | compressed, `plain_len` exact | same bytes | no v3 / compression | | 4 GiB + 5 | compressed, declares `plain_len = 5`, replica refuses | shipped uncompressed, applies | no v3 / compression | ## Tests - New unit test `effects::v3::records::tests::a_frame_whose_lengths_do_not_fit_u32_is_not_written`. It builds the prefix from the lengths alone and allocates nothing large. - Before the fix (the same `as u32` logic, extracted unchanged into `frame_prefix`): `left: Some([5, 0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 0, 0, ...]) right: None` - After: `ok` - `cargo test -p graph --lib effects`: 197 passed, including the existing compression round-trip tests. Full `cargo test -p graph --lib` passes except the known `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy reports no warnings in the touched file. - Flow tests (RLTest, release): `test_effects_wire` 14/14 (covers compressed payloads), `test_effects_values` 9/9, `test_replication` 2/2. `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes effects payloads of 4 GiB or more shipping with a truncated compressed-frame length. `maybe_compress` narrowed the frame's `plain_len` and `comp_len` with `as u32`, so a 4 GiB + 5 byte payload declared a length of 5; the replica takes that declared length as its decompress ceiling, rejects the frame, and loops on forced resyncs. - The 12-byte prefix is now built by `frame_prefix`, which refuses lengths that don't fit `u32` and leaves such payloads uncompressed. Compression is skipped when the plaintext alone already exceeds `u32`. - Payloads under 4 GiB produce the same bytes as before. - New unit test builds the prefix from its lengths alone, without allocating the 4 GiB payload. Written for commit a735fa87f86174a520723bafeeb77b95c14a7c35. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: fix: a deleted edge no longer keeps its type after a constraint registers a new type
issues.body: Closes #3244 ## Problem `Graph::get_type_id_mut` registered a relationship type and its tensor but did not call `resize()`, so `relationship_type_matrix` (edges x types) stayed one column short. `get_relationship_matrix_mut` and `get_label_id_mut` both resize for this reason. Its callers that register a type with no edge are `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE ... RELATIONSHIP ` on the primary and `ADD_SCHEMA` in effects apply on a replica. After that, edge deletes (`delete_relationships`, `delete_implicit_edges`) built a removal mask `relationship_cap x relationship_types.len()` that the narrower matrix refused with `GrB_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`. Only a `debug_assert` checks it, so in release the deleted edge kept its type, and the edge that reused its id read back with the old type. ## Fix Call `self.resize()` in `get_type_id_mut` after registering the type. `resize` costs a few comparisons when nothing changed, and this runs once per type ever. The one change covers both the primary and the replica path. ``` CREATE (:N)-[:A]->(:N) GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE g MANDATORY RELATIONSHIP B PROPERTIES 1 x MATCH ()-[r]->() DELETE r MATCH (a), (b) WHERE id(a) = 0 AND id(b) = 1 CREATE (a)-[:C]->(b) MATCH ()-[r]->() RETURN id(r), type(r) ``` | | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | primary `type(r)` | `A` | `C` | `C` | | replica `type(r)` | `A` | `C` | n/a (C cannot read v3 effects) | ## Tests - New flow test `test_effects_ddl.py:testEffects_01_ConstraintAsEffect.test04_a_type_registered_by_a_constraint_does_not_stick_to_deleted_edges` runs the repro on a primary/replica pair and checks `type(r)` and the `:A` count on both sides. - Before the fix: fails twice, `[[0, 'A']] == [[0, 'C']]`, once for the primary and once for the replica. - After: passes. - Flow suites (release): `test_constraint.py` 26/26, `test_effects_topology.py` 3/3, `test_effects_opcodes.py` 12/12, `test_effects_ddl.py` 18/19. The one failure is `testEffects_06_ConstraintSettlingRaces.test02` (`[[1]] == [[2]]`). It also fails on `main` with the class run alone, and the test's own comment records it as a known intermittent failure. - `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except the known macOS `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). `cargo fmt --check` is clean, with no clippy warnings in the touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #3244: a deleted edge no longer keeps its type after a constraint registers a new type. `get_type_id_mut` registered a relationship type and its tensor but didn't resize `relationship_type_matrix`, so a type registered with no edge (a `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT` on the primary, an `ADD_SCHEMA` on a replica) left the edge×type matrix one column short. The next edge delete then built a removal mask the narrower matrix rejected — only a `debug_assert` caught the mismatch — so in release builds the deleted edge kept its type and the edge that reused its id read back the old type. The fix routes every type registration through `register_relationship_type`, a single helper that pushes the type name, inserts its tensor, and always calls `resize()`. Both `get_type_id_mut` and `get_relationship_matrix_mut` now go through it, so no registration site can skip the resize. `resize` costs a few comparisons when nothing changed and runs once per type. The change covers the primary and replica paths, and the new flow test runs the repro against both. Written for commit 5733f785611bbb41133ce8aa290be7fa9cd497e8. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Relationship types remain consistent across graph updates and constraints, including on replicas. When a deleted edge’s ID is reused for a different relationship type, the edge is associated only with its current type; stale associations are no longer retained on the master or replicas. This keeps relationship information accurate after edge changes.

issues.title: [Rust] Compressed effects payloads of 4 GiB or more declare a truncated length and never apply on the replica
issues.body:
### Summary

When `EFFECTS_COMPRESSION` is on, a v3 effects payload whose plaintext is 4 GiB or larger is written with its decompressed length truncated to `u32`. The replica uses the declared length as the ceiling for `zstd::bulk::decompress`, so it rejects the frame. The write never applies on the replica, and the divergence guard forces a resync that fails again in the same way. The same truncation affects `comp_len` when the compressed frame is 4 GiB or larger.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

This was not run live, because it needs a 4 GiB payload. It is confirmed by code reading and by a unit test that builds the frame prefix from the lengths alone. `graph/src/effects/v3/records.rs`, `maybe_compress`:

```rust
let plain_len = (buf.len() - HEADER) as u32;   // 4 GiB + 5 -> 5
let comp_len = frame.len() as u32;
```

With that logic extracted unchanged into a helper, the prefix it produces for `plain_len = 2^32 + 5, comp_len = 10` is:

```
left: Some([5, 0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0])   // declares 5 bytes of plaintext
```

On the reading side, `open_payload` calls `zstd::bulk::decompress(frame, 5)`, which fails with `BadCompression`. `GRAPH.EFFECT` then returns `effect apply failed`, and `divergence_guard::on_failure` forces a resync.

C has no v3 or compression (C `master` is at `EFFECTS_VERSION 2`), so there is no C behaviour to compare against.

### Mechanism

`graph/src/effects/v3/records.rs:1376-1377`. Both lengths are narrowed to `u32` with `as`, with no check.

### Expected

A payload that the `u32` length fields cannot describe is not compressed. It ships uncompressed, which has no length field and applies normally.

### Suggested fix

Narrow with `u32::try_from` and fall back to the uncompressed payload (`maybe_compress` returns `false`) when either length does not fit. Also check the plaintext length before compressing, so that a 4 GiB payload is not compressed only to be thrown away.

issues.title: [Rust] GRAPH.BULK reply and point() error messages differ from C
issues.body:
### Summary

Two replies are worded differently from C:

1. `GRAPH.BULK` replies `N nodes created, M relations created`. C replies `N nodes created, M edges created`.
2. `point()` errors use Rust's own messages, and the same map gets a different error depending on whether it is written in the call or passed in as a value. For example, `point({latitude: null, longitude: 1})` says `point() requires 'latitude' field`, but `WITH {latitude: null, longitude: 1} AS m RETURN point(m)` says `Type mismatch: 'latitude' must be a number, got Null`. Rust also accepts a map with extra keys, which C rejects.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
redis-cli GRAPH.BULK bg BEGIN 0 0 0 0
```
Rust: `0 nodes created, 0 relations created`. C: `0 nodes created, 0 edges created`.

`RETURN point(<m>)` / `WITH <m> AS m RETURN point(m)`:

| `<m>` | Rust (literal / value) | C (both forms) |
|---|---|---|
| `{latitude:null, longitude:1}` | `point() requires 'latitude' field` / `Type mismatch: 'latitude' must be a number, got Null` | `'latitude' and 'longitude' values in point map were not both valid numerics` |
| `{latitude:'a', longitude:1}` | `Type mismatch: 'latitude' must be a number, got String` | `'latitude' and 'longitude' values in point map were not both valid numerics` |
| `{latitude:1}`, `{}` | `point() requires 'longitude'/'latitude' field` | `A point map should have 2 elements, latitude and longitude` |
| `{latitude:1, longitude:2, x:3}` | returns a point | `A point map should have 2 elements, latitude and longitude` |
| `{Latitude:1, longitude:2}` | `point() requires 'latitude' field` | `Did not find 'latitude' value in point map` |
| `{latitude:100, longitude:1}` | `latitude should be within the range -90.0 to 90.0, got 100` | `latitude should be within the -90 to 90 range` |
| `{latitude:1, longitude:200}` | `longitude should be within the range -180.0 to 180.0, got 200` | `longitude should be within the -180 to 180 range` |

### Mechanism

- `src/commands/bulk_insert.rs:852` and `:1011` format the reply with `relations created`.
- `point()` has two implementations with different messages (`graph/src/runtime/functions/spatial.rs`): `point_struct_pure`, used when the binder rewrites a literal map into positional slots, and the map path in the `point` function. The binder's rewrite (`rewrite_struct_constructor`, `graph/src/planner/binder.rs`) fills a missing key with `null`, so the struct path cannot tell a missing key from a `null` one. Neither path checks the key count. The range check runs after narrowing to `f32` (`Point::validate`), so `90.0000001` is accepted where C rejects it.

### Expected

C's reply text and C's `point()` checks and messages, the same for both forms.

### Suggested fix

Change the bulk reply text. Route both `point()` paths through one helper that applies C's checks in C's order (key count, presence, numeric, range on `f64`). Keep the struct rewrite only for maps that carry both keys, so a missing key reaches the map path.

(Also seen: `CREATE INDEX` on a new label reports `Labels added: 1` where C does not. That is the same cause as #2655 and is noted there.)

issues.title: fix: a refused fulltext CREATE INDEX no longer leaks the RediSearch options block
issues.body: Closes #3273 ## Problem `Index::create_rs_index` allocated the RediSearch index options (`RediSearch_CreateIndexOptions`, an `rm_calloc`), then hit early returns that skipped `RediSearch_FreeIndexOptions`: a stopword, language or label with a NUL byte (`CString::new(...)?`), and `Language is not supported`. Each refused fulltext `CREATE INDEX … OPTIONS {language:'klingon'}` or `{stopwords:['a\u0000b']}` leaked ~56 bytes. ## Fix Do the `CString` conversions before allocating the options, so a `?` cannot leak them. On the remaining error path, the `SetLanguage` failure, free the options before returning. Same behaviour and error texts as before. `used_memory` growth per refused statement (20 000 statements): | Statement | `main` | This PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | `… OPTIONS {language:'klingon'}` | +56.0 B | ~0 B | crashes (#2448) | | `… OPTIONS {stopwords:['a\u0000b']}` | +54.2 B | ~0 B | accepted (no error path) | | control `… OPTIONS {weight:'x'}` | ~0 B | ~0 B | ~0 B | ## Tests - New flow test `test_index_create.py::test20_failed_fulltext_create_does_not_leak`: 10 000 refusals of each statement must grow `used_memory` by less than 200 KB. - Before the fix: `544640 < 200000` (language) and `559800 < 200000` (stopword) fail. - After: pass. - Flow (RLTest, release): `test_index_create` 19/19, `test_fulltext_query` 5/5, `test_index_delete` 14/14, `test_index_updates` 11/11, `test_index_scans` 38/38. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 495 passed, 1 failed (`cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, pre-existing on macOS, #2922). `cargo fmt --check` and clippy clean on the touched code. Related: #2449 (language validated only when the spec is created) touches the same function and is not changed here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #3273: a refused fulltext `CREATE INDEX` no longer leaks the RediSearch options block. **Bug Fixes** - Moves `CString` conversions before the options allocation so early returns cannot leak it. - Frees the options block on the unsupported-language error path; behavior and error messages are unchanged. - Adds a flow test that verifies 10,000 refused statements grow `used_memory` by under 200 KB. Written for commit a927344321ec143f268b9d90443c14fb7f8b2d20. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: [Rust] Failed fulltext CREATE INDEX leaks the RediSearch options block (unsupported language, NUL in a stopword)
issues.body:
### Summary

`Index::create_rs_index` leaks the RediSearch index-options block (~56 bytes, plus any stopword copies) every time it returns an error. A fulltext `CREATE` with an unsupported language or a stopword containing a NUL byte reaches that path, so each failing statement leaks.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

10 000-20 000 failing statements each, then `INFO memory` `used_memory` growth:

| Statement (repeated) | Error | Rust `main` | Control: `OPTIONS {weight:'x'}` (fails earlier) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.s) OPTIONS {language:'klingon'}` | `Language is not supported: klingon` | +56.0 B/stmt | ~0 B/stmt |
| `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.s) OPTIONS {stopwords:['a\u0000b']}` | `nul byte found in provided data at position: 1` | +54.2 B/stmt | ~0 B/stmt |

C has no equivalent leak: the `klingon` statement crashes C (#2448), and C accepts the NUL stopword (`Indices created: 1`).

### Mechanism

`graph/src/index/mod.rs:1112` calls `RediSearch_CreateIndexOptions()` (an `rm_calloc`), then three early returns skip `RediSearch_FreeIndexOptions`: the stopword `CString::new(...)?` (:1122), the language `CString::new(...)?` and the `Language is not supported` return (:1141-1143), and the label `CString::new(...)?` (:1151). After `RediSearch_IndexOptionsSetStopwords`, the deep-copied stopwords are lost along with the block.

### Expected

A refused statement leaves memory where it was.

### Suggested fix

Run the fallible `CString` conversions before allocating the options, and free the options on the `SetLanguage` failure path.

issues.title: [Rust] Procedure output differs from C: dbms.functions type order, fulltext.drop message, db.indexes/db.constraints row order and info
issues.body:
### Summary

Several procedure outputs differ from C in form, not in which data exists. Two are plain formatting slips; the rest need a decision on whether to copy C.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

**1. `dbms.functions` union type order.** Rust prints union members in declaration order, C in its fixed type order (`Map, Node, Edge, List, Path, Datetime, Date, Time, Duration, String, Boolean, Integer, Float, Null, Pointer, Point, Vectorf32`, the order Rust's own `Any` spelling already uses).

```
GRAPH.QUERY o "CALL dbms.functions() YIELD name, return_type, arguments WHERE name IN ['point','distance','tofloat','vecf32'] RETURN name, return_type, arguments"
```

| name | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `point` | `Point or Null` | `Null or Point` |
| `distance` | `[Point or Null, Point or Null]` | `[Null or Point, Null or Point]` |
| `tofloat` | `[String, Float, Integer, or Null]` | `[String, Integer, Float, or Null]` |
| `vecf32` | `Vectorf32 or Null` | `Null or Vectorf32` |
| `vec.cosineDistance` / `vec.euclideanDistance` | `[Vectorf32 or Null, …]` | `[Null or Vectorf32, …]` |

**2. `db.idx.fulltext.drop` error text.** `CALL db.idx.fulltext.drop('Nope')`: Rust `Unable to drop index on :Nope(): no such index.`, C `Unable to drop index on :Nope: no such index.` (the `()` comes from formatting an empty attribute list).

**3. `db.indexes()` / `db.constraints()` row order.** Indexes created on `B`, `A`, `()-[:Z]-()`, `C`; constraints UNIQUE B, UNIQUE A, MANDATORY C, MANDATORY Z:

| | `db.indexes()` labels | `db.constraints()` labels |
|---|---|---|
| Rust | A, B, C, Z | B, A, C, Z (creation order) |
| C | Z, C, A, B | Z, C, A, B |

**4. `db.indexes()` `info` column.** Rust: `{fields: [{name: range:x}, …]}`. C: RediSearch's index info (`gcPolicy`, `score`, `lang`, per-field `path`/`options`/`textWeight`/`tagCaseSensitive`, `numDocuments`, `numTerms`, `invertedSize`, …).

**5. Other `dbms.functions` differences** (99 shared names, 16 differ, plus name sets): operator rows C lists (`and`, `eq`, `starts with`, `subscript`, …) are absent in Rust; spellings differ (`isempty`/`isEmpty`, `randomuuid`/`randomUUID`, `tofloatornull`/`toFloatOrNull`, `typeof`/`typeOf`, `startNode`/`startnode`, `starts with`/`starts_with`); signatures differ for `contains`, `indegree`, `outdegree`, `date.transaction` & co., `percentileCont`/`Disc`, `pow`, `intern`.

**6. `db.idx.fulltext.drop` on a label with only a range index**: C succeeds silently (nothing dropped), Rust errors `no such index`.

### Mechanism

1. `type_to_dbms_string` (`graph/src/runtime/functions/procedures.rs:686`) joins `Type::Union` members in declaration order.
2. `Graph::drop_index` error (`graph/src/graph/graph.rs:3980`) always prints `({attr_list})`.
3–6. Different storage/registry iteration and a reduced `info` map; C's index order looks like an artifact of its schema arrays, not a contract.

### Expected

1 and 2: match C byte for byte (cosmetic, no decision needed).

3–6 need a decision. Options: (a) copy C exactly; (b) keep Rust's output and document it (row order of a procedure without `ORDER BY` is not a contract; `info` exposes RediSearch internals); (c) copy only what clients are known to parse. Recommendation: (b) for 3, 4 and 6; for 5, at least make the names C lists resolvable/listed consistently, as tools that introspect `dbms.functions` match on names.

### Suggested fix

1. Sort union members by the canonical type order before joining. 2. Omit the parentheses when no attribute is named. A PR doing 1 and 2 follows; 3–6 left open for the decision.

issues.title: [Rust] A query may end with WITH and returns its projection (C: Query cannot conclude with WITH)
issues.body:
### Summary

A query whose last clause is `WITH` is accepted and returns the `WITH` projection as its result set. C rejects it, and so does openCypher: a query must end with `RETURN`, an update clause, a procedure call or a non-returning subquery. The same holds inside a `CALL { … }` body.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

| query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (n) WITH n` | returns every node | `Query cannot conclude with WITH (must be a RETURN clause, an update clause, a procedure call or a non-returning subquery)` |
| `UNWIND [1] AS x WITH x` | `[[1]]` | same error |
| `WITH 1 AS x` | `[[1]]` | same error |
| `CREATE (a) WITH a` | creates the node and returns it | same error, nothing created |
| `MATCH (n) CALL { WITH n MATCH (m) WITH m } RETURN 1` | runs | same error |
| `MATCH (n) CALL { WITH n } RETURN 1` | runs | same error |
| `RETURN 1 AS x UNION WITH 2 AS x` | `All sub queries in a UNION must have the same column names.` | same `cannot conclude with WITH` error |

### Mechanism

`QueryIR::inner_validate` (`graph/src/parser/ast.rs:1271-1274`) handles `With` and `Return` in one arm and accepts both as the last clause. `Match` and `Unwind` in the same function already return the "Query cannot conclude with …" error when nothing follows them.

### Expected

`Query cannot conclude with WITH (must be a RETURN clause, an update clause, a procedure call or a non-returning subquery)`, as in C.

### Suggested fix

Split the `With` arm from `Return`, and return that error when `iter.next()` is `None`, the same way the `Match` and `Unwind` arms do. Validation runs after binding, and the binder's synthetic import `WITH` at the start of a `CALL` body is always followed by the body's own clauses, unless the body is only an import `WITH`, which C rejects too.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the AST validator (`proofs/`, ledger entry W4-plan-5).

issues.title: fix: accept a list or map subscript as a WHERE predicate
issues.body: Closes #3261 ## Problem `Binder::expr_may_return_boolean` put `ExprIR::GetElement` with the node kinds that can never be boolean, so any subscript used as a predicate (`WHERE n.flags[0]`, `WHERE true AND l[0]`, `WHERE m['a']`) failed with `Expected boolean predicate` before the query ran. C accepts these and checks the element's type at runtime. ## Fix Move `GetElement` to the "may be boolean" arm next to `Property`, `Variable` and `Parameter`. `GetElements` (a slice, always a list) is still rejected. | query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (n:N) WHERE n.flags[0] RETURN count(n)` | Expected boolean predicate | 1 | 1 | | `MATCH (n:N) WHERE NOT n.flags[0] RETURN count(n)` | Expected boolean predicate | 1 | 1 | | `WITH [true] AS l WHERE true AND l[0] RETURN 1` | Expected boolean predicate | 1 row | 1 row | | `WITH {a: true} AS m WHERE m['a'] RETURN 1` | Expected boolean predicate | 1 row | 1 row | | `WITH [null] AS l WHERE l[0] RETURN count(*)` | Expected boolean predicate | 0 | 0 | | `WITH [1] AS l WHERE l[0] RETURN 1` | Expected boolean predicate | Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer | same | | `WITH [true] AS l WHERE l[0..1] RETURN 1` | Expected boolean predicate | Expected boolean predicate | same | (graph: `CREATE (:N {flags: [true, false]}), (:N {flags: [false]}), (:N)`) One difference is left. C constant-folds a subscript of a literal (`WHERE [1][0]`) and rejects it as `Expected boolean predicate` at compile time. Rust now gives the runtime `Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer`. Both are errors. `test_reduce.py::test_nested_reduction` asserted the compile-time message for `WHERE [x IN [0] | reduce(...)][0]`. C gives `Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer` for that query, so the assertion now matches C. ## Tests New flow test `test_filters.py::test10_subscript_as_predicate`. Before the fix (`main` @ b033aecc6) it fails with `redis.exceptions.ResponseError: Expected boolean predicate`. After the fix: `[PASS]`. Also run: `test_filters`, `test_query_validation`, `test_comprehension_functions`, `test_function_calls`, `test_with_clause`, `test_list`, `test_map`, `test_null_handling`, `test_reduce` (all pass); `tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py` (131 passed); `cargo test -p graph --lib` (only the known macOS failure `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, #2922); `cargo fmt --check`; no clippy warnings in the touched code. Binder-only change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the binder rejecting subscripts as WHERE predicates: `WHERE n.flags[0]`, `WHERE l[0]`, and `WHERE m['a']` now pass binding and have their element type checked at runtime, as C does. Non-boolean elements raise `Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer` at runtime instead of `Expected boolean predicate` at binding; slices like `l[0..1]` are still rejected as predicates. Test expectations updated to match C behavior, including the nested reduction query. One divergence remains: C constant-folds literal subscripts such as `[1][0]` and rejects them at compile time, while Rust now raises the runtime type mismatch; both are errors. Written for commit 8153a05b085f50f5e64e51cfce85bbc55bd9d157. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: fix: fulltext query procedures return no rows for a non-string label or query
issues.body: Closes #3265 ## Problem `NodeByFulltextScanOp` / `EdgeByFulltextScanOp` (the planner's rewrite of `db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes` / `queryRelationships`) returned `Err` when the evaluated label or query was not a string, failing the whole query. C returns no rows. ## Fix Return `Ok(None)` (no rows for that input row) instead, the same answer as a label with no fulltext index. | query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `queryNodes(1, 2)` | `fulltext query expects a string label` | no rows | no rows | | `queryNodes(null, 'x')` | `fulltext query expects a string label` | no rows | no rows | | `queryNodes('W', 1)` | `fulltext query expects a string query` | no rows | no rows | | `queryRelationships(1, 2)` | `fulltext query expects a string relationship type` | no rows | no rows | One deliberate difference: `UNWIND [1, 'L1'] AS l CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes(l, 'hello') ...` returns the `'L1'` rows on Rust after the fix; C returns nothing for the whole query once one row's label is not a string, which looks like a C artifact, so it is not copied. ## Tests - New flow test `tests/flow/test_fulltext_query.py::test06_fulltext_query_non_string_arguments`. - Before (module built from `main`): FAIL (`fulltext query expects a string label`). - After: `test_fulltext_query.py` 6/6, `test_procedures.py` 12/12, `test_index_scans.py` 38/38 pass. - `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p graph --all-targets` clean for touched files. Error branch only, no hot-path change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes fulltext query procedures (`db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes` / `queryRelationships`) so that non-string labels or queries return no rows instead of failing the whole query, matching C behavior. One deliberate difference: with `UNWIND [1, 'L1'] AS l CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes(l, ...)`, Rust returns the rows for `'L1'` while C returns no rows at all once any row's label is non-string; the C behavior looks like an artifact and is not copied. Adds a flow test covering both cases. Written for commit 496aba8a4d91823db33cdd01cee80f27cf3f3bfa. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: [Rust] Module-load arguments parsed unlike C: case-sensitive names, any boolean value, ASYNC_DELETE ignored, invalid/unknown args load
issues.body:
### Summary

Module-load arguments (`--loadmodule falkordb.so NAME VALUE ...`) are parsed differently from C, and differently from `GRAPH.CONFIG SET` (which #3021 aligned with C). Names are case-sensitive for some fields, booleans accept anything, some fields are ignored at load, and invalid or unknown arguments load where C refuses to start.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

Each row starts a fresh `redis-server --loadmodule <module> <args>` and then runs `GRAPH.CONFIG GET <name>`.

| Load args | Rust | C (`bin/macos-arm64v8-release/falkordb.so`) |
|---|---|---|
| `CMD_INFO YES` | loads, `CMD_INFO 0` | loads, `1` |
| `CMD_INFO garbage` | loads, `0` | refuses to load |
| `DELAY_INDEXING YES` | loads, `0` | loads, `1` |
| `cache_size 10` | loads, `CACHE_SIZE 25` (ignored) | loads, `10` |
| `ASYNC_DELETE no` / `async_delete no` | loads, `1` (ignored) | loads, `0` |
| `timeout_max 7` | loads, `7` | loads, `7` |
| `CACHE_SIZE 0` | loads, `0` | refuses (must be positive) |
| `CACHE_SIZE 5000` | loads, `5000` | loads, `5000` |
| `THREAD_COUNT 0` | loads, auto (`11`) | refuses (must be positive) |
| `MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES 0` | loads, `0` | refuses (must be positive) |
| `FOO 1` (unknown name) | loads, ignored | refuses: `Encountered unknown configuration field 'FOO'` |
| `CACHE_SIZE` (odd arg count) | loads, `25` | refuses: all configurations should be key-value pairs |

### Mechanism

The arguments are handled by two parsers:

- Fields registered in `redis_module!` (`src/lib.rs:97-118`, `module_args_as_configuration: true`) are read by redismodule-rs before `graph_init`. Its `find_config_value` compares names byte for byte (case-sensitive), and `get_bool_default_config_value` returns `value == "yes"` (so `YES` and `garbage` both give `false`, with no error). This covers `CACHE_SIZE`, `THREAD_COUNT`, `INDEX_WORKER_THREADS`, `NODE_CREATION_BUFFER`, `VKEY_MAX_ENTITY_COUNT`, `JS_*`, `IMPORT_FOLDER`, `TEMP_FOLDER`, `CMD_INFO`, `DELAY_INDEXING`.
- The remaining fields are handled by an ad-hoc loop in `graph_init` (`src/module_init.rs:161-221`). It is case-insensitive but has no `ASYNC_DELETE` arm, uses plain `parse::<i64>()` without C's sign rules (`MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES 0`), and skips unknown names and a trailing odd argument.

C's `Config_Init` (`src/configuration/config.c`) refuses an odd argument count and unknown names, matches names case-insensitively, and sends every pair through `Config_Option_set`, the same setter `GRAPH.CONFIG SET` uses.

### Expected

Load arguments are accepted and refused exactly as C does, by the same validation `GRAPH.CONFIG SET` uses (`validate_config_set` in `src/commands/config_cmd.rs`, from #3021).

### Decisions needed

1. **One parser or two.** (a) Turn off `module_args_as_configuration` and parse every pair in `graph_init`: uppercase the name, send runtime fields through `validate_config_set` + `apply_config_set`, and give the load-only fields (`CACHE_SIZE`, `THREAD_COUNT`, `OMP_THREAD_COUNT`, `NODE_CREATION_BUFFER`, `INDEX_WORKER_THREADS`, `IMPORT_FOLDER`, `TEMP_FOLDER`, `BOLT_PORT`) a load-time validator with C's rules. (b) Keep the macro and re-apply/validate in `graph_init`. That leaves two parsers that can disagree, and an exact-case value set twice.
2. **Precedence over `graph.*` in redis.conf.** Because the fields are registered as Redis module configs, `graph.CACHE_SIZE 5` in redis.conf currently overrides the module argument (`LoadConfigs` runs after the defaults are taken from the arguments). Under (a), `graph_init` runs after `LoadConfigs`, so module arguments would win. C has no `graph.*` configs, so this only affects Rust-only setups.
3. **Strictness that would newly refuse to start.** Refusing unknown names, odd argument counts, `CACHE_SIZE 0`, `THREAD_COUNT 0` (today "auto") and `MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES 0` matches C, but a Rust deployment that passes any of these today would stop loading after the upgrade. Rust's names are a superset of C's (`EFFECTS_COMPRESSION`, `INDEX_WORKER_THREADS`, `BOLT_PORT` are extra), so nothing valid on C would be refused. `THREAD_COUNT 0` / `OMP_THREAD_COUNT 0` meaning "auto" is Rust-only behaviour that someone may rely on.

### Recommendation

Option (a), with C's rules throughout. Possibly keep `THREAD_COUNT 0` as "auto" (log a warning) as the one deliberate extension. Release-note the stricter start-up and the redis.conf precedence change.

issues.title: fix: nested lists in an effects payload can no longer reserve memory quadratic in its size
issues.body: Closes #3266 ## Problem The v3 `SIValue` decoder checks a nested `T_ARRAY`'s child count only against the bytes left after it, and ignores the siblings that its ancestor frames still owe. Every level of `[[[…` can therefore claim the whole remainder, and each level then calls `ThinVec::with_capacity` for that claim. The reservations add up to the square of the payload. Any client can send `GRAPH.EFFECT`, and a 1 MB payload pushed `redis-server` to a 2.3 GB peak RSS before the decode failed at the end of the buffer. ## Fix `Value::decode` keeps `owed`, the number of children the open frames still need beyond the one being read now (`Σ (left − 1)`). A new list must fit `n + owed` values in the remaining bytes. Its own children and the siblings it would otherwise take bytes from are disjoint byte ranges, so the total capacity reserved across the stack stays at or below `remaining / 4`, which is linear in the payload. Legitimate values are unaffected, because their claims are always backed by real bytes. Peak RSS of `redis-server` after one hostile `GRAPH.EFFECT` (repro script in #3266, fresh server per row, `/usr/bin/time -l`): | payload | Rust `main` | this PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | none (idle) | 23.6 MB | 23.6 MB | – | | 256 KB | 566 MB, fails at EOF | 24.7 MB, refused at once (`ImplausibleCount`) | no v3 decoder | | 1 MB | 2.31 GB, 1.34 s | 25.5 MB, under 10 ms | no v3 decoder | ## Tests - New unit test `effects::v3::value::tests::nested_lists_cannot_each_claim_the_whole_remaining_buffer`, which uses 1,000 levels, each claiming the most its trailing bytes allow. - Before the fix: `FAILED … expected the claim to be refused up front, got UnexpectedEof { want: 4, have: 0 }` - After: `ok`. The payload is refused at the second level. - `cargo test -p graph --lib effects`: 197 passed, including the 5,000-deep round trip and the nested-list round trip. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except the known `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy reports no warnings in the touched file. - Flow tests (RLTest, release): `test_effects_values` 9/9, `test_effects_wire` 14/14, `test_effects_shapes` 22/22, `test_effects_opcodes` 12/12, `test_replication` 2/2. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents a DoS vector where a 1 MB `GRAPH.EFFECT` payload could push `redis-server` to 2.3 GB RSS by reserving memory quadratically. `Value::decode` now tracks how many children the open frames still owe and checks each nested list's count against that total, so capacity reservations stay linear in the payload size. Written for commit d86f3b56049b8c9cac6f506fa18bf98d9b790166. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: [Rust] Nested lists in a client GRAPH.EFFECT payload reserve memory quadratic in its size (1 MB -> 2.3 GB RSS)
issues.body:
### Summary

A nested-list `SIValue` in a `GRAPH.EFFECT` payload can make the v3 decoder reserve memory that grows with the square of the payload size before it fails. Every client can send `GRAPH.EFFECT`, and the payload is decoded before it is rejected. A 1 MB payload pushes the server to a 2.3 GB peak RSS. The reserved address space grows quadratically, to about 16·(bytes/8)² bytes, which is roughly 260 GB for 1 MB.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

The payload is one `CREATE_NODE` record with one attribute. Its value is `levels` nested `T_ARRAY` headers. Level *k* claims `2·(levels−k−1)` children, which is the most that the bytes after it could hold, so every level passes the width check:

```python
import struct, redis
T_ARRAY = 1 << 3
def payload(levels):
    value = b''.join(struct.pack('<II', T_ARRAY, 2 * (levels - k - 1)) for k in range(levels))
    rec = struct.pack('<IIHHHI', 3, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1) + bytes([0, 0, 1])  # CREATE_NODE, 1 id, attr 0
    return bytes([3, 0]) + rec + value
redis.Redis(port=PORT).execute_command('GRAPH.EFFECT', 'h', payload(LEVELS))
# -> ERR effect apply failed: truncated effects buffer: want 4 bytes, have 0
```

Peak RSS of `redis-server` (`/usr/bin/time -l`, fresh server per row, macOS arm64):

| payload | levels | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| none (idle) | 0 | 23.6 MB |
| 128 KB | 16,000 | 291 MB |
| 256 KB | 32,000 | 566 MB |
| 512 KB | 64,000 | 1.13 GB |
| 1 MB | 128,000 | 2.31 GB |

RSS grows by about one touched page per level. The reservations behind those pages add up to the square of the payload. On a host with strict overcommit (`vm.overcommit_memory=2`), an allocation failure aborts the process.

C has no v3 decoder (C `master` is at `EFFECTS_VERSION 2`), so there is nothing to compare against.

### Mechanism

`graph/src/effects/v3/value.rs`, `read_one`, in the `T_ARRAY` arm:

```rust
let n = r.guard_count(u64::from(n), MIN_VALUE_BYTES)?;
stack.push(Frame::List { items: ThinVec::with_capacity(n), left: n });
```

`guard_count` checks `n * 4 <= remaining`. That check covers one level only. `remaining` still includes the bytes that the open ancestor frames need for their own siblings, so every level of `[[[…` can claim the whole remainder, and each level reserves capacity for that claim.

### Expected

The total capacity reserved while decoding is linear in the payload. A claim that cannot fit next to the siblings already owed is refused immediately with `ImplausibleCount`.

### Suggested fix

Keep a count of the children that the open frames still owe, `owed = Σ (left − 1)`, and check `n + owed` instead of `n` for a new list. The children of each open frame are then disjoint byte ranges, so the sum of the capacities stays at or below `remaining / 4`.

### Found by

Lean model of the effects codec (bug ledger), confirmed live as shown above.

issues.title: [Rust] db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes/queryRelationships with a non-string label or query error; C returns no rows
issues.body:
### Summary

`db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes` / `queryRelationships` with a non-string label or query fail the whole query. C returns no rows for them.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:W) ON (n.name)"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CREATE (:W {name:'1'})"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes(1, 2)"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes(null, 'x')"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes('W', 1)"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships(1, 2)"
```

| | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `queryNodes(1, 2)` | `fulltext query expects a string label` | empty result |
| `queryNodes(null, 'x')` | `fulltext query expects a string label` | empty result |
| `queryNodes('W', 1)` | `fulltext query expects a string query` | empty result |
| `queryRelationships(1, 2)` | `fulltext query expects a string relationship type` | empty result |

### Mechanism

The planner rewrites these calls to `NodeByFulltextScan` / `EdgeByFulltextScan`. The ops return `Err` when the evaluated label or query is not a `Value::String` (`graph/src/runtime/ops/node_by_fulltext_scan.rs:87,96`, `edge_by_fulltext_scan.rs:92,101`).

### Expected

No rows, as C, the same as querying a label that has no fulltext index (which Rust already answers with no rows).

### Suggested fix

In both ops, return `Ok(None)` (no rows for this input row) instead of `Err` when the label or query is not a string.

Re-checked against C while filing: `db.idx.fulltext.drop` on a label with no fulltext index errors on **both** engines (`Unable to drop index on :Nope: no such index.`), so that one is not a divergence, only a message-text difference (Rust prints `:Nope()`); it is listed with the other output differences in a separate issue.

issues.title: fix: keep an earlier MATCH … WHERE / UNWIND under a variable-length traverse
issues.body: Refs #2972. This is the variable-length shape of that bug. #3099 fixes the fixed-length `CondTraverse` shape and closes the issue. This PR fixes the separate `CondVarLenTraverse` code path, so it does not close #2972. ## Problem `MATCH (a) WHERE a.v=1 MATCH (a)-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2})` returned rows for every `a`, not only for `a.v = 1`. `plan_query` stitches the first clause, `Filter(AllNodeScan a)`, under the second clause's `CondVarLenTraverse`. `select_var_len_scan_node` (`graph/src/planner/optimizer/select_scan_node.rs`) reverses a leaf traverse when `to` is the more selective end. `planner_scan_alias` looks through `Filter` wrappers, so the stitched clause was taken for the planner's own scan of `from`. The leaf rewrite then pruned it and pushed a bare scan of `b`, keeping only an `Argument` leaf. The non-leaf branch above it already refused a `Filter` wrapper; the leaf branch did not. Anything planned below the scan was dropped too, such as an earlier `UNWIND`. ``` Project Conditional Variable Length Traverse | (a)-[_anon_0*1..2]->(b) Filter Node By Label Scan | (b:B) <- a.v = 1 is gone ``` ## Fix The leaf rewrite now runs only when the subtree is the planner's own scan: no `Filter` wrapper, and nothing under the scan except an `Argument` leaf, which is the only thing it carries over. Otherwise the planner's direction is kept. `IncludePending` (MERGE) is still rebuilt as before. Setup: `CREATE (a1 {v:1})-[:R]->(:B {w:2}), (a2 {v:0})-[:R]->(:B {w:2}), (a3 {v:0})-[:R]->(:X)-[:R]->(:B {w:2})` | query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (a) WHERE a.v=1 MATCH (a)-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2}) RETURN a.v, b.w` | `[1,2],[0,2],[null,2],[0,2]` | `[1,2]` | `[1,2]` | | `UNWIND [1,2] AS i MATCH (a) WHERE a.v = 1 MATCH (a)-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2}) RETURN count(*)` | 4 | 2 | 2 | | `UNWIND [1,2] AS i MATCH (a)-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2}) RETURN count(*)` | 4 | 8 | 8 | | `MATCH (a {v:0})-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2}) RETURN count(*)` (single clause, still scans `b:B`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | ## Tests New `tests/test_e2e.py::test_var_len_traverse_keeps_earlier_clause_below_it` covers the WHERE, WHERE + UNWIND, and UNWIND shapes. It also checks that a single MATCH still starts from the selective end (plan unchanged: `Node By Label Scan | (b:B)`). - before (origin/main b033aecc6 build): `assert [[1, 2], [0, ...e, 2], [0, 2]] == [[1, 2]]`, FAILED - after: passed Other checks (release build, private ports): - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. The one failure, `test_load_csv`, fails the same way on main because the local import folder `/var/lib/FalkorDB/import/` is missing. - Flow: `test_variable_length_traversals` 18/18, `test_varlength_traversal` 9/9, `test_traversal_construction` 16/16, `test_graph_merge` 38/38, `test_optional_match` 27/27, `test_call_subquery` 56/56, `test_path_filter` 19/19, `test_bidirectional_traversals` 12/12, `test_path` 8/8 - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 495 passed. The 1 failure is the known macOS-only `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). - `cargo fmt --check` passes, and `cargo clippy -p graph --all-targets` reports no warnings in `select_scan_node.rs`. This change is optimizer-only. Plans change only for queries that had an earlier clause under the traverse, and those now keep it, as C does. It touches the same file as #3099 and #3046, in a different function (`select_var_len_scan_node`). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes variable-length traversals dropping an earlier `MATCH ... WHERE` filter or `UNWIND` when the planner reversed the traversal to scan the more selective endpoint. - The leaf rewrite now runs only when the subtree below the scan is the planner's own scan (no `Filter` wrapper, only an `Argument` leaf); otherwise the original direction is kept. - Adds e2e tests covering the `WHERE`, `UNWIND`, and combined shapes, and confirms a single-clause traversal still scans the selective end. Written for commit 583a8846fff7f0383cb5f207eac91ad3dfd277b3. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: fix: GRAPH.UDF LOAD rejects an empty library name or script, like C
issues.body: Closes #3259 ## Problem `udf_load` (`src/commands/udf.rs`) checked only the library name's maximum length. An empty name was accepted and its functions registered as `.f`, which no Cypher query can call; an empty script was accepted as a library with no functions. C rejects both. ## Fix Reject them before the length check, with C's messages and in C's order (name first). | | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `GRAPH.UDF LOAD ""

issues.title: fix: give graphs loaded from an RDB the configured CACHE_SIZE
issues.body: Closes #3251 ## Problem `src/redis_type.rs` hard-coded `DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE = 25` and passed it to `rdb_load_graph` in `graph_rdb_load` and `graphmeta_rdb_load`, and to the multi-key placeholder graph. So a graph loaded from an RDB (restart, `DEBUG RELOAD`, a replica's full sync) always had a 25-entry plan cache, whatever `CACHE_SIZE` the module was loaded with. Graphs created at run-time honour it. ## Fix The load callbacks run on the main thread, so `io_cache_size` takes the context Redis attaches to the IO handle (`RedisModule_GetContextFromIO`) and reads `CONFIGURATION_CACHE_SIZE` with it, the way `create_virtual_keys` already reads `VKEY_MAX_ENTITY_COUNT`. The constant is gone. `CACHE_SIZE 1`, `DEBUG RELOAD`, then `RETURN 1`, `RETURN 2`, `RETURN 1`: | | `main` | This PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | `Cached execution` | 0, 0, **1** | 0, 0, 0 | 0, 0, 0 | ## Tests - New flow test `test_cache.testCache.test_15_cache_size_survives_rdb_load` (`CACHE_SIZE 1`, reload, check a second query evicts the first). - Before: `True == False` FAIL at the last `RETURN 1`. - After: pass. - Flow (RLTest, release): `test_cache` 15/15, `test_encode_decode` 19/19 (multi-key load path, `VKEY_MAX_ENTITY_COUNT 10`), `test_persistency` 11/11, `test_rdb_load` 2/2, `test_replication` 2/2. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. `cargo fmt --check` clean; `clippy --all-targets` has no warnings in touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes graphs loaded from an RDB (restart, `DEBUG RELOAD`, or replica full sync) so they use the configured `CACHE_SIZE` instead of the previously hard-coded default of 25. Load callbacks run on the main thread, so they now read the configured value through the context Redis attaches to the IO handle, matching how graphs created at runtime behave. - Adds a flow test that reloads with `CACHE_SIZE 1` and verifies a second query evicts the first from the cache. - Closes #3251. Written for commit 52e5fe159bf3391b98ad7e4754dc6adb16c539ad. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: [Rust] A list or map subscript is rejected as a WHERE predicate (Expected boolean predicate)
issues.body:
### Summary

A list or map subscript (`l[0]`, `m['k']`) is never accepted as a predicate. `WHERE n.flags[0]` fails with `Expected boolean predicate` before the query runs, even when the element is a boolean. C runs the query and checks the element's type at runtime.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:N {flags: [true, false]})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n:N) WHERE n.flags[0] RETURN count(n)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "WITH [true] AS l WHERE true AND l[0] RETURN 1"
GRAPH.QUERY g "WITH {a: true} AS m WHERE m['a'] RETURN 1"
GRAPH.QUERY g "WITH [null] AS l WHERE l[0] RETURN 1"
GRAPH.QUERY g "WITH [1] AS l WHERE l[0] RETURN 1"
```

| query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `WHERE n.flags[0]` | `Expected boolean predicate` | 1 |
| `WHERE true AND l[0]` | `Expected boolean predicate` | 1 row |
| `WHERE m['a']` | `Expected boolean predicate` | 1 row |
| `WHERE l[0]` with `l = [null]` | `Expected boolean predicate` | 0 rows |
| `WHERE l[0]` with `l = [1]` | `Expected boolean predicate` | `Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer` |

A slice (`l[0..1]`) and a negation (`-null`) are rejected by both engines, so those already agree.

### Mechanism

`Binder::expr_may_return_boolean` (`graph/src/planner/binder.rs:2329-2339`) lists `ExprIR::GetElement` with the node kinds that can never be boolean. A subscript returns whatever the element is, so it belongs with `Property`, `Variable` and `Parameter`, which are left to the runtime type check.

### Expected

As in C: the query runs, a boolean element filters, `null` drops the row, and any other type is a runtime type error.

### Suggested fix

Move `ExprIR::GetElement` to the "may be boolean" arm. `GetElements` (slice) always returns a list and stays where it is.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the binder (`proofs/`, ledger entry W4-plan-2).

issues.title: fix: NOT over a pattern predicate drops rows where the predicate is null
issues.body: Closes #3241 ## Problem `Planner::expr_to_plan` planned `NOT (complex)` as `AntiSemiApply(input, plan(inner))`. The inner plan passes a row only when the inner predicate is `true`, so `AntiSemiApply` passed every row where it was not `true`, including the rows where it is `null`. `NOT null` is `null` and should drop the row. ## Fix When `NOT` wraps an `AND`, `OR` or `NOT` (under any parentheses), push it down with De Morgan before planning (`push_not_down`, `graph/src/planner/mod.rs`). These identities hold in three-valued logic. The leaves become `NOT pattern`, planned as `AntiSemiApply` (a pattern is never `null`), or `NOT scalar`, planned as an ordinary `Filter`. Other operators (`XOR`) keep the existing path. Graph: `CREATE (:N {v: 0}), (:N), (:N {v: 5}), (:N)-[:R]->(:M)`, query `MATCH (a:N) WHERE RETURN count(a)`: | predicate | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `NOT (a.v > 1 OR (a)-->())` | 2 | 1 | 1 | | `NOT (a.v > 1 AND (a)-->())` | 4 | 3 | 3 | | `NOT (NOT (a.v > 1 OR (a)-->()))` | 2 | 2 | 2 | | `NOT (a.v = 0 OR NOT (a)-->())` | 1 | 0 | 0 | | `NOT ((a)-->() OR NOT (a.v < 3 AND (a)<--()))` | 0 | 0 | 0 | ## Tests New flow test `test_path_filter.py::test19_negated_pattern_predicate_drops_null_rows`. Before the fix (`main` @ b033aecc6): ``` ❌ (FAIL): [[2]] == [[1]] [NOT (a.v > 1 OR (a)-->())] ❌ (FAIL): [[4]] == [[3]] [NOT (a.v > 1 AND (a)-->())] ❌ (FAIL): [[1]] == [[0]] [NOT (a.v = 0 OR NOT (a)-->())] ``` After: `[PASS]`. Also run: `test_path_filter` (20/20) and every flow suite that uses `NOT` (30 suites, all pass except `test_defrag::test_frag_ratio`, which fails on `main` too); `tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py` (131 passed); `cargo test -p graph --lib` (only the known macOS failure `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, #2922); `cargo fmt --check`; no clippy warnings in the touched code. Planner-only change, no runtime hot path touched. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `NOT` over a pattern predicate returning rows where the negated predicate is `null`. `NOT null` is `null`, so those rows should be dropped, but the planner's `AntiSemiApply` over the inner predicate kept every row where the inner predicate was not `true`, including the `null` ones. - Pushes `NOT` down to the leaves with De Morgan when the wrapped expression is `AND`, `OR`, or `NOT` (under any parentheses), which holds in three-valued logic. - Leaves become `NOT pattern`, planned as `AntiSemiApply` (patterns are never `null`), or `NOT scalar`, planned as a regular `Filter`. - Adds a flow test covering mixed pattern and scalar predicates. Written for commit 020cd2d5b583fdf4a7a8d52a09deccb9c496dfd6. Summary will update on new commits.

issues.title: [Rust] GRAPH.UDF LOAD accepts an empty library name (functions uncallable) and an empty script
issues.body:
### Summary

`GRAPH.UDF LOAD "" <script>` is accepted, but the library's functions can never be called. C rejects it with `empty lib name`. Likewise an empty script is accepted (a library with no functions), where C replies `empty script`.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.UDF LOAD "" "falkor.register('f', function(){ return 1; });"
GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN .f()"
GRAPH.UDF LIST
GRAPH.UDF LOAD x ""
```

| | `LOAD ""` | `RETURN .f()` | `UDF LIST` | `LOAD x ""` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rust | `OK` | parse error | lists a library named `""` with function `f` | `OK` |
| C | `empty lib name` | parse error | — | `empty script` |

### Mechanism

`udf_load` (`src/commands/udf.rs:117`) only checks the name's maximum length (`validate_identifier_len`), never that it is non-empty. The repository registers the function as `.f`, which no Cypher function name can spell. No check on the script either.

### Expected

Reject both, with C's messages: `empty lib name`, `empty script` (C `cmd_udf_load.c` checks the name first).

### Suggested fix

In `udf_load`, before the length check: `if lib_name.is_empty() { return Err("empty lib name") }`, `if script.is_empty() { return Err("empty script") }`.
