issues.title: fix: stop the LIMIT/SKIP budget at row-dropping operators (#2957, #2659)
issues.body:
Closes #2957
Closes #2659

## Problem

`Runtime` pushes a `Limit`'s row budget down the plan, and `CondTraverseOp`, `ExpandIntoOp` and `SortOp`'s top-k treat it as a **hard** stop. The budget came from `effective_limit`, which walked *through* `CondTraverse`/`ExpandInto`, operators that can turn a row into zero rows. It also used `effective_skip`, which counted only the first `Skip`. So a traverse feeding another traverse, stacked `SKIP`s, or a `Sort` feeding a `MATCH` lost rows:

| query | before | C | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (a:A)-[:R]->(b)-[:R]->(a) RETURN a.id LIMIT 1` | `[]` | `[2]` | `[2]` |
| `MATCH (a:A)-[:R]->(b)-[:R]->(c) RETURN c.id LIMIT 1` | `[]` | `[30]` | `[30]` |
| `MATCH (a:A)-[:R]->(b)-[:R]->(c) RETURN c.id SKIP 1 LIMIT 1` | `[]` | `[200]` | `[200]` |
| `MATCH (a:A)-[:R]->(b) WITH b SKIP 0 RETURN b.id SKIP 1 LIMIT 1` | `[]` | `[20]` | `[20]` |
| `UNWIND range(1,20) AS x WITH x ORDER BY x SKIP 0 RETURN x SKIP 10 LIMIT 10` (#2659) | `[]` | `[]` | `11..20` |
| `MATCH (a:A) WITH a ORDER BY a.id MATCH (a)-[:R]->(b) RETURN b.id LIMIT 1` | `[]` | `[]` | `[20]` |

On the last two, C is wrong too. openCypher requires the rows (the `LIMIT` applies after the later clauses), so this PR follows openCypher there and C everywhere else.

## Fix

- One walk, `Runtime::row_budget`, computes both budgets: `Limit n` bounds the budget at `n`, every `Skip s` adds `s`, and `Project` passes it through.
  - **`hard_record_cap`** stops at anything else, including `CondTraverse`/`ExpandInto`. This is the budget proven sound as a stop (Lean `Budget.need_sound`, `proofs/runtime_core`). It feeds the three hard stops: CondTraverse, ExpandInto and Sort top-k (`SortOp` now takes one `record_cap` in place of `limit` and `skip`).
  - **`record_cap`** also walks through traverses and is used only as the `BatchedResultEmitter` pack-ceiling hint. That hint sizes batches and grows back, so it cannot change results (Lean `Emitter.drive_flatten`). This is what keeps early termination: the lower traverse in a two-hop still packs a small first batch. `CondTraverseOp::new`/`ExpandIntoOp::new` take both values.
- `BatchedResultEmitter::emit_lazy` doubled its ceiling even on the empty call operators make before seeding their first input, so the first real batch was 2× the hint. It now grows only after it emits a batch, as the field's doc already said. Without this change, `test_optimizations_plan`'s "Expand Into is aware of limit" check reports 2 records instead of 1. With it, leaf scans under a `LIMIT` produce exactly `LIMIT` rows (below).

## Tests

- New flow tests. Both **fail on `main`** (`[] == [[2]]`, `[] == [[30]]`, `0 == 1`; `[] == [[11]..[20]]`, `[] == [[10],[11],[12]]`, `[] == [[20]]`) and **pass** with the fix:
  - `test_traversal_construction.py::test_limit_budget_through_traversals`
  - `test_order_by.py::test09_top_k_budget`
- New unit test `batched_result_emitter::tests::empty_emit_keeps_the_ceiling`: fails without the emitter change, passes with it. `pack_ceiling_grows_back_to_batch_size` now drives the ceiling with real emitted batches.
- `cargo test -p graph`: 423 passed. `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 125 passed. TCK (`tck_done.txt`) passed. `test_mvcc.py` + `test_concurrency.py`: 14 passed.
- Flow tests, run with RLTest on a private port: `test_optimizations_plan` 32/32, `test_order_by` 9/9, `test_traversal_construction` 17/17, `test_bidirectional_traversals` 12/12, `test_maintain_record_order` 5/5, `test_fulltext_query` 5/5, `test_call_subquery` 54/54, `test_distinct` 10/10, `test_optional_match` 26/26, `test_unwind_clause` 7/7, `test_variable_length_traversals` 17/17.
- `cargo fmt --check` is clean. `clippy --all-targets` reports no warnings in touched code.

## Benchmark

Release build, macOS arm64. Graph: 500k chains `(:N)-[:R]->(:N)-[:R]->(:N)`, 1M edges. Timings are wall-clock per query over redis; C/base/fix runs alternate. The machine is shared (load average 9-11), so p99 is noisy.

| query | C p50 / p99 (ms) | base p50 / p99 | fix p50 / p99 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (a)-[:R]->(b) RETURN b LIMIT 10` | 0.432 / 0.701 | 0.433 / 0.717 | 0.428 / 0.643 |
| `MATCH (a)-[:R]->(b)-[:R]->(c) RETURN c LIMIT 10` | 0.452 / 0.711 | 0.448 / 0.656 | 0.441 / 0.762 |
| `... RETURN b, c LIMIT 10` (unfused 2-hop) | 0.570 / 0.885 | 0.571 / 0.865 | 0.568 / 0.846 |
| `... RETURN b, c SKIP 100 LIMIT 10` | 0.792 / 1.186 | 0.351 / 0.630 ✗ | 0.601 / 1.053 |

That was the 300-run pass. A 500-run repeat gave the same p50s (within 0.02 ms). Its p99s moved ±0.2 ms in both directions (e.g. 1-hop fix 1.158 vs base 0.948; 2-hop fix 0.975 vs base 0.979). ✗: base returns **0 rows** for the SKIP query (C and fix return 10). Its speed comes from stopping early and dropping the answer.

Rows produced per operator (`GRAPH.PROFILE`) show that early termination is kept, and is tighter than before:

| query | C (scan / CT1 / CT2) | base | fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-hop `LIMIT 10` | 20 / 10 | 20 / 10 | **10 / 10** |
| 2-hop `LIMIT 10` | 30 / 20 / 10 | 20 / 10 / 10 | **10 / 10 / 10** |
| 2-hop `SKIP 100 LIMIT 10` | 330 / 220 / 110 | 20 / 10 / 10 (wrong) | **110 / 110 / 110** |

issues.title: [Rust] Batched OPTIONAL MATCH emits NULL-fallback rows after matched rows (order differs from input and from C; low)
issues.body:
### Summary

Low severity. A batched `OPTIONAL MATCH` emits all of a batch's unmatched (NULL) rows **after** all of its matched rows, so the output order differs from the input order. openCypher leaves this order unspecified, but it shows through `collect()` and in results without `ORDER BY`, and C keeps input order.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 2363723ac)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:A {w:1}), (:A {w:2})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND [3,1,2] AS x OPTIONAL MATCH (a:A {w:x}) RETURN collect(x)"
Rust: [1, 2, 3]
C:    [3, 1, 2]
```

### Mechanism

`OptionalOp::next_batched` (`graph/src/runtime/ops/optional.rs:172-186`), and the optional arm of `ApplyOp::next_batched` (`apply.rs:210-229`), emit each sub-plan output batch as soon as it is produced. Only after the sub-plan is exhausted do they gather the origins that never matched into one NULL-fallback batch. Per-row mode keeps input order.

### Expected (C behaviour)

Rows in input order: `[3, 1, 2]`.

### Why no fix yet

Interleaving the fallback rows means buffering all of the sub-plan's output for an input batch and re-gathering it by origin. That adds a copy and a gather to every batched OPTIONAL MATCH, which is a hot path, only to reproduce an order the language does not guarantee. A cheap special case would be: when the sub-plan produced exactly one output batch, merge it with the fallback rows by origin. That still costs a gather per batch. Filed so the divergence is on record. It is worth doing only if a zero-cost way appears, or if matching C's order becomes a requirement.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the correlated operators (`proofs/ops_apply`), theorems `optionalBatched_order_differs` (and `optionalBatched_perm_ref`: the output is only a permutation); Rust repro `graph/tests/lean_ops_apply.rs` (`bug_optional_fallback_rows_reordered`).

issues.title: [Rust] Index created on a label while another is populating is never populated, yet reports OPERATIONAL
issues.body:
### Summary

If a second index is created on a label while the first one is still being populated, the new field is often **never populated**. The index still turns `OPERATIONAL`, and the planner uses it, so queries through it silently return 0 rows. C returns the full count.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 55204c94b)

```
GRAPH.QUERY ti "UNWIND range(0,29999) AS x CREATE (:L {a:x, b:x})"
GRAPH.QUERY ti "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.a)"
GRAPH.QUERY ti "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.b)"       -- sent right after, while (n.a) is populating
-- wait until CALL db.indexes() reports OPERATIONAL
GRAPH.QUERY ti "MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.a >= 0 RETURN count(n)"   -- 30000
GRAPH.QUERY ti "MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.b >= 0 RETURN count(n)"   -- 0      (plan: Node By Index Scan)
```

Out of 10 back-to-back rounds, 7 were wrong at 30k nodes and 8 at 100k (`b` = 0 each time). C: 0 of 5. With 300k nodes and a delay between the two `CREATE INDEX` (`proofs/search_concurrency/repro/twoidx.py`), it depends on timing.

### Mechanism

- `Indexer::create_index` (`graph/src/index/indexer.rs:319-331`) bumps the index generation (`bump_id`) only when it adds a vector field (`recreate_index`). For a range or fulltext field, the new population job gets a ticket in the **same** generation as the one still running.
- `populate_index_batch` (`graph/src/graph/graph.rs:510`) bails when `ticket_pending_changes(&ticket) > 1`. The new job (field snapshot `{a,b}`) is queued while the old job's batch holds the indexer lock. When the lock is released, it usually sees 2 pending tickets and bails first. The old job (snapshot `{a}`) then continues to the end and releases its ticket, `pending` reaches 0, and the index goes OPERATIONAL without `b`.

### Expected

Matches C: every field that is indexed covers all existing entities by the time the index is OPERATIONAL.

### Suggested fix

Bump the generation whenever a field is added to an existing entry, not only for vector fields. The stale job then fails `is_ticket_current` at its next batch, and the new job, which has the full field set, populates from the start.

### Found by

Lean 4 model `proofs/search_concurrency` (`Tickets.second_index_never_populated`, fix: `Tickets.fixed_trace_complete`). Repro: `proofs/search_concurrency/repro/twoidx.py`.

issues.title: fix: push an IN into the range index only when its indexed side is the bare property
issues.body:
Closes #2962

## Problem

`try_in_filter_scan` only checked that one side of `IN` *contains* a property of the scanned alias, then took the first property it found in that subtree. So an `IN` over an expression was pushed as if it were over the bare property:

| Query (index on `:L(a)`) | no index | `main` + index | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WHERE abs(n.a) IN [1]` | 1, 2 | 1 | 1, 2 |
| `WHERE toString(n.a) IN ['1']` | 1 | — | 1 |
| `WHERE n.a + 1 IN [2]` | 1 | — | 1 |
| `WHERE 2 IN [n.a, n.b]` (array-contains on `a`) | 3 | — | 3 |
| `WHERE -1 IN [n.a]` | 2 | — | 2 |

C agrees with the full scan on the rows it returns. C raises a type error for `n.a + 1 IN [2]` and `-1 IN [n.a]`, and Rust without the index does not; this PR doesn't change that.

## Fix

An `IN` is pushed only when the indexed side *is* `Property(<scanned alias>)`: `n.a IN [...]` for InList, `x IN n.a` for array-contains. The comparison path (`try_single_filter_scan`) already had this rule. Other shapes stay as label scan plus filter.

## Tests

- New flow test `test_index_scans.py::test_39_in_needs_the_bare_property` checks that the 5 shapes above aren't pushed and match the full scan, and that `n.a IN [1, 2]` still uses the index. On `main` all 5 fail. With this PR the test passes.
- Flow `test_index_scans` 36/36 with RLTest on a private port.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy reports nothing in `utilize_index.rs`. This runs once per plan, so it isn't a hot path.

Found by the Lean model in `proofs/optimizer_scan` (`IndexCex` C7, C7', C8).

issues.title: fix: match every MERGE input row before creating anything (#3039)
issues.body:
Closes #3039

## Problem

`MergeOp::next` pulled one input batch, ran the match sub-plan for it, created or updated its rows, and only then pulled the next batch. A row in a later batch therefore saw an earlier batch's creations, after their `ON CREATE SET`. A row in the same batch did not; only the created-pattern cache stood in for those. The result depended on where the 1024-row boundaries fell:

```
UNWIND range(1,N) AS x WITH x WHERE x = 1 OR x = N
MERGE (n:L {v: CASE x WHEN 1 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END}) ON CREATE SET n.v = 2
Rust main: N=2 -> 2 nodes, N=1025 -> 1 node        C: 2 and 2
```

## Fix

Do what C's `op_merge.c` does: consume the whole input and match every row before anything is created. The new `MergeOp::match_all` pulls all input batches on the first `next()` and runs one match sub-plan per input batch, so matching stays batched. Creating, `ON MATCH`/`ON CREATE SET` and emitting then proceed over the matched rows in input order, as before. Duplicates within the input are still resolved by the created-pattern cache.

Most of the diff is re-indentation. `git diff -w` is +81/-52, most of it the code moving into `match_all`.

Memory: the operator now holds every input row and its matches until it has emitted them. Before, it held one batch at a time. C holds all input records in the same way (`input_records`, `output_records`).

## Tests

- New flow test `test_graph_merge:testGraphMergeFlow.test41_merge_result_does_not_depend_on_batch_boundaries` uses N = 2, 1025 and 3000, plus duplicates across batches (3000 rows onto 7 nodes). Expected values checked against the C module.
  - Before (`main` @ 2363723ac): FAIL, `1.0 == 2`.
  - After, all with RLTest/pytest on private ports: `test_graph_merge` 39/39, `test_call_subquery` 54/54, `test_constraint` 26/26, `test_foreach` 19/19, `test_effects_opcodes` 12/12, `test_access_del_entity` 18/18, and `tests/test_e2e.py` + `tests/test_mvcc.py` 94/94.
- Bench (release, 20 alternating runs, load avg ~17–28). No difference beyond noise:

| query | main p50 / p99 | this PR p50 / p99 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| all-match, indexed: `UNWIND range(1,20000) AS x MERGE (n:Q {v:x}) RETURN count(*)` over 20k `:Q` nodes | 423.7 / 440.4 ms; swapped 416.1 / 440.4 ms | 420.2 / 431.7 ms; swapped 418.8 / 461.1 ms |
| all-create: `CREATE (t:T) WITH t UNWIND range(1,3000) AS x MERGE (t)-[:R]->(:X {v:x}) RETURN count(*)` | 10.24 / 17.45 ms; swapped 10.48 / 18.08 ms | 10.23 / 16.18 ms; swapped 10.45 / 17.52 ms |

issues.title: fix: reject UDF qualified-name collisions and keep UDF names case-sensitive
issues.body:
Closes #3065

## Problem

- `UdfRepo::load` only compared library names, so `Coll` + `coll` (both registering `f`), or `a` registering `b.c` + `a.b` registering `c`, were both accepted. The second silently replaced the first's function in the registry, and deleting it unregistered the first library's function while `GRAPH.UDF LIST` still showed it.
- The UDF registry and the per-thread JS function cache were keyed by the lowercased qualified name, so `cased.f()` and `cased.F()` both ran `F`, and `COLL.f()` resolved.

C rejects the colliding load (`function: 'coll.f' already registered`), returns 1 / 2 for `cased.f()` / `cased.F()`, and reports `COLL.f` as unknown.

## Fix

- `graph/src/udf/repository.rs`: `load` rejects a library if one of its qualified names equals, ignoring case, a name held by another library (the library being replaced is excluded): `Failed to register UDF library 'coll': function 'coll.f' already registered`. RDB load (`deserialize`) is unchanged so existing data still loads.
- `graph/src/runtime/functions/mod.rs`: `register_udf` / `unregister_udf` / the UDF fallback in `Functions::get` use the exact name. Built-in functions stay case-insensitive.
- `graph/src/udf/js_context.rs`: the JS function cache is keyed and looked up by the exact name.

Matches C, including comparing collisions ignoring case while resolving calls case-sensitively. (C itself then crashes in `UDF_Flush` / `AR_FuncRemoveUDF` after a library registered both `f` and `F`; Rust does not.)

## Tests

- New flow test `tests/flow/test_udf.py::test_qualified_name_collisions`: `coll` after `Coll` and `a.b` after `a` are rejected and the first library keeps working; `REPLACE` of a library with its own names works; `cased.f()`, `cased.F()` return 1, 2; `CASED.f()` is unknown.
  - Before (module built from `main`): FAIL (`[[2, 2]] == [[1, 2]]`, colliding loads accepted, `[[2]] == [[1]]`).
  - After: `tests/flow/test_udf` 45/45 pass (RLTest on a private port).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `CXX=clang++ cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean for touched code.

issues.title: [Rust] UDF libraries: qualified-name collisions accepted (silent shadowing) and function names case-folded
issues.body:
### Summary

UDF library loading accepts qualified-name collisions between libraries, and UDF function names are case-folded, so one library can silently shadow another's function and `f` / `F` in one library run the same body. C rejects the colliding library and keeps names case-sensitive.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 2363723ac)

```
GRAPH.UDF LOAD Coll "falkor.register('f', function(){ return 1; });"
GRAPH.UDF LOAD coll "falkor.register('f', function(){ return 2; });"
-- Rust: OK                C: Failed to evaluate UDF library 'coll', Exception: TypeError: function: 'coll.f' already registered
GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN Coll.f()"
-- Rust: 2 (shadowed)      C: 1
GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN COLL.f()"
-- Rust: 2                 C: Unknown function 'COLL.f'

GRAPH.UDF LOAD a "falkor.register('b.c', function(){ return 1; });"
GRAPH.UDF LOAD a.b "falkor.register('c', function(){ return 2; });"
-- Rust: OK                C: ... function: 'a.b.c' already registered

GRAPH.UDF LOAD cased "falkor.register('f', function(){ return 1; }); falkor.register('F', function(){ return 2; });"
GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN cased.f(), cased.F()"
-- Rust: 2, 2              C: 1, 2
```

Deleting the shadowing library also unregisters the other library's function while `GRAPH.UDF LIST` still shows it.

### Mechanism

- `graph/src/udf/repository.rs:98-140` (`UdfRepo::load`) only checks the library name, not the qualified function names other libraries hold.
- The UDF registry is keyed by the lowercased qualified name (`graph/src/runtime/functions/mod.rs:1121` `register_udf`, `unregister_udf`, `Functions::get`), and so is the per-thread JS function cache (`graph/src/udf/js_context.rs:228`, `call_udf_bridge`).

### Expected

Match C: reject a library whose qualified name is already held by another library (C compares ignoring case), and resolve UDF calls case-sensitively.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the UDF repository (`proofs/algo_udf`, theorems `Repo.collision_accepted`, `Repo.delete_breaks_other`); Rust repros `graph/tests/lean_algo_udf.rs::bug_udf_qualified_name_collision_accepted`, `bug_udf_function_names_case_folded`.

issues.title: fix: merge only conditions served by the same label's index in a multi-label scan
issues.body:
Closes #2960

**Stacked on #2975** (same function; review the last commit, `fix: merge only conditions served by the same label's index…`).

## Problem

For `(n:A:B)` with `x` indexed on `A` and `y` indexed on `B`, `try_filter_pushdown` built one index query from every pushable conjunct (or OR branch) and kept only the first label. The condition on `y` was looked up in `A`'s index, which has no `y` field. `build_query_node` returned a null child, which empties an `AND` and is skipped in an `OR`.

| Query | no index / C | `main` + index | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (n:A:B) WHERE n.x = 1 AND n.y = 2` | `ab` | — | `ab` |
| `MATCH (n:B:A) WHERE n.y = 2 AND n.x = 1` | `ab` | — | `ab` |
| `MATCH (n:A:B {x:1, y:2})` | `ab` | — | `ab` |
| `MATCH (n:A:B) WHERE n.y = 2 OR n.x = 1` | `ab`, `ab2` | `ab` | `ab`, `ab2` |

## Fix

- `AND`: a conjunct is merged only if it is served by the same label as the first merged conjunct. Otherwise it stays in the post-filter.
- `OR`: if the branches need different labels, the predicate is not pushed, and the label scan plus filter is used (as in C).

## Tests

- New flow test `test_index_scans.py::test_37_multi_label_conditions_stay_on_their_index` runs 6 queries (AND, reversed label order, inline map, 3 conjuncts, 2 OR shapes) with and without the indexes. On #2975 without this commit, 5 of 6 fail (for example `[] == [['ab']]`, `[['ab']] == [['ab'], ['ab2']]`). With this commit all pass.
- Flow tests with RLTest on a private port: `test_index_scans` 37/37, `test_constraint` 26/26.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy reports nothing in `utilize_index.rs`.
- Not a hot path: this runs once per plan.

Found by the Lean model in `proofs/index_layer` (`bug_multilabel_and`, `bug_multilabel_or`) and `proofs/optimizer_scan` (`IndexCex` C5, C6).

issues.title: fix: bulk-imported attribute spans never overflow Slot::len
issues.body:
Refs #2539 (fixes the silent loss of *every* property; the separate "reject the CREATE with C's error" part stays open there)

## Problem

`Slot.len` is a `u16` written as `n as u16` (`attribute_store.rs:598`, `:609`). The bulk import path handed the span writer every resolved column, including columns the full dictionary refused to mint (`ATTRIBUTE_ID_NONE`). With 65,535 real ids plus the sentinel, the span had 65,536 entries, so `len = 0` and the node lost all its properties. With 65,537 entries it kept one. Live through `GRAPH.BULK`: N=65,536 → `size(keys(n)) = 0`, `n.p0 = NULL`.

## Fix

`AttributeStore::import_attrs_resolved` now brings each span to the invariant the RDB decoder already enforces through `attr_limit`: after the (stable) sort it removes repeated ids, keeping the first column, and drops a trailing `ATTRIBUTE_ID_NONE`. A span therefore has at most 65,535 entries and fits `Slot.len`. Widening `Slot.len` was the alternative, but it would add 4 bytes per entity. The refused names read as absent, which is the contract in `get_or_create`'s doc comment.

## Tests

New unit test `attribute_store::tests::resolved_import_never_overflows_the_slot_length`: 65,535 real ids plus 1, 2 or 70 sentinel entries keep all 65,535 values; a repeated id keeps its first value.

- Before (fix reverted, test kept): `assertion left == right failed: extra = 1, left: 65536, right: 65535`.
- After: passes. `cargo test -p graph`: 422 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `batched_result_emitter::tests::cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, which is unrelated and fails the same way without this change (this PR touches only `attribute_store.rs`).
- Live `GRAPH.BULK` with N = 65,535 / 65,536 / 65,537 properties: before `[65535,…]`, `[0, NULL, NULL]`, `[1, 0, NULL]`; after `[65535, 0, 65534]` for all three.
- Flow `test_bulk_insertion` 14/14 (RLTest on a private port).
- Bulk load of 500k nodes × 5 properties, 8 alternating A/B runs (load ~20-30): base median 234.7 ms, fix median 233.3 ms.
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets` no warnings in the touched file.

This overlaps with #3026 (GRAPH.BULK duplicate header column) on repeated ids. Both keep the first value, so they agree and can merge in either order.

issues.title: fix: pattern predicates in WITH ... WHERE refer to pre-projection variables (#3061)
issues.body:
Closes #3061

## Problem

In `WITH … WHERE`, a scalar predicate can read a variable from before the projection, but a pattern predicate could not. `bind_graph` looks aliases up only in the current scope table, so the pattern's `n` became a fresh, unconstrained node:

* `MATCH (n) WITH n.v AS k WHERE (n)-->() RETURN k` gave all 3 rows (C: `[[1]]`);
* `WHERE NOT (n)-->()` gave `[]` (C: `[[0],[5]]`).

Pattern comprehensions already copied parent names in first. But when the projection had renamed the variable (`WITH n AS m WHERE size([(n)-->(x) | x]) > 0`), both forms still missed it: `resolve_name` returns the variable under `m`.

## Fix

`Binder::import_parent_names`, used by both pattern comprehensions and pattern predicates when parent-scope names are visible:

* a parent variable is copied in under its own name, as before for comprehensions;
* a renamed one is entered under the pattern's name while the pattern is bound, and removed afterwards (its id stays held by `m`, so no id is freed).

This matches C for the pattern-predicate forms. For the renamed comprehension form C errors out, while Rust now gives the answer the scalar form implies.

## Tests

* New flow test `test_with_clause.py::test17_where_pattern_predicate_reads_the_pre_projection_variable`, with five queries, run with RLTest on a private port. All five fail on `main`; with the fix, 15/15.
* Also pass with the fix: `test_comprehension_functions` 25/25, `test_optional_match` 26/26, `test_query_validation` 50/50, `test_path_filter` 19/19, `test_order_by` 8/8, `test_call_subquery` 54/54, `test_star_projections` 5/5.
* `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 125 passed. fmt is clean and clippy reports nothing new.
* The change is bind-time only; no hot path is touched.

issues.title: [Rust] Pattern predicate in WITH ... WHERE rebinds a pre-projection variable as a fresh node (WHERE (n)-->() tests any node)
issues.body:
### Summary

In `WITH … WHERE`, a scalar predicate can read a variable from before the projection: `WITH n.v AS k WHERE n.v > 0` refers to the matched `n`, in both C and Rust. A **pattern predicate** naming that variable does not refer to it in Rust. Its `n` is bound as a fresh, unconstrained node, so the predicate tests "does any node have an out-edge" instead of "does this `n`".

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 2363723ac)

Graph: `CREATE (:A {v:1})-[:R {w:2}]->(:B {v:0}), (:B {v:5})`

| query | C | Rust |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (n) WITH n.v AS k WHERE (n)-->() RETURN k` | `[[1]]` | **`[[0],[1],[5]]`** |
| `MATCH (n) WITH n.v AS k WHERE NOT (n)-->() RETURN k` | `[[0],[5]]` | **`[]`** |
| `MATCH (n) WITH n.v AS k WHERE (n)<--() RETURN k` | `[[0]]` | **`[[0],[1],[5]]`** |
| `MATCH (n) WITH n AS m WHERE (n)-->(:B) RETURN m.v` | `[[1]]` | **`[[0],[1],[5]]`** |
| `MATCH (n) WITH n AS m WHERE size([(n)-->(x) \| x]) > 0 RETURN m.v` | error (C can't resolve the comprehension) | **`[[0],[1],[5]]`** (expected `[[1]]`) |

### Mechanism

`bind_graph` resolves pattern aliases through `define_name_in_scope` (`graph/src/planner/binder.rs:2114-2121`), which only looks in the current scope table. The parent-scope lookup that scalar references get lives in `resolve_name` (`:2182`). Pattern comprehensions copy parent names in first (`:1853`), but pattern predicates do not. And when the projection renamed the variable (`WITH n AS m`), `resolve_name` finds it through `parent_to_child_scope`, but under `m`, so even the comprehension pre-copy leaves `n` undefined for `bind_graph`.

### Expected

Match C: in `WITH … WHERE` (and ORDER BY), a pattern's name that matches a pre-projection variable refers to that variable, as it does in a scalar predicate.

### Suggested fix

Share the pattern comprehension's pre-copy with pattern predicates. When the resolved variable lives under another name (the rename case), enter it under the pattern's name for the duration of the pattern bind.

### Found by

Lean model `proofs/binder` (W2-binder-7): `defineName_ignores_parent`. Rust repro `graph/tests/lean_binder.rs::bug_with_where_pattern_predicate_ignores_outer_variable`.

issues.title: fix: parser accepts invalid / rejects valid syntax (NOT NOT, SET [n), f(1,), MATCH MATCH, LOAD CSV WITH, IS NULL IN)
issues.body:
Closes #3057

## Problem

Several small slips in the hand-written parser let it accept inputs outside the openCypher grammar, some of which then ran with a changed meaning. One input the grammar allows was rejected. C follows the grammar in each case:

| Query | `main` | This PR | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RETURN NOT NOT 1` | `1` | `Type mismatch: expected Boolean` | type mismatch |
| `MATCH (n) SET [n).x = 5` | runs as `SET n.x = 5` | syntax error | syntax error |
| `MATCH (n) REMOVE [n).x` | runs as `REMOVE n.x` | syntax error | syntax error |
| `RETURN 1 IS NULL IN [false]` | syntax error | `true` | `true` |
| `RETURN abs(-1,)` | `1` | syntax error | syntax error |
| `MATCH MATCH (n) RETURN n` | `[]` | syntax error | syntax error |
| `LOAD CSV WITH FROM 'x' AS r …` | accepted | `expected Headers` | `expected WITH HEADERS` |

## Fix

All in `graph/src/parser/cypher.rs`:

- **NOT run** (level 3 of `parse_expr_inner`): a run of NOTs folds to one `Not` (odd count) or two (even count) instead of to one or none. `NOT NOT x` keeps NOT's operand type check, and a run of 20,000 NOTs is still two levels deep, so `collapsing_nesting_is_not_capped` still holds.
- **`IS [NOT] NULL`** (level 5): after the `IS` loop, push the frame back onto level 5 instead of returning. More string, list or null predicates can then follow, per `( SP | LP | NP )*`.
- **`parse_expression_list`**: only an empty list may close at once. After a `,` an expression is required.
- **SET/REMOVE targets**: `recurse` from `parse_primary_expr` is accepted only for a `(`. A new `reject_unparenthesized_target` rejects an open list literal, which used to be dropped.
- **`MATCH MATCH`**: removed the stray `optional_match_token!(Match)`.
- **`LOAD CSV WITH`**: `HEADERS` is required after `WITH`.

The issue lists `'a' IS NULL STARTS WITH 'a'` too. It now parses, but Rust returns null for `STARTS WITH` on a non-string where C raises a type error. That is an evaluation difference outside this parser change.

## Tests

- New unit tests in `parser::cypher::tests`:
  - `invalid_syntax_is_rejected`: six rejections, plus six valid neighbours that must still parse.
  - `predicates_chain_after_is_null`
  - `not_not_keeps_its_type_check`: 1 to 5 NOTs give 1, 2, 1, 2, 1 `Not` nodes.

  All three fail on `main` (`accepted "RETURN abs(-1,)"`, `rejected "RETURN 1 IS NULL IN [false]"`, `left: 0, right: 2`) and pass with the fix.
- New e2e tests `test_syntax_outside_the_grammar_is_rejected`, `test_predicates_after_is_null` and `test_not_not_type_checks_its_operand`. All three fail against the `main` module and pass with the fix. The SET test also checks that the property is unchanged.
- `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: all pass. TCK (`TCK_DONE=tck_done.txt`) passes.
- Flow tests (RLTest, release), all green:

  | Test | Passed |
  |---|---|
  | `test_query_validation` | 50 |
  | `test_function_calls` | 96 |
  | `test_filters` | 9 |
  | `test_null_handling` | 9 |
  | `test_load_csv` | 18 |
  | `test_entity_update` | 44 |
  | `test_label_update` | 6 |
  | `test_optional_match` | 26 |
  | `test_multi_pattern` | 7 |
  | `test_comprehension_functions` | 25 |
  | `test_path_filter` | 19 |
- `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922, which already fails on macOS arm64). `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy --all-targets` are clean.

## Conflict note

This conflicts textually with #2900, which replaces the two `if recurse { … }` blocks in `parse_set_items` / `parse_remove_items` with `parse_update_target`. Whichever lands second should move the one-line `self.reject_unparenthesized_target(&expr)?;` into `parse_update_target`'s `if recurse` branch. It merges cleanly with #2908, #2910, #3019 and #3041.

issues.title: fix: keep columnar unbound-slot semantics in Batch::concat and to_owned_row
issues.body:
Closes #2971

## Problem

Two columnar primitives disagree with their row-at-a-time definition about whether a slot is unbound (`None`) or in scope (`Some(Null)`). This is latent: no Cypher trigger is known, and both bugs reproduce on the `pub` batch API.

1. **`Batch::concat`** (generic fallback, `batch.rs:990-997`) set `bound_anywhere` from every input batch, including batches with no active rows. A slot bound only in an empty batch came out **bound**. The per-row concat, and the typed fast path `concat_typed_column`, leave it unbound.
2. **`BatchRow::to_owned_row`** (`batch.rs:1403`) inserted only non-`Unbound` columns, so the owned `Row` ended at the last bound column. For a trailing unbound slot, `view.value_at(i) == Some(Null)` but `to_owned_row().value_at(i) == None`, and `resolve_var` turns that `None` into "Variable ... not found".

## Fix

1. The `concat` fallback loop skips batches with `active_len() == 0`, as `concat_typed_column` already does.
2. `to_owned_row` builds the row with one slot per batch column, using the new `Row::push_slot(value, bound)`. An `Unbound` column becomes an unbound `Null` slot, and a value-only column keeps its value with the bound bit cleared (same as before). `Row`'s `Hash` already skips unbound `Null` slots, and `BatchBuilder` turns them back into `Column::Unbound`.

   The first version only padded the old row at the end. That cost about 4% p50 on a 2M-row `UNION ALL` (each union branch has the other branch's column as a trailing `Unbound`). The single-pass push replaces the per-slot `insert_by_id` bounds check and resize, and costs nothing (numbers below).

Not changed: `VectorEval::eval_variable` (`vector_expr.rs:310`) has the same shape beyond the batch's column space (it reads `Null` where per-row eval errors). No query reaches it, and a regression test needs a full `Runtime`, so it is noted in #2971 but left out of this PR.

## Tests

New unit tests in `graph/src/runtime/batch.rs` (`runtime::batch::tests`):
- `concat_ignores_bindings_of_empty_batch`: before the fix it fails with `assertion failed: !concat.is_bound_at(1, 0)`; after the fix it passes.
- `to_owned_row_keeps_trailing_unbound_slots_in_scope`: before the fix it fails with `slot 1  left: "Some(Null)"  right: "None"`; after the fix it passes.

Also run on this branch:
- The Lean repros `graph/tests/lean_columnar.rs::latent_concat_empty_batch_binds_column` and `latent_to_owned_row_drops_trailing_unbound_slot` fail on `main` and pass here. The other 7 tests in that file still pass. The file itself is not part of this PR.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `CXX=clang++ cargo clippy --all-targets`: no warnings in touched files.
- `cargo test -p graph`: 423 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `batched_result_emitter::tests::cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (`1025 != 1024`), is in a file this PR does not touch; it only exercises `BatchedResultEmitter::new`.
- `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 125 passed. TCK (`tck_done.txt`): passed. `test_mvcc.py` and `test_concurrency.py`: 14 passed.
- Flow tests (RLTest on a private port, `flow_tests_done.txt`): all pass, except `test_udf_cluster`, which was not run (it needs cluster mode). `test_varlength_traversal` and `test_effects_ddl` also pass when rerun in isolation; their failures in the batched run came from a leftover cluster instance and a timing race.

## Benchmark (release, macOS, shared machine with load avg 12-30; base = `main` @ 55204c94b)

A/B interleaved on two servers, 1M-node graph, client-side ms:

| query | runs | base p50 / p99 | fix p50 / p99 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CALL { MATCH (n:N) RETURN n.v AS v UNION ALL MATCH (m:M) RETURN m.v AS v } RETURN count(v)` (2M rows) | 40 | 185.2 / 240.8 | 182.2 / 280.0 |
| `MATCH (n:N) OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[:R]->(x) RETURN count(x)` (1M rows) | 40 | 103.0 / 119.5 | 103.7 / 127.3 |
| same, 2nd run | 40 | 100.9 / 114.2 | 99.9 / 121.4 |
| `MATCH (n:N) WITH n.v AS v, n.s AS s ORDER BY v, s RETURN count(s)` (full sort → `Batch::concat`) | 30 | 443.6 / 1351.6 | 421.9 / 996.6 |
| `MATCH (n:N) RETURN n.v, n.s ORDER BY n.s DESC LIMIT 10` (top-k, `to_owned_row`) | 30 | 180.6 / 220.9 | 181.9 / 262.1 |
| `MATCH (a:A), (b:B) RETURN count(*)` (cartesian → `Batch::concat`) | 30 | 17.8 / 20.1 | 17.5 / 19.9 |

p50 is within ±2% (noise), except full sort at -5%. p99 moves in both directions; on this loaded machine that is noise.

issues.title: fix: handle unknown labels / relationship types in algo.* like C
issues.body:
Closes #3056

## Problem

- `algo.pageRank('Nope', NULL)` (or a label no node has) failed with `LAGr_PageRank failed: -6`: the compact matrix was 0x0. `algo.pageRank(NULL, 'Nope')` ranked every node because the unknown type was dropped. C returns no rows for all of these.
- `algo.betweenness`, `algo.labelPropagation` and `algo.HarmonicCentrality` silently returned no rows for an unknown `nodeLabels` entry (or ignored it next to a known one) and ran unfiltered for an unknown `relationshipTypes` entry. C fails with a configuration error.

`graph/src/runtime/functions/algo_procedures.rs`:
- `check_known_labels_and_types` helper; betweenness, labelPropagation and HarmonicCentrality call it right after parsing (before the empty-graph early return, as C errors on an empty graph too) with C's exact messages. HarmonicCentrality's existing relationship-type check is replaced (message changes from `Relationship type 'X' does not exist` to C's `harmonic centrality configuration contains non-existent type:X`).

Matches C. Not changed: `algo.WCC({nodeLabels:['Nope']})` — C returns every node there (drops the unknown label and runs unfiltered), which looks like the odd one out; Rust keeps returning no rows.

issues.title: [Rust] Parser accepts invalid syntax (NOT NOT x → x, SET [n).x, f(1,), MATCH MATCH, LOAD CSV WITH FROM) and rejects x IS NULL IN [..]
issues.body:
### Summary

The hand-written parser accepts several inputs outside the openCypher grammar, some of which then run with a changed meaning. It also rejects one input the grammar allows. Each case is a small local slip in `graph/src/parser/cypher.rs`. C matches the grammar in every case below.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 55204c94b)

| # | Query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `RETURN NOT NOT 1` | `1` | `Type mismatch: expected Boolean or Null but was Integer` |
| 2 | `MATCH (n:N) SET [n).x = 5 RETURN n.x` | `5` (runs as `SET n.x = 5`) | `Invalid input ')' …` |
| 2 | `MATCH (n) REMOVE [n).x` | runs as `REMOVE n.x` | syntax error |
| 3 | `RETURN 1 IS NULL IN [false]` | `Unexpected clause following RETURN … pos 16` | `true` |
| 3 | `RETURN 'a' IS NULL STARTS WITH 'a'` | same syntax error | parses (then a type error) |
| 4 | `RETURN abs(-1,)` | `1` | `Invalid input ')' …` |
| 5 | `MATCH MATCH (n) RETURN n` | `[]` | `Invalid input '(': expected '='` |
| 6 | `LOAD CSV WITH FROM 'x' AS r RETURN r` | parses (fails later on the file path) | `Invalid input 'F': expected WITH HEADERS` |

### Mechanism

1. **`NOT NOT x` → `x`** (`cypher.rs:2193`): the NOT prefix keeps only the parity of the count, so an even run disappears. NOT type-checks its operand, so the check is lost with it.
2. **`SET`/`REMOVE` target** (`3225-3229`, `3291-3295`): `parse_primary_expr` returns `recurse = true` for both `(` and an open list `[`. The target code treats both as `(`: it drops the list node, parses `n`, and expects `)`.
3. **Predicate after `IS NULL`** (`2405`): after the `IS [NOT] NULL` loop, level 5 returns instead of going back for more predicates. The grammar is `AddOrSubtract ( StringPredicate | ListPredicate | NullPredicate )*`.
4. **Trailing comma** (`parse_expression_list`, `2722`): after `,` the loop re-checks for the closing `)` and stops, so `f(1,)` is `f(1)`.
5. **`MATCH MATCH`** (`924`): an `optional_match_token!(Match)` right after `MATCH`.
6. **`LOAD CSV WITH FROM`** (`940`): `optional(With) && optional(Headers)` makes `HEADERS` optional after `WITH`.

### Expected

Match the grammar and C: reject 2, 4, 5 and 6; accept 3; keep NOT's type check in 1.

### Suggested fix

1. Fold a run of NOTs to one or two by parity, never to zero. This keeps `NOT NOT … x` from nesting deeper, which the "collapsing nesting is not capped" test relies on.
2. When `recurse` comes back for a SET/REMOVE target, require that the node is a `Paren`.
3. After `IS [NOT] NULL`, push the frame back onto level 5.
4. Require an expression after every `,`.
5. Drop the stray `optional_match_token!(Match)`.
6. Require `HEADERS` after `WITH`.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the parser (`proofs/parser_grammar`), theorems `not_not_dropped`, `set_bracket_paren_accepted`, `is_null_then_predicate_rejected`, `call_trailing_comma`. The clause cases were found by differential tests against C. Rust repros are in `graph/tests/lean_parser_grammar.rs`: `bug_not_not_is_dropped`, `bug_set_remove_bracket_target_accepted`, `bug_predicate_after_is_null_rejected`, `bug_call_trailing_comma_accepted`, `bug_match_match_accepted`, `bug_load_csv_with_without_headers_accepted`.

issues.title: fix: MERGE with a path variable returns every match over bound endpoints (#3040)
issues.body:
Closes #3040

## Problem

`MergeOp::next` has a shortcut: when every node and every *named* relationship of the pattern is already bound, it emits only the first match. A path variable binds the anonymous relationship too, so each parallel edge is a different row:

```
CREATE (a:A),(b:B),(a)-[:R {k:1}]->(b),(a)-[:R {k:2}]->(b)
MATCH (a:A),(b:B) MERGE p=(a)-[:R]->(b) RETURN count(p)
Rust main: 1      C: 2
```

## Fix

Take the shortcut only when the pattern has no path variable (`pattern.paths().is_empty()`, `ops/merge.rs`). Without a path variable nothing changes: C also returns one row for `MERGE (a)-[:R]->(b)`, and the test checks that.

## Tests

- New flow test `test_graph_merge:testGraphMergeFlow.test40_merge_path_over_bound_endpoints_keeps_every_match`. Expected values checked against the C module.
  - Before (`main` @ 2363723ac): FAIL, `[[1]] == [[1], [2]]`.
  - After: `tests/flow/test_graph_merge` passes 39/39, run with RLTest on a private port.
- No benchmark: the change adds one emptiness check per matched input row, and only on patterns with no path variable; nothing else on the path changes.

issues.title: fix: drop a collapsed edge from its siblings' uniqueness checks
issues.body:
Closes #3047

## Problem

`reduce_expand_into` sets `emit_relationship = false` on a named edge nothing reads. The traverse then yields one row per (src, dst) pair and binds one representative edge. The sibling traverses of the same pattern still listed that edge in `sibling_edges`, and `edge_already_used` rejected the representative. So the count depended on which parallel edge happened to be picked:

```
CREATE (a:N {id:1}), (b:N {id:2}), (c:N {id:3}),
       (a)-[:R {w:1}]->(b), (a)-[:R {w:2}]->(b), (b)-[:R {w:3}]->(c)
MATCH (a)-[r]->(x)<-[s]-(c) RETURN count(*)          -- main: 1          C: 2
MATCH (a)-[r]->(x)<-[s]-(c) RETURN a.id, c.id        -- main: (1,1)      C: (1,1), (2,2)
```

## Fix

When `reduce_expand_into` collapses an edge, it also removes it from the `sibling_edges` of every `CondTraverse` / `ExpandInto` in the same scope (`forget_sibling_edge`). A collapsed edge stands for all of its parallel edges, so it takes no part in uniqueness. That is C's semantics for unread edges: the count is the number of endpoint pairs. Edges that are emitted per edge (read by `RETURN r.w`, a path, ...) keep the check, so `RETURN r.w, s.w` still gives openCypher's 2 rows. C gives 4 there because it does no uniqueness check at all.

I rejected the alternative, keeping a sibling-read edge un-collapsed. It gives neither C's nor openCypher's count on chains (per-edge `r` × per-pair `s`), and it disables the batched path for every same-type multi-hop pattern.

PR #2918 (#2896) does not fix this: its `ir_references_variable` / `variable_read_outside` do not consider `sibling_edges`. This PR is based on `main`. Both touch `reduce_expand_into.rs`, but this one only adds a call in the `!referenced` branch and a new function, so rebasing either on the other is mechanical.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_e2e.py::test_collapsed_edge_takes_no_part_in_uniqueness`: `count(*)` (untyped and `:R`), `a.id, c.id`, the forward chain `(a)-[r]->(x)-[s]->(c)` (1, as in C), and `r.w, s.w` with both read (openCypher's two rows).
  - On `main` (release): **fails**, `[[1]] == [[2]]`.
  - With the fix: **passes**.
- Flow tests (RLTest on a private port): `test_optimizations_plan` 32/32, `test_traversal_construction` 16/16, `test_bidirectional_traversals` 12/12, `test_path_filter` 19/19, `test_call_subquery` 54/54.
- Run on the combined W2 fix build:
  - `cargo test --release -p graph`: 422 passed.
  - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 128 passed.
  - TCK (`tck_done.txt`): passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `CXX=clang++ cargo clippy --all-targets`: no warnings in touched code.

## Bench

Release, 40 alternating main/fix runs (A/B/A/B), machine load ~30. The graph has 3000 `:T` nodes, each with 2 targets and 2 parallel `:R` edges per target. Times in ms:

| query | main p50 | main p99 | fix p50 | fix p99 | rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (a:T)-[r:R]->(b)-[s:R]->(c) RETURN count(*)` | 11.23 | 12.82 | **2.21** | **2.90** | 12000 = 12000 |
| `MATCH (a:T)-[r:R]->(b)<-[s:R]-(c) RETURN count(*)` | 11.80 | 13.44 | **8.36** | **9.36** | 12000 = 12000 |
| `MATCH (a:T)-[r:R]->(b)-[s:R]->(c) RETURN count(s)` | 12.30 | 13.96 | 12.48 | 13.05 | 24000 = 24000 |
| `MATCH (a:T)-[:R]->(b)-[:R]->(c) RETURN count(*)` | 2.15 | 3.35 | 2.14 | 2.33 | 12000 = 12000 |

The first two get faster because a traverse whose `sibling_edges` is now empty qualifies for the batched path (`cond_traverse.rs:311`).

Found by the Lean model in `proofs/ops_traverse` (`twoHop_collapse_changes_count`).

issues.title: fix: GRAPH.MEMORY accepts SAMPLES 0; GRAPH.CONSTRAINT parses entity type and count as C

Closes #3052

## Problem

- `GRAPH.MEMORY USAGE g SAMPLES 0` was rejected; C accepts any non-negative count and clamps it to `1..=10000`.
- `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT` accepted `LABEL`/`EDGE` as entity types and `+1`/`01` as property counts, creating constraints C refuses.

issues.title: fix: skip SET/REMOVE on a relationship the query already deleted (#2967)
issues.body:
Closes #2967

## Problem

A write to a relationship the query has already deleted was applied and counted. The same write to a deleted node is skipped, which is also what C does.
- `MATCH ()-[r]->() DELETE r REMOVE r.v`: the `Value::Relationship` arm in `ops/remove.rs` had no deletion check. Result: `Properties removed: 1`, where C reports none.
- `MATCH (a)-[r]->() DETACH DELETE a SET r.v = 2`: the cascaded edge is recorded only in `Runtime::deleted_relationships` (the snapshot map) until commit. `ops/set.rs` did not consult that map, so the write went through. Result: `Properties set: 1, Properties removed: 1`, where C reports none.

## Fix

Add one predicate, `Runtime::is_relationship_deleted`. It returns true if the edge is pending-deleted, if it is committed-deleted and not recreated this segment, or if it is snapshotted as deleted.
- SET uses it in place of its inline check.
- REMOVE now skips such edges. The `REMOVE r:Label` type error still fires first.
- SET's `skip_delete_checks` pre-check also looks at the relationship snapshot map.

Interplay with #2964: a snapshotted id is treated as deleted. That is sound once #2964 drops the snapshot when the id is reissued. Without #2964, a reissued id already reads as the dead edge everywhere (#2876).

Cost: REMOVE on 100k relationships (`MATCH ()-[r:R]->() REMOVE r.v`), release build, 20 alternating runs, 2 rounds, shared machine with load 20-35. p50 main 95.8 / 116.5 ms vs fix 97.5 / 116.2 ms. That is within noise. The max-of-20 values (118/157 vs 153/166) are noisy too.

## Tests

New flow test `test_graph_deletion.py::test15_1_writes_to_deleted_relationships_are_skipped`. It covers REMOVE after DELETE, and SET and REMOVE after a DETACH cascade. Expected values were checked against the C module.
- On `main`: fails 4 assertions (`1.0 == 0` for properties_removed / properties_set).
- With the fix: passes.

Also run with the fix, via RLTest on a private port and all passing: flow `test_graph_deletion` (46), `test_entity_update` (44), `test_edge_index_updates`, `test_graph_merge`, `test_foreach`, `test_constraint`, `test_call_subquery`, `test_effects_commit`, `test_effects_shapes`. `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_mvcc.py`: 94 passed. `cargo fmt --check` and clippy are clean.

issues.title: fix: scope MERGE's created-pattern cache to its own operator (#3038)
issues.body:
Closes #3038

## Problem

`Runtime::merge_pattern_cache` remembers the bindings a MERGE created, so that a later row with the same pattern reuses them. It was keyed only by the pattern hash, so it was shared by every MERGE clause of the query. A later clause with an equal pattern that found no match in the graph got a hit on the earlier clause's entry and inserted the **earlier clause's** variable ids:

```
MERGE (a:M {v:1}) ON CREATE SET a.v = 2 MERGE (b:M {v:1}) RETURN a.v, b.v
Rust main: Variable b not found (rolled back)      C: 2|1, 2 nodes
MERGE (a:U {v:1}) ON CREATE SET a.v = 2 RETURN a.v AS v UNION ALL MERGE (b:U {v:1}) RETURN b.v AS v
Rust main: 2, 2 and 1 node                         C: 2, 1 and 2 nodes
```

## Fix

Key the cache by `(MergeOp plan node, pattern hash)`, so each MERGE operator dedups only its own creations, like C's per-op `unique_entities` (`runtime.rs`, `ops/merge.rs`).

## Tests

- New flow test `test_graph_merge:testGraphMergeFlow.test39_equal_patterns_in_separate_merge_clauses` covers two clauses and two UNION branches.
  - Before (`main` @ 2363723ac): FAIL, `Variable b not found`.
  - After, with RLTest on a private port: `tests/flow/test_graph_merge` passes 39/39 and `tests/flow/test_call_subquery` passes 54/54.
- Bench (release, 20 alternating runs, load avg ~45): `CREATE (t:T) WITH t UNWIND range(1,20000) AS x MERGE (t)-[:R {v: x % 2000}]->(:X) RETURN count(*)` goes through the cache 18k times per run. Neutral within noise:

issues.title: fix: keep CREATE and pattern-comprehension labels out of the MATCH label set (#3048)
issues.body:
Closes #3048

## Problem

The binder collects every label written on a node variable into one set per variable (`node_labels`), and `update_all_node_labels` writes that set into every MATCH occurrence of the node. OPTIONAL MATCH and pattern predicates save and restore the set around their pattern. CREATE and pattern comprehensions did not, so their labels tightened the earlier MATCH scan:

* `MATCH (a) CREATE (a:Z)-[:T]->(:C) RETURN count(*)` gave `[[0]]` (C: `[[3]]`);
* `MATCH (a) RETURN a.v, [(a:A)-->(b) | b.v] AS l` returned only the `:A` node (C: all three, with `[]` for the others).

## Fix

Save and restore `node_labels` around the CREATE bind and around a pattern comprehension's `bind_graph`, the same way OPTIONAL MATCH and pattern predicates already do.

* A node created by CREATE cannot be referenced by a later MATCH without a `WITH`, and `WITH` gives it a new id, so nothing downstream needs CREATE's labels in the set.
* The comprehension's own pattern still gets its labels at bind time.

This matches C.

## Tests

* New flow tests, run with RLTest on a private port, fail on `main` and pass with the fix:
  * `test_create_clause.py::test20_create_labels_do_not_constrain_the_match`: `[[0]] == [[3]]` on main; 8/8 with the fix.
  * `test_comprehension_functions.py::test25_pattern_comprehension_labels_do_not_constrain_the_match`: `[[1, [0]]] == [[0, []], [1, [0]], [5, []]]` on main; 26/26 with the fix.
* Also pass with the fix: `test_optional_match` 26/26, `test_query_validation` 50/50, `test_with_clause` 14/14, `test_foreach` 19/19, `test_graph_create` 10/10, `test_path_filter` 19/19.
* `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 125 passed. fmt is clean and clippy reports nothing new.
* The change is bind-time only; no hot path is touched.

issues.title: [Rust] Labels from CREATE and from pattern comprehensions tighten the earlier MATCH scan (0/1 rows where C returns 3)
issues.body:
### Summary

The binder merges every label written on a node variable, across the whole query, into one set per `(scope, id)`, and writes that set back into **every** occurrence of the node (`update_all_node_labels`). Only OPTIONAL MATCH and pattern predicates save and restore this set. CREATE and pattern comprehensions do not, so their labels tighten the scan of the MATCH that bound the node.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 2363723ac)

Graph: `CREATE (:A {v:1})-[:R {w:2}]->(:B {v:0}), (:B {v:5})`

| query | C | Rust |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (a) CREATE (a:Z)-[:T]->(:C) RETURN count(*)` | `[[3]]` (3 edges created) | **`[[0]]`**: the MATCH became `MATCH (a:Z)` |
| `MATCH (a) RETURN a.v, [(a:A)-->(b) \| b.v] AS l` | `[[0,[]],[1,[0]],[5,[]]]` | **`[[1,[0]]]`**: the MATCH became `MATCH (a:A)` |

### Mechanism

* `bind_graph` extends `node_labels[(scope, id)]` with the labels of every occurrence (`graph/src/planner/binder.rs:1327-1331`).
* `update_all_node_labels` (`:122-154`) then replaces the labels of every MATCH node with that set.
* OPTIONAL MATCH (`:338`) and pattern predicates (`:2061`) clone `node_labels` before `bind_graph` and restore it after. CREATE (`bind_graph_create` → `bind_graph`, `:1645`) and pattern comprehensions (`:1847-1904`) do not.

### Expected

Match C: a label in CREATE is a label to create, and a label inside a pattern comprehension filters only the comprehension. Neither constrains the earlier MATCH.

### Suggested fix

Save and restore `node_labels` around the CREATE bind and around a pattern comprehension's `bind_graph`, as OPTIONAL MATCH and pattern predicates already do.

issues.title: [Rust] Collapsed (unread) named edge still takes part in relationship uniqueness, so the count depends on which parallel edge was picked
issues.body:
## Summary

`reduce_expand_into` collapses a named-but-unread edge to one row per (src, dst) pair and binds one representative edge. A sibling traverse in the same pattern still checks relationship uniqueness against that representative (`edge_already_used`). So the row count depends on *which* parallel edge was picked, and it matches neither C nor openCypher.

## Reproduction

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (a:N {id:1}), (b:N {id:2}), (c:N {id:3}), (a)-[:R {w:1}]->(b), (a)-[:R {w:2}]->(b), (b)-[:R {w:3}]->(c)"
```

| query | Rust `main` (2363723ac) | C |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (a)-[r]->(x)<-[s]-(c) RETURN count(*)` | **1** | 2 |
| `MATCH (a)-[r]->(x)<-[s]-(c) RETURN a.id, c.id` | **`1,1`** | `1,1` / `2,2` |
| `MATCH (a)-[r]->(x)<-[s]-(c) RETURN r.w, s.w` | `1,2` / `2,1` | 4 rows (C checks no uniqueness here) |

The `(b)->(c)` pair has one edge, `e3`. With `r` collapsed to `e3`, the traverse for `s` rejects `e3` as "already used", so the `(2,2)` row disappears. For `(a,b)`, one of the two parallel edges survives, whichever the representative isn't.

## Mechanism

- `planner/optimizer/reduce_expand_into.rs:118-143` sets `emit_relationship = false` for `r` and `s`, because no ancestor reads them.
- Both traverses keep each other in `sibling_edges` (`planner/mod.rs:1888`). The runtime check `ops/mod.rs:155 edge_already_used` compares against whatever edge the collapsed sibling bound.

PR #2918 (#2896) does not change this. Its `variable_read_outside` / `ir_references_variable` still ignore `sibling_edges`, so the same collapse happens on that branch.

## Expected

A collapsed edge stands for all of its parallel edges, so the uniqueness check cannot use its arbitrary representative. C semantics for unread edges is one row per endpoint pair with no uniqueness check against them. That gives 2 here, and `(1,1), (2,2)`.

## Suggested fix

When `reduce_expand_into` collapses an edge, drop it from every sibling list in the same scope. Only edges that are emitted per edge take part in uniqueness. An alternative is to keep a sibling-read edge un-collapsed (openCypher multiplicity). It costs the batched path, and on the query below it gives neither C's nor openCypher's count (per-edge `r` × per-pair `s`).

## Found by

Lean theorem `TwoHop.collapse_changes_count` (`twoHop_collapse_changes_count`), `proofs/ops_traverse` (W2-traverse-1).

issues.title: fix: bind only what the chain's leaf binds when select_scan_node keeps an outer child
issues.body:
Closes #3037

## Problem

`select_scan_node` seeded the chain's bound set with the best-scoring endpoint even when it keeps the bottom traverse's outer-context child. In that case no scan is built for that endpoint. The hops were then ordered, and the inline-attribute filters placed, as if it were bound:

```
CREATE (b:A), (d:D), (c {v:1}), (z:Z), (d)-[:X]->(b), (d)-[:R]->(c), (c)-[:R]->(z)
MATCH (b:A) WITH b LIMIT 1 MATCH (b)<-[]-(d)-[:R]->(c {v:1})-[:R]->(z) RETURN count(*)
-- main: 0   C: 1        (also WITH DISTINCT b; plain WITH b is fine)

Aggregate
    Conditional Traverse | (c)->(z)
        Conditional Traverse | (d)->(c)
            Filter                          <- c.v = 1, before c is bound
                Conditional Traverse | (b)<-(d)
                    Limit ...
```

## Fix

`initial_bound` is what the new chain's leaf actually binds. That is `{best_node}` when a scan is built for it, and otherwise the kept child's variables. If no hop can start from those, the existing "leave the chain alone" path applies. After the fix the filter lands above the hop that binds `c`:

```
Aggregate
    Conditional Traverse | (c)->(z)
        Filter
            Conditional Traverse | (d)->(c)
                Conditional Traverse | (b)<-(d)
                    Limit ...
```

This is related to #2972 (there the earlier clause's scan subtree is discarded), but it is a separate defect in the kept-child path.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_e2e.py::test_scan_below_outer_child_binds_only_what_the_child_binds`: the query with `WITH b`, `WITH b LIMIT 1`, `WITH b SKIP 0`, `WITH DISTINCT b` and `WITH b ORDER BY b`.
  - On `main` (release): **fails** at `WITH b LIMIT 1`, `[[0]] == [[1]]`.
  - With the fix: **passes**.
- Flow tests (RLTest on a private port): `test_optimizations_plan` 32/32, `test_traversal_construction` 16/16, `test_with_clause` 14/14.
- Run on the combined W2 fix build:
  - `cargo test --release -p graph`: 422 passed.
  - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 128 passed.
  - TCK (`tck_done.txt`): passed.
  - `test_call_subquery`, `test_optional_match`, `test_index_scans`: pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `CXX=clang++ cargo clippy --all-targets`: no warnings in touched code.

This change is in the optimizer only; the runtime is untouched.

Found by the Lean `ScanOrder` model (`proofs/optimizer_scan`, counterexample to `place_wellScoped`).

issues.title: fix: size HarmonicCentrality's source vector by the id bound
issues.body:
Closes #3044

## Problem

Unfiltered `algo.HarmonicCentrality` built its source vector with `g.node_count()` entries while the matrix has `node_count + deleted_nodes_count` rows. With `k` deleted nodes, the top `k` ids were never sources: they were missing from the output, and the scores / `reachable` counts that should include them were too small (chain 1->2->3->4 with node 0 deleted: node 4 missing, node 1 `reachable` 3 instead of 4).

## Fix

`graph/src/runtime/functions/algo_procedures.rs`: size the vector with `node_count + deleted_nodes_count`, as the matrix is. Deleted ids are already filtered from the output.

Sweep of the other procedures in the file: pageRank, WCC, betweenness and CDLP already use `node_count + deleted_nodes_count`; BFS runs on the full matrix; MSF and the compact paths size by the collected ids; maxFlow uses `max_node_id() + 1`. No other instance of the mistake.

## Tests

- New flow test `tests/flow/test_harmonic_centrality.py::test09_centrality_with_deleted_node` (expected values from the C module).
  - Before (module built from `main`): FAIL `[[1, 3], [2, 2], [3, 1]] == [[1, 4], [2, 3], [3, 2], [4, 1]]`.
  - After: `tests/flow/test_harmonic_centrality` 9/9 pass (RLTest on a private port).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `CXX=clang++ cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean for touched code.

issues.title: [Rust] algo.HarmonicCentrality skips the highest node ids after a delete (vector sized by node_count)
issues.body:
### Summary

After a node is deleted, unfiltered `algo.HarmonicCentrality` drops the node with the highest id from its results, and every score and `reachable` count that should include that node is too small.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 2363723ac)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0, 4) AS i CREATE (:A {id: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a:A), (b:A) WHERE b.id = a.id + 1 AND a.id > 0 CREATE (a)-[:R]->(b)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n:A {id: 0}) DELETE n"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CALL algo.HarmonicCentrality() YIELD node, reachable, score RETURN node.id, reachable, score ORDER BY node.id"
-- Rust: 1|3|1.5027  2|2|1.0015  3|1|0            (node 4 missing)
-- C:    1|4|1.8372  2|3|1.5027  3|2|1.0015  4|1|0
```

### Mechanism

`graph/src/runtime/functions/algo_procedures.rs:2777-2779` sizes the source vector with `g.node_count()`, while the unfiltered matrix has `node_count + deleted_nodes_count` rows (`:2755`). With `k` deleted nodes the top `k` ids are never sources.

A sweep of the other `algo.*` procedures in the file found no other place that sizes by `node_count()` alone: pageRank, WCC, betweenness and CDLP use `node_count + deleted_nodes_count`, BFS and MSF use the matrix or the collected ids, maxFlow uses `max_node_id() + 1`.

### Expected

Match C: every live node is a source and is reported.

### Suggested fix

Size the vector with `node_count + deleted_nodes_count` (the id bound), as the matrix is.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the algo procedures (`proofs/algo_udf`, theorem `Harmonic.unfiltered_drops_high_ids`); Rust repro `graph/tests/lean_algo_udf.rs::bug_harmonic_centrality_with_deleted_node`.

issues.title: fix: verbose reply prints top-level points and NaN as C does
issues.body:
Closes #3042

## Problem

Verbose replies printed a top-level point as `point({latitude: 1.000000, longitude: 2.000000})` (C: `point({latitude:1.000000, longitude:2.000000})`) and NaN inside lists, maps and vectors as `NaN` (C: `nan`).

issues.title: fix: a list slice bound that fails to parse is an error, not 0 / end of list
issues.body:
Closes #3036

## Problem

`parse_list_operator_expression` kept each slice bound's `Result` and turned *any* error into a missing bound (`0` for `from`, `i64::MAX` for `to`). So a slice whose bound failed to parse ran anyway and returned a wrong result:

| Query | `main` | This PR | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RETURN [1,2,3][abs()..2]` | `[1, 2]` | `Received 0 arguments to function 'abs', expected at least 1` | same |
| `RETURN [1,2,3][1..abs()]` | `[2, 3]` | arity error | same |
| `RETURN [1,2,3][1+..2]` | `[1, 2]` | syntax error | syntax error |
| `RETURN [1,2,3][(1..2]` | `[1, 2]` | syntax error | syntax error |
| `[..2]`, `[1..]`, `[..]` | ok | ok (unchanged) | ok |

## Fix

A bound is absent only when the token where it would start is `..` (for `from`) or `]` (for `to`). Otherwise the bound is parsed and its error propagates with `?`. The single-index form `[i]` takes the same path as before.

## Tests

- New unit test `parser::cypher::tests::slice_bound_errors_are_reported`. It checks that six malformed slices are rejected and that five valid ones (including all the omitted-bound forms) still parse.
  - Before the fix: `FAILED … accepted "RETURN [1,2,3][1+..2]"`.
  - After: `ok`.
- New e2e test `tests/test_e2e.py::test_list_range_bound_errors`. It fails against the `main` module (`AssertionError: Expected an error`) and passes with the fix.
- `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 126 passed.
- Flow tests (RLTest, release): `test_function_calls` 96/96, `test_query_validation` 50/50.
- `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except `batched_result_emitter::tests::cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, which already fails on macOS arm64 (#2922, unrelated). `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy --all-targets` are clean.

Merges cleanly with #2900, #2908, #2910 and #3019.

issues.title: [Rust] MERGE p=(a)-[:R]->(b) with a, b bound returns only the first of several parallel matches
issues.body:
### Summary

`MATCH (a:A),(b:B) MERGE p=(a)-[:R]->(b)` with two parallel `:R` edges returns one row, not two. When every node and every *named* relationship of the pattern is already bound, MERGE keeps only the first match. A path variable over an anonymous relationship still tells the matches apart.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 2363723ac)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (a:A),(b:B),(a)-[:R {k:1}]->(b),(a)-[:R {k:2}]->(b)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a:A),(b:B) MERGE p=(a)-[:R]->(b) RETURN count(p)"
Rust: 1
C:    2
```

### Mechanism

`MergeOp::next` (`graph/src/runtime/ops/merge.rs:368-400`) computes `all_vars_bound`: all nodes bound, and every relationship alias not starting with `_anon_` bound. In that case it emits only `matches[0]`. That is right when the output cannot tell the matches apart. A path variable (`p = ...`) binds the anonymous relationship, though, so every parallel edge is a distinct result row.

### Expected (C behaviour)

One row per match: `2`.

### Suggested fix

Don't take the shortcut when the MERGE pattern binds a path variable.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of MERGE (`proofs/ops_apply`), theorem `allBound_first_only`; Rust repro `graph/tests/lean_ops_apply.rs` (`bug_merge_all_bound_drops_path_matches`).

issues.title: [Rust] MERGE result depends on BATCH_SIZE: matching runs per input batch and sees earlier batches' creations
issues.body:
### Summary

The result of a MERGE depends on where the 1024-row batch boundaries fall. MERGE matches its pattern once per input **batch**. Rows in later batches therefore see what earlier batches created (after `ON CREATE SET`), while rows in the same batch do not. The same two rows create 2 nodes when they are adjacent and 1 node when they are 1024 rows apart.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 2363723ac)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1,2) AS x WITH x WHERE x = 1 OR x = 2
               MERGE (n:L {v: CASE x WHEN 1 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END}) ON CREATE SET n.v = 2"
Rust: Nodes created: 2       C: Nodes created: 2

GRAPH.QUERY g2 "UNWIND range(1,1025) AS x WITH x WHERE x = 1 OR x = 1025
                MERGE (n:L {v: CASE x WHEN 1 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END}) ON CREATE SET n.v = 2"
Rust: Nodes created: 1       C: Nodes created: 2
```

In the second query the first row creates `(:L {v:1})`, and `ON CREATE SET` turns it into `v:2`. The last row is in the next batch, so its match sub-plan runs afterwards and finds that node.

### Mechanism

`MergeOp::next` (`graph/src/runtime/ops/merge.rs:313-343`) pulls one input batch, runs the match sub-plan for that batch, then creates or updates row by row. Only then does it pull the next batch. Within a batch, only `merge_pattern_cache` stands in for earlier rows' creations. Across batches, the match sub-plan sees them directly, including their `ON CREATE`/`ON MATCH` updates.

### Expected (C behaviour)

C's `op_merge.c` is eager and batch-independent. It consumes the whole input, matches every row against the graph as it was before this MERGE created anything, and only then creates the rows that did not match. Rows that would create a duplicate are postponed and matched after the commit. Both queries create 2 nodes.

### Suggested fix

Make `MergeOp` eager like C: pull all input batches and run the match sub-plan for each of them before any create or `SET`, then create/update and emit. Batching of the match sub-plan stays. Only the interleaving of matching with creating changes, and the memory cost is holding the input rows, as C does.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of MERGE (`proofs/ops_apply`), theorems `batch_dependent`, `merge_noSet_any_batch_size`; Rust repro `graph/tests/lean_ops_apply.rs` (`bug_merge_result_depends_on_batch_boundary`).

issues.title: [Rust] MERGE's created-pattern cache is shared by all MERGE clauses: 'Variable b not found' / UNION branch aliases the other branch's node
issues.body:
### Summary

The MERGE "already created in this query" cache is shared by **every** MERGE clause of a query. A later MERGE whose pattern hashes the same as an earlier clause's (same labels and property map) reuses the earlier clause's cached bindings. Its own variable is then left unbound and the query is rolled back. In a UNION branch it silently aliases the other branch's node instead of creating its own.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 2363723ac)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "MERGE (a:M {v:1}) ON CREATE SET a.v = 2 MERGE (b:M {v:1}) RETURN a.v, b.v"
Rust: Variable b not found        (query rolled back, 0 nodes)
C:    2|1                         (2 nodes)

GRAPH.QUERY g "MERGE (a:U {v:1}) ON CREATE SET a.v = 2 RETURN a.v AS v UNION ALL MERGE (b:U {v:1}) RETURN b.v AS v"
Rust: 2, 2                        (1 node)
C:    2, 1                        (2 nodes)
```

### Mechanism

`Runtime::merge_pattern_cache` (`graph/src/runtime/runtime.rs:163`) is keyed only by the pattern hash from `compute_merge_pattern_hash`. That hash covers labels, property values and bound endpoints, but not which MERGE it came from. In `MergeOp::do_create_fallback` (`merge.rs:118-135`), the second clause finds no match in the graph (the first node now has `v = 2`), gets a cache hit on the first clause's entry, and inserts the cached `(variable id, value)` pairs. Those are the **first** clause's variable ids: `b` stays unbound ("Variable b not found"). In a UNION branch, where variable ids start again, `b` gets the first branch's node.

### Expected (C behaviour)

The dedup of created patterns is per MERGE operator (C keeps `unique_entities` per op). The second clause creates its own node: `2|1`, 2 nodes.

### Suggested fix

Key the cache by `(MergeOp plan idx, pattern hash)`.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of MERGE (`proofs/ops_apply`), theorems `cross_clause_unbound`, `per_clause_cache_fixes`; Rust repro `graph/tests/lean_ops_apply.rs` (`bug_merge_cache_shared_across_clauses`, `bug_merge_cache_shared_across_union_branches`).

issues.title: [Rust] select_scan_node treats the best endpoint as bound when it keeps an outer child, so an inline filter runs before its variable is bound (0 rows)
issues.body:
## Summary

When the bottom `CondTraverse` of a chain keeps an outer-context child (`WITH b LIMIT 1`, `WITH DISTINCT b`, `ORDER BY`, `SKIP`, ...), `select_scan_node` still treats the endpoint it scored best as bound, even though no scan is built for it. The hops are then ordered, and the inline-attribute filter placed, as if that variable were bound. In the plan below, `c`'s filter `{v: 1}` runs before `c` is bound, and every row is dropped.

## Reproduction

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (b:A), (d:D), (c {v:1}), (z:Z), (d)-[:X]->(b), (d)-[:R]->(c), (c)-[:R]->(z)"
```

| query | Rust `main` (2363723ac) | C |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (b:A) WITH b LIMIT 1 MATCH (b)<-[]-(d)-[:R]->(c {v:1})-[:R]->(z) RETURN count(*)` | **0** | 1 |
| same with `WITH DISTINCT b` | **0** | 1 |
| same with plain `WITH b` | 1 | 1 |

```
GRAPH.EXPLAIN g "MATCH (b:A) WITH b LIMIT 1 MATCH (b)<-[]-(d)-[:R]->(c {v:1})-[:R]->(z) RETURN count(*)"
Aggregate
    Conditional Traverse | (c)->(z)
        Conditional Traverse | (d)->(c)
            Filter                          <- c.v = 1, but c is bound only by the hop above
                Conditional Traverse | (b)<-(d)
                    Limit
                        Project
                            Node By Label Scan | (b:A)
```

## Mechanism

`graph/src/planner/optimizer/select_scan_node.rs:893-900`:

```rust
let initial_bound: HashSet<u32> = {
    let mut b = HashSet::new();
    b.insert(best_node.alias.id);            // even when no scan is built for it
    if let Some(child) = &existing_child {
        b.extend(collect_subtree_variables(&child.root()));
    }
    b
};
```

`best_node` is `c` (filtered). `bound_vars` comes from `collect_output_aliases(child)`, which sees nothing through `Limit`, so `b` does not score as bound. With `existing_child` kept, `make_scan_subtree(&best_node, ..)` is never built (`:1080`), yet `placed_bound` starts with `c`, so the inline filter on `c` is placed right after the first hop. A plain `WITH b` works because the child is then a `Project`, whose outputs count as bound.

Related to, but distinct from, #2972. In that bug the earlier clause's scan subtree is thrown away. Here the child is kept, but the bound set is wrong.

## Expected

`1`, as C returns. Only what the chain's leaf actually binds counts as bound.

## Suggested fix

Seed `initial_bound` with `best_node` only when a scan is built for it (`existing_child` is `None`). Otherwise seed it with the kept child's variables. If no hop can then start from what is bound, the existing "leave the chain alone" path applies.

## Found by

Lean `ScanOrder` counterexample to `place_wellScoped`, `proofs/optimizer_scan` (W2-scan-1). The repro was found by that model's oracle fuzz (1 Rust-only mismatch in 480 queries).

issues.title: [Rust] A list slice bound that fails to parse is silently read as 0 / end of list ([1,2,3][abs()..2] returns [1, 2])
issues.body:
### Summary

A list slice bound that fails to parse is silently replaced by `0` (for `from`) or `i64::MAX` (for `to`), so an invalid slice runs and returns a wrong result instead of an error. C reports the error.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ 55204c94b)

| Query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `RETURN [1,2,3][abs()..2]` | `[1, 2]` | `Received 0 arguments to function 'abs', expected at least 1` |
| `RETURN [1,2,3][1..abs()]` | `[2, 3]` | same arity error |
| `RETURN [1,2,3][1+..2]` | `[1, 2]` | `Invalid input '.': expected NOT, '+', '-', …` |
| `RETURN [1,2,3][(1..2]` | `[1, 2]` | `Invalid input '.': expected a property name` |

Leaving out a bound on purpose (`[..2]`, `[1..]`, `[..]`) works on both engines and must keep working.

### Mechanism

`parse_list_operator_expression` (`graph/src/parser/cypher.rs:2123-2131`) calls `parse_expr` for each bound and keeps the `Result`. Then `from.unwrap_or_else(|_| 0)` / `to.unwrap_or_else(|_| i64::MAX)` treats *any* parse error as "bound left out". The error is dropped, and the lexer resumes from wherever the failed parse left it.

### Expected

A bound is missing only when `..` or `]` comes where the bound would start. Otherwise the bound is parsed and its error is returned, as in C.

### Suggested fix

Check the current token (`DotDot` before `from`, `RBrace` before `to`) to decide whether the bound is present, and propagate `parse_expr`'s error with `?`.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the parser (`proofs/parser_grammar`, theorem `slice_bound_error_swallowed`). Rust repro: `graph/tests/lean_parser_grammar.rs::bug_slice_bound_error_is_swallowed`.

issues.title: fix: keep outer rows apart in a hash join under a batched sub-plan (#3012)
issues.body:
Closes #3012

## Problem

A batched Apply, Optional or Merge hands its sub-plan one argument batch that holds every outer row, each tagged with its `origin_row`. `ValueHashJoinOp` built one table over the right side's rows of *all* origins and probed it with every left row, so rows of different outer rows joined:

```
UNWIND [1,2] AS i CREATE (:A {v:1, w:i}), (:B {v:1, w:i})
UNWIND [1,2] AS x MATCH (a:A),(b:B) WHERE a.v = b.v RETURN count(*)          Rust main 16, C 8
UNWIND [1,2] AS x OPTIONAL MATCH (a:A),(b:B)
  WHERE a.v = b.v AND a.w = x AND b.w = x RETURN x, a.w, b.w                  Rust main: each row twice
UNWIND range(1,3000) AS x MATCH (a:C {w:x}),(b:C) WHERE b.v = a.v AND b.w <= 20
  RETURN count(*)                                                            Rust main 6006912, C 6000
```

## Fix

The issue offered two options: add `IR::ValueHashJoin` to the `can_batch` blacklists, which forces per-row mode, or make the join origin-aware. This PR makes the join origin-aware, so the sub-plan stays batched:

- `set_argument_batch` sets `per_origin` when the argument batch holds more than one row.
- The build then keeps one `JoinHashTable` per origin, each with its own int/value promotion. The probe looks only in the table of the left row's `origin_row`.
- Top-level joins never receive a multi-row argument batch. They keep a single table, and their code path is unchanged apart from indexing table 0.

## Tests

- New flow test `test_hashjoin:testHashJoin.test_join_inside_batched_subplan_keeps_outer_rows_apart` covers Apply, OPTIONAL MATCH, and an outer input of more than one batch. Expected values checked against the C module.
  - Before (`main` @ 2363723ac): FAIL, `[[16]] == [[8]]`, duplicated optional rows, and `[[6006912]] == [[6000]]`.
  - After, all with RLTest/pytest on private ports: `tests/flow/test_hashjoin` 5/5, `tests/flow/test_optional_match` 26/26, `tests/test_e2e.py` 90/90, and `cargo test -p graph --lib value_hash_join` 5/5.
- Bench (release, alternating runs, load avg ~45–55). Graph: `UNWIND range(1,20000) AS i CREATE (:L {k: i % 1000, w: i}), (:R {k: i % 1000})`.

| query | A p50 / p99 | B p50 / p99 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| top-level join `MATCH (l:L), (r:R) WHERE l.k = r.k AND l.w <= 2000 RETURN count(*)`, main vs PR (30 runs) | main 6.53 / 7.56 ms | PR 6.64 / 7.45 ms |
| same, order swapped | PR 6.58 / 7.18 ms | main 6.48 / 7.36 ms |
