pulls.title: feat(replication): load replica full syncs straight off the socket (diskless load)
pulls.body: Closes #3309. Covers the short-read half of #3177. The malformed-payload half is still open: #3309 has the gap analysis, made by running #3141's own tests against Rust. ## What changes A replica with `repl-diskless-load on-empty-db` or `swapdb` now decodes the primary's RDB straight from the socket. Before, Redis refused (`Skipping diskless-load because there are modules that don't handle read errors`) and wrote the payload to disk first. On this machine, full syncs are **21–23% faster**, with the same peak memory. Numbers are below. ### Turning it on - `module_init.rs`: declare `HANDLE_IO_ERRORS | HANDLE_REPL_ASYNC_LOAD`, and subscribe to `REDISMODULE_EVENT_REPL_ASYNC_LOAD`. - Reading needed no change. Every RDB read goes through redismodule-rs's `raw::load_*`, which checks `RedisModule_IsIOError` after each read and returns `Err`. ### `on-empty-db`: a failed load must leave nothing behind - `on_loading(LOADING_FAILED)` now **discards** half-decoded multi-key graphs (`discard_pending_graphs`) instead of finalizing them. - Every load start (`RDB`, `AOF` or `REPL`) clears `DECODE_STATE`. - Before: the replica's retry merged into the stale leftovers and diverged silently, while still reporting `Finished with success`. - `graph_aux_load` / `graphmeta_aux_load` (`AFTER_RDB`) now fail the load on a short read. Before, they ignored it and finalized what had arrived. ### `swapdb`: don't touch live state until Redis swaps Redis loads into a temporary database and keeps the live one in service. With `async_loading` it keeps answering clients from inside the decode. - `redis_type.rs` adds a `SwapLoad` state: - **`STARTED`**: graphs that `graph_rdb_load` registers, and the UDFs `graph_aux_load` validates, are staged instead of replacing the live ones. - **`COMPLETED`**, fired right after the swap: the staged graphs replace `GRAPH_REGISTRY` wholesale, so names the old snapshot had and the new one doesn't are dropped too, and the staged UDFs are installed. - **`ABORTED`**: the staged state and `DECODE_STATE` are dropped. The `LOADING_FAILED` that follows skips the virtual-key cleanup, because the live database still holds the previous snapshot. - `UdfRepo::deserialize` is split into `stage` (validate) and `install`, so validation still happens at aux time and a bad library still fails the load. - `dispatch::must_run_inline` adds `ASYNC_LOADING`. Redis reports it *instead of* `LOADING`, and only delivers a blocked client's reply from the main loop. Before, every query sent during an async load hung until the load ended. Now reads are served throughout, from the previous snapshot. - `GRAPH.DEBUG AUX` is refused while async loading. Running inside the decode, it would deadlock on `DECODE_STATE`. ### Separate bug fixed: `GRAPH.DEBUG AUX END` left `VKEY_STATE` set `AUX START` creates virtual keys through `create_virtual_keys`. `AUX END` deleted them but left `VKEY_STATE` behind. Every later save then wrote a multi-key header naming keys that no longer existed, and the loader kept an empty placeholder. Reproduced on `main` with a plain disk-based replica: 100 nodes on the primary, 0 on the replica. `AUX END` now also calls `delete_virtual_keys`, the way a finished `SAVE` does. ## Tests `tests/flow/test_diskless_replication.py`: | Test | What it checks | |---|---| | `test01_full_sync_loads_from_socket` | `on-empty-db` loads from the socket (`EOF to parser`, no `Skipping`) and matches the primary | | `test02_aborted_multi_key_load_is_discarded` | link cut partway through a multi-key graph; after the retry the replica matches the primary | | `test03_swapdb_replaces_graphs_and_udfs` | graphs changed, added and removed, and the UDF replaced, all applied by the swap | | `test04_swapdb_aborted_load_keeps_live_data` | after an aborted load the live graphs and UDFs are unchanged, and once promoted the replica can write to **every** graph | | `test05_async_load_serves_previous_snapshot` | full sync that keeps the replication id (backlog overflow inside `MULTI`); every sample taken while `async_loading:1` shows the old snapshot, and the end state shows the new one | Each test fails without the change that makes it pass: | Build | Result | |---|---| | `main` | test01–02 fail: `Skipping diskless-load` (test03–05 were added later and not run on `main`) | | `HANDLE_IO_ERRORS` only, no failure cleanup | test02 fails: replica has property sum 1812450 instead of 2001000, and 1610/2000 edges | | `on-empty-db` complete, no `HANDLE_REPL_ASYNC_LOAD` | test03–05 fail: `Skipping diskless-load` (Redis requires it for `swapdb`) | | no `swapdb` staging | test04 fails (UDF from the aborted load, and `graph was deleted or replaced…` on writes); test05 fails (new UDF visible mid-load) | | no `ASYNC_LOADING` inline routing | test05 fails: `replica never async loaded` (queries blocked until the load ended) | | this PR | 5/5, release (4 runs) and debug | Also run: 13 neighbouring flow files (replication, replication states, RDB load, C-layout RDB, persistence, AOF, encode/decode, copy, UDF, divergence report, role-change and pause races): **119/119** pass. `cargo fmt --check` is clean, and clippy reports the same warnings as `main`. ### CI routing The test reconfigures replication for the whole server, so it can't share the services container. I added an explicit spawn opt-in: - `test_matrix_split.py` routes any file with a `# flow-matrix: spawn` line to the spawn bucket (now 10 files, up from 9); - `Env()` exposes `replica_log_path` in local, services (`None`) and spawn mode. Spawn mode used to drop the replica's log path. I couldn't run spawn mode locally (no Docker daemon), so the first CI run is the first real test of that path. ## Measurements Full-sync time on the replica, from `REPLICAOF` until `master_link_status:up` and `loading:0`. Median of 5 runs. Apple M3 Pro, local NVMe, loopback, Redis 8.6.2. The primary uses `repl-diskless-sync yes` with delay 0. Graph: N × `(:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(:City)`, 7 properties, range index. | Graph | RDB | disk (`disabled`) | `main` + `on-empty-db` | this PR, `on-empty-db` | `swapdb` empty | `swapdb` populated | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2M nodes | 92 MB | 1.89 s | — | **1.46 s** | 1.44 s | 1.43 s | | 8M nodes | 356 MB | 7.38 s | 7.54 s (fell back to disk) | **5.85 s** | 5.85 s | 5.99 s | - Decode time is identical in every mode (5.83 s at 8M nodes). Diskless removes the separate transfer-to-file phase (1.53 s here) by overlapping it with decoding. Over a real network the saving is up to `min(transfer, decode)`. - The disk path had two 10 s outliers in 5 runs at 2M nodes. The diskless runs stayed within ±0.03 s. - Peak replica RSS is unchanged (0.73 / 2.8 GB). `swapdb` into a populated replica holds both copies until the swap (1.23 / 4.8 GB), as `swapdb` always does. ## Reviewer notes - `GRAPH_REGISTRY` is replaced as a whole on `COMPLETED`. `graph_free` then runs (possibly on Redis's lazyfree thread) for the old database's values. It unregisters by `data_ptr` and finds nothing, which is correct. - C declares `HANDLE_IO_ERRORS` (#3141) but not `HANDLE_REPL_ASYNC_LOAD`. So `swapdb` is a Rust-only improvement, and C still falls back to disk there. - While a `swapdb` load runs, queries run inline from inside the decode: they read the live graphs, and the decoder holds `DECODE_STATE` across its reads. No query path takes `DECODE_STATE`; `GRAPH.DEBUG AUX` is the only command that does, and it is now refused there. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Replica full syncs now decode the primary's RDB straight off the socket instead of spooling it to disk first, cutting full-sync time roughly 21–23% with the same peak memory. A replica with `repl-diskless-load on-empty-db` or `swapdb` previously fell back to disk because the module didn't declare it could handle read errors. **`on-empty-db`** - A load that fails mid-stream discards the multi-key graphs it half decoded; before, the retry merged into the stale leftovers and the replica diverged silently. - Aux loads now fail on a short read instead of finalizing what had arrived, and every load starts from an empty decode state. **`swapdb`** - Graphs and UDFs are staged in the temporary database and replace the live ones only when Redis swaps it in; an aborted load leaves the live data untouched. - Queries issued during an async load are served from the previous snapshot; before, they hung until the load ended. - `GRAPH.DEBUG AUX` is refused during async loading — it would deadlock. Also fixes `GRAPH.DEBUG AUX END` leaving virtual-key state set, so later saves encoded a multi-key header naming keys that no longer existed. Written for commit 0a1ecfa6bac20e6eb2062de7fd29a4cb02dc7a26. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved replica behavior during diskless synchronization. Existing graph data remains available while a replacement snapshot loads, and incomplete or aborted loads no longer replace live data. * Successful database swaps now replace graphs and user-defined functions together, helping keep replica state consistent. * `GRAPH.DEBUG AUX` actions now return an error while Redis is loading asynchronously, rather than running during that period.

pulls.title: perf(index): apply native-index writes once per unit of work
pulls.body: Closes #3306 The native index is now updated once per unit of work instead of once per graph write call. ## One index update per unit of work The graph's write paths no longer change the native index themselves. Each records its changes in a `PendingIndexWrites` buffer carried in the unit of work's `IndexDocs`, the struct that already holds its RediSearch documents. The owner applies it once: - a Cypher query at the end of each `Commit` segment (`Pending::commit`), so a later operator in the same query reads the writes, as it does through RediSearch; - a replicated effects buffer once per buffer (`effects::v3::apply`); - `GRAPH.BULK` once per token. The 14 graph write methods take `&mut IndexDocs` in place of the single RediSearch map they took, and fill the same map as before plus, with the `index-falkordb` feature, `docs.native`. The write functions in `graph_writes` take `&Graph` and the buffer. `PendingIndexWrites` and its module exist only with the feature, and `PendingIndexWrites::apply` takes the `FalkorDbIndex`. `IndexDocs` moves from `runtime::pending` to `index::index_docs` and is re-exported from `runtime::pending`. The buffer keeps changes in the order they were made and applies only the last change to each `(value, id)`, because one write step can add an entry and then remove it: `SET n.v = 5 DELETE n` stages the SET's add before the DELETE's remove. `FalkorDbIndex::merge` is replaced by `apply_writes`. --- ## Summary by cubic The native index is now updated once per unit of work instead of once per graph write call. Graph write paths no longer touch the native index. The `graph_writes` helpers take `&Graph` and return the `IndexChanges` one write makes, encoded and in order; the graph's write methods stage them into a `PendingIndexWrites` buffer carried by the unit of work's `IndexDocs`, which now lives in `index::index_docs` and is re-exported from `runtime::pending`. Owners apply the buffer through `Graph::apply_index_writes` (which calls `FalkorDbIndex::apply`): a Cypher query at the end of each `Commit` segment, a replicated effects buffer once per buffer, and `GRAPH.BULK` once per token. `GRAPH.BULK` and the replica publish both index kinds at once through `Graph::commit_index_docs`, replacing the old `BulkIndexDocs` wrapper. `PendingIndexWrites` is plain data (`extend`, `drain`, `clear`, `is_empty`); the index digests it. **Last change per tuple wins** Batching removes the per-call removes-then-adds ordering. `SET n.v = 5 DELETE n` stages `add (5, n)` then `remove (5, n)` in one batch, so the buffer collapses each `(value, id)` to its final change before a single batched remove and add per column, keeping the deleted node out of the index. Written for commit cf878b9dd73e518717dd18a66f2126dcdd2b6bfc. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved index consistency when graph changes are combined in a single operation, including updates followed by deletions. * Updated node and relationship indexes after attribute changes, label changes, deletions, and bulk imports. * Preserved unaffected indexed records when applying batches of graph changes.

pulls.title: fix: run long clause chains (5000 UNWINDs, 1000 OPTIONAL MATCHes) instead of overflowing the stack
pulls.body: Closes #3304 ## Problem Each clause puts its operator on top of the previous clause's, so a long query produces a tall plan. Four places recurse once per plan level: the optimizer passes, the runtime's operator build, every `next()` pull, and the operator tree's drop. On a 2 MiB pool worker, 2000 chained `UNWIND`s crashed the server with a SIGSEGV, and so did about 285 `OPTIONAL MATCH ... WHERE` or `CALL {}` clauses. C runs these queries. Parsing, binding and planning were fine up to 100 000 clauses. ## Fix - New `planner::with_plan_stack(plan, f)`. If the plan is tall, it runs `f` on a stack segment sized from the plan's height: 16 KiB per level, about twice the costliest level measured, plus 1 MiB. It uses `stacker::grow`, which stays on the same thread, so thread-locals, the Redis context, the GIL state and inline (MULTI) execution are unaffected. The segment is address space only: it is mapped for the call and unmapped after it, and only the pages the query touches get committed. - It wraps the two recursive stages: `optimize` in `Graph::get_plan` (both the cached and the uncached path), and `Runtime::query`, which builds, pulls and drops the operator tree. That covers GRAPH.QUERY / RO_QUERY / PROFILE / RECORD and EXPLAIN. - Shallow queries pay one O(1) `plan.len() <= 128` check. 128 levels of the costliest kind fit easily in the existing 2 MiB worker stack. - As a last resort, `Planner::check_depth` rejects plans taller than 10 000 levels, twice C's 5000 `UNWIND`s, with the existing `Query nesting exceeds the maximum depth of …` error, so a pathological query cannot ask for an unbounded stack. - New dependency: `stacker` (with `psm`), the crate rustc uses for the same purpose. Clause counts per shape: `main` crash point (bisected), and whether each count runs. "Rust after" was run on both the pool and inline (MULTI): | Shape (per clause) | count | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---|---| | `UNWIND [1] AS xN` | 5000 | crash (~1600) | ok, 0.74 s | ok, 33 s | | `WITH xN AS xN+1` | 2000 | crash (~1600) | ok, 0.07 s | ok | | `WITH xN AS xN+1, count(*) AS cN` | 2000 | crash (~800) | ok, 0.07 s | ok, 0.07 s | | `OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-->(bN)` | 1000 | crash (~460) | ok, 0.12 s | ok, 80 s | | `OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-->(bN) WHERE bN.v > 0` | 1000 | crash (~285) | ok, 0.35 s | - | | `CALL { WITH xN RETURN xN + 1 AS xN+1 }` | 1000 | crash (~285) | ok, 0.11 s | - | | `MERGE (aN:M {k: ..})` | 1000 | crash (~370) | ok, 0.27 s | - | | `FOREACH (x IN [1] \| SET a.fN = x)` | 1000 | crash (~400) | ok, 0.20 s | - | | `WITH ... ORDER BY ... SKIP 0 LIMIT 5` | 1000 | crash (~380) | ok, 0.26 s | - | | `SET a.vN = N WITH a` | 1000 | crash (<500) | ok, 0.33 s | - | | `UNWIND` ×10 001 | | crash | `Query nesting exceeds the maximum depth of 10000` | - | Every shape also runs at the cap: 9 999 `UNWIND`s take 2.9 s, and 9 990 `OPTIONAL MATCH ... WHERE` take 32 s, most of it in the optimizer. GRAPH.EXPLAIN of 9 999 `UNWIND`s and GRAPH.PROFILE of 5 000 work. JS UDFs called inside a deep plan behave as on `main`, and QuickJS's own stack limit still fires. **Latency** (shallow queries, p50 / p99 in µs over 3 rounds, `main` vs this PR): | Query | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | cached 1-hop with params (20k) | 215-216 / 257-263 | 215-218 / 262-264 | | cached aggregate (5k) | 251-260 / 308-320 | 251-263 / 292-300 | | uncached 1-hop (10k distinct) | 214-216 / 263-281 | 213-216 / 260-266 | | 40-clause WITH chain (10k) | 244-250 / 293-311 | 239-250 / 292-300 | **Memory** (RSS, KB): | | idle | after 2000 shallow queries | after 10× 300-clause `OPTIONAL MATCH ... WHERE` | |---|---|---|---| | main | 22 352 | 32 256 | crashed | | this PR | 22 464 | 32 256 | 120 096 | | C | 19 344 | 28 704 | 163 232 | Worker stacks are unchanged (2 MiB), and VSZ at idle is identical to `main`. ## Tests - New `tests/test_e2e.py::test_long_clause_chains_run`: 2000 `UNWIND`s, 400 `OPTIONAL MATCH ... WHERE`, 400 `CALL {}`, and 10 001 `UNWIND`s rejected with the server still up. Against the `main` module it fails (`ConnectionError: Connection closed by server`). With this PR it passes. - The full flow suite (`flow_tests_done.txt`, 126 files) passes. - `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py tests/test_mvcc.py tests/test_concurrency.py`: 146 passed. The TCK done list passes. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: everything passes except `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, which already fails on macOS (#2922). `cargo fmt --check` is clean, and clippy reports nothing in touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes server crashes on long clause chains: the optimizer, runtime operator build, `next()` pulls, and operator tree drops each recurse once per plan level, so 2000 chained `UNWIND`s or ~285 `OPTIONAL MATCH ... WHERE` / `CALL {}` clauses overflowed a 2 MiB worker stack and SIGSEGV'd the server. - Runs the recursive optimizer and runtime stages on a stack segment sized from the plan's height (16 KiB per level plus 1 MiB) using `stacker`, on the same thread, so thread-locals and the Redis context stay valid. - Plans with 128 levels or fewer, nearly every query, pay one O(1) length check. - Added a 10,000-level cap that returns the existing `Query nesting exceeds the maximum depth of 10000` error instead of crashing. Written for commit 9ff2395e7c98503962899c3ed156293355eea183. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Improvements** * Long queries with extensive chains of clauses can now complete more reliably, including queries with thousands of `UNWIND` clauses and deeply nested operations. * Queries that exceed the supported plan depth now return a clear maximum-depth error. The server remains responsive after such a query.

pulls.title: fix: name unnamed pattern entities @anon_N so a query variable can't collide with them
pulls.body: Closes #3302 ## Problem Unnamed nodes and relationships were named `_anon_`, which is a plain identifier a query can write. A user variable `_anon_0` and the unnamed `(:B)` in `MATCH (_anon_0:A), (:B)` became one node. About 15 `starts_with("_anon")` checks in the binder, planner, optimizer and runtime also treated any variable starting with `_anon` as anonymous. For example, `count(_anonymous)` got a fresh variable instead of the one `MATCH` bound. ## Fix - `parser::ast` gets `ANON_PREFIX = "@anon_"` (C's spelling) and `is_anon()`. The parser builds names from the prefix, and every `starts_with("_anon")` check is now `is_anon(..)`. An unquoted identifier cannot start with `@`, so a query can only collide by backquoting the name, which is also true in C. - `RETURN *` used to skip `_`-prefixed names, which covered the old anonymous prefix. It now also skips `is_anon` names, so its output is unchanged. - `EXPLAIN` shows `@anon_N` where it showed `_anon_N`, as C does. The one flow assertion that quoted the old name is updated. | Query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (_anon_0:A), (:B) RETURN count(*)` | 0 | 1 | 1 | | `MATCH (_anonymous:A) RETURN count(_anonymous)` | 0 | 1 | 1 | | `GRAPH.EXPLAIN ... (n)-->()` | `(n)->(_anon_1)` | `(n)->(@anon_1)` | `(n)->(@anon_0)` | Not in this PR: the other internal names (`_slot_`, `_lc_`, `_quant_`, ...) are still writable. `RETURN *` still drops user variables that start with `_`, so `MATCH (_x:A) RETURN *` errors where C returns `_x`. The issue lists this separately. ## Tests - New `tests/test_e2e.py::test_variable_named_like_an_anonymous_entity`: against the `main` module it fails with `assert [[0]] == [[2]]`. With this PR it passes. The expected values were checked against C. - The full flow suite (`flow_tests_done.txt`, 126 files) passes with this PR. `test_execution_plan_print` now expects `@anon_0`. - `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py tests/test_mvcc.py`: 136 passed. The TCK done list passes. Before the `RETURN *` adjustment it caught Match4 [5] listing the anonymous var-len edge. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: everything passes except `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, which already fails on macOS (#2922). `cargo fmt --check` is clean, and clippy reports nothing in touched code. - No hot-path change: each `is_anon` is the same single prefix compare as before, made at plan or op-construction time. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes variable collisions with unnamed pattern entities by renaming them from `_anon_N` to `@anon_N`. - The old `_anon_` prefix was a valid identifier, so `MATCH (_anon_0:A), (:B)` treated both nodes as the same, and any user variable starting with `_anon` was handled as anonymous. - Unnamed nodes and relationships now use C's `@anon_N`, which can only be written by backquoting. All internal `starts_with("_anon")` checks now use the shared `is_anon()` helper. - `EXPLAIN` output now shows `@anon_N` where it showed `_anon_N`. - Adds a test covering queries using `_anon_`-like user variables. Written for commit 0dc8ba5b22b8598b635e50c7301e47704e5df152. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Variables beginning with `_anon` are now treated as regular named variables, preserving expected matching and query results. * Anonymous entities are consistently identified across query planning and execution, improving handling of variable-length traversals and relationship patterns. * Execution plan output now uses a distinct label for anonymous relationships.

pulls.title: fix: word GRAPH.BULK and point() errors the way C does
pulls.body: Closes #3275 ## Problem - `GRAPH.BULK` replied `N nodes created, M relations created`. C replies `... M edges created`. - `point()` had two implementations with their own error messages: `point_struct_pure`, used when the binder rewrites a literal map into positional slots, and the map path. The same map got a different error depending on whether it was written in the call or passed in as a value, and neither matched C. The rewrite fills a missing key with `null`, so the struct path could not tell "missing" from "null". Neither path checked the key count (`{latitude:1, longitude:2, x:3}` returned a point), and the range was checked after narrowing to `f32`, so `90.0000001` passed. ## Fix - Bulk reply text: `edges created`. - One helper, `point_from_map_entries`, serves both paths and applies C's checks in C's order: key count == 2, `latitude` and `longitude` present, both numeric, then the range on the `f64` values. A NaN is still refused (C lets it through), with the old message. - `Functions::set_required_struct_fn` marks a struct constructor whose map must carry every slot. `rewrite_struct_constructor` leaves such a call on the general path when a slot is missing. `point` uses it; the temporal constructors keep the optional-slot behaviour. A literal map with both keys still takes the positional fast path. - `Point::validate` had no other caller and is removed. | Input | `main` (literal / value) | This PR (both) | C (both) | |---|---|---|---| | `GRAPH.BULK bg BEGIN 0 0 0 0` | `0 nodes created, 0 relations created` | `0 nodes created, 0 edges created` | same as PR | | `point({latitude:null, longitude:1})` | `point() requires 'latitude' field` / `Type mismatch: 'latitude' must be a number, got Null` | `'latitude' and 'longitude' values in point map were not both valid numerics` | same as PR | | `point({latitude:1})`, `point({})` | `point() requires '…' field` | `A point map should have 2 elements, latitude and longitude` | same as PR | | `point({latitude:1, longitude:2, x:3})` | returns a point | `A point map should have 2 elements, latitude and longitude` | same as PR | | `point({Latitude:1, longitude:2})` | `point() requires 'latitude' field` | `Did not find 'latitude' value in point map` | same as PR | | `point({latitude:90.0000001, longitude:2})` | returns a point | `latitude should be within the -90 to 90 range` | same as PR | | `point({latitude:1, longitude:200})` | `longitude should be within the range -180.0 to 180.0, got 200` | `longitude should be within the -180 to 180 range` | same as PR | Behaviour change: a point map with extra keys is now refused, as C refuses it. ## Tests - New flow test `test_point.testPath.test_point_map_errors`: 9 maps × {literal, value}, exact error text. - C module: pass. `main`: 18 mismatches (e.g. `"point() requires 'latitude' field" == "'latitude' and 'longitude' values in point map were not both valid numerics"`). This PR: pass. - `test_bulk_insertion.py:994` now expects `1 edges created`. `main`: `'1 nodes created, 1 relations created' should contain '1 edges created'` FAIL. This PR: 14/14. - Flow (RLTest, release): `test_point` 6/6, `test_bulk_insertion` 14/14, `test_function_calls` 98/98, `test_effects_shapes` 22/22, `test_filters` 9/9, `test_constraint` 26/26. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 495 passed, 1 failed (`cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, pre-existing on macOS, #2922). `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. TCK temporal subset passes. `cargo fmt --check` clean; `clippy --all-targets` has no warnings in touched code. The other wording difference seen here (`CREATE INDEX` on a new label reporting `Labels added: 1`) has the same cause as #2655 and is noted there, not changed here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `GRAPH.BULK` and `point()` reply wording and validation to match the C implementation. - `GRAPH.BULK` now replies `N nodes created, M edges created` instead of `N relations created`. - `point()` now goes through one helper for both literal maps and map values, applying C's checks in C's order: exactly two keys, both present, both numeric, then the range checked on the `f64` value before narrowing to `f32`. - The positional-slot rewrite now only applies when a literal map has both keys, so a missing key is reported as missing rather than as `null`. - Behavior change: a point map with extra keys (e.g. `{latitude: 1, longitude: 2, x: 3}`) is now rejected, matching C. Written for commit f96ea3d3505abd22d382ddbe37c54184dda452f7. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: reject SET (n.x) = 5, SET/REMOVE (n):L and [:A:B] like C
pulls.body: Closes #3299 ## Problem The parser accepted, and ran, shapes that C rejects as syntax errors: - a parenthesized `SET`/`REMOVE` target that does not open a property lookup: `SET (n.x) = 5` set `n.x`, `SET (n) = {..}` replaced the map, and `SET (n):L` / `REMOVE (n):L` changed labels; - relationship types joined by a bare `:`: `[:A:B]` was read as `[:A|B]`. The same happened inside `shortestPath(...)`. ## Fix - `parse_set_items` and `parse_remove_items` call a new `expect_property_after_paren` after the `)` of a parenthesized target. Only `(expr).prop...` gets through. - A new `parse_relationship_types` replaces the two copies of the type loop (patterns and `shortestPath`). It joins alternatives only with `|`, keeping the legacy `|:` spelling. | Query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (n) SET (n.x) = 5` | sets `n.x = 5` | `Invalid input '=': expected '.'` | `Invalid input '=': expected '.'` | | `MATCH (n) SET (n) = {a:1}` | replaces the map | `Invalid input '=': expected '.'` | `Invalid input '=': expected '<', '-' or '.'` | | `MATCH (n) SET (n):L` / `REMOVE (n):L` | adds / removes label | `Invalid input ':': expected '.'` | `Invalid input ':': expected '<', '-' or '.'` | | `MATCH ()-[:A:B]->() RETURN 1` | runs as `[:A\|B]` | `Invalid input ':': expected '}'` | `Invalid input ':': expected '\|', '*', '{', a parameter or ']'` | | `shortestPath((a)-[:A:B*]->(b))` | runs | `Invalid input ':'` | `Invalid input ':'` | | `SET (n).x = 6`, `REMOVE (n).x`, `[:A\|B]`, `[:A\|:B]` | ok | ok | ok | (The `expected '}'` wording for a bad token before `]` is the existing message from `match_token!(RBrace)`. This PR doesn't change it.) Note: #2900 also edits the head of `parse_set_items` / `parse_remove_items`, moving it into `parse_update_target`. Whichever lands second has a one-line conflict: the `expect_property_after_paren()?` call goes after the `RParen` match in that helper. ## Tests - `parser::cypher::tests::paren_update_targets_and_colon_joined_types_are_rejected`: 9 rejected and 8 accepted shapes. Against the `main` parser it fails with `accepted "MATCH (n) SET (n.x) = 5"`. With this PR it passes. - Flow `test_query_validation::test52_paren_update_targets_and_colon_joined_types`: on the `main` module it fails (all 6 shapes run, and `n.x` is overwritten). With this PR, 52/52 pass. - Also green with this PR: test_all_shortest_paths 7/7, test_entity_update 44/44, test_label_update 6/6, test_multi_label 12/12, test_relation_patterns 13/13, test_shortest_path 7/7, test_traversal_construction 16/16, test_varlength_traversal 9/9, test_graph_merge 38/38. The TCK done list passes. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 496 passed. The one failure is `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, which already fails on macOS (#2922). - `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. - `cargo fmt --check` is clean, and clippy reports nothing in touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Rejects query shapes the parser previously accepted and ran, matching C's syntax. Parenthesized `SET`/`REMOVE` targets now have to open a property lookup: `SET (n.x) = 5`, `SET (n) = {..}`, and `SET (n):L` / `REMOVE (n):L` are syntax errors instead of writes. Relationship types are parsed by a helper shared between patterns and `shortestPath` that joins alternatives only with `|` (optionally `|:`), so `[:A:B]` is rejected rather than read as `[:A|B]`. Valid spellings — `SET (n).x = 5`, `REMOVE (n).x`, `[:A|B]`, `[:A|:B]` — behave unchanged. Written for commit f8ff5fe9355ca06ec3d3a37cdc23423bb349d14f. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Query Validation** * Relationship-type alternatives joined by `|` are accepted, including the legacy `|:` form. Bare-colon-separated types are rejected, including in `shortestPath` relationships. * Parenthesized `SET` and `REMOVE` targets must be followed by a property lookup. Parenthesized whole-entity assignments, label updates, and property expressions are rejected. * Valid forms such as `(n).x` and `:A|:B` continue to work.

pulls.title: fix: refuse a GRAPH.EFFECT CREATE_NODE record that repeats a node id
pulls.body: Closes #3247 ## Problem `apply_record` for `CREATE_NODE` turned the record's `IdList` into a `RoaringTreemap` and created that set. A repeated id was merged before anything could see it, so a client-sent `GRAPH.EFFECT` whose record names ids `[0, 0]` (count 2) created one node and replied `OK`. The label and attribute writes after it walk the list, not the set. `CREATE_EDGE` has refused the same shape since #2846 (`create_relationships_bulk`). ## Fix Before creating, compare the set's size with the record's id count. On a mismatch, refuse with the same wording as the edge path: `bulk node create got N ids of which only M are distinct; an id names one node`. The buffer is rejected and nothing is applied. | Record | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `CREATE_NODE` ids `[0, 0]` on an empty graph | `OK`, 1 node | `effect apply failed: bulk node create got 2 ids of which only 1 are distinct; an id names one node`, 0 nodes | n/a: C reads effects only up to v2 (`version mismatch expected version <= 2 got: 3`) | | `CREATE_EDGE` ids `[1, 1]` | refused | refused (unchanged) | n/a | ## Tests - New unit test `effects::v3::apply::tests::a_repeated_node_id_in_one_create_is_refused`. - Before (with the check disabled): `expected a refusal, got Ok(())`. - After: `ok`. - New flow test `test_effects_wire.py:testEffects_01_UnreadableBuffer.test09_a_repeated_id_in_one_create_record_is_refused`. It sends a node record with ids `[2, 3, 2]` and an edge record with ids `[1, 1]`. It checks that both are refused, that there is no resync, that the graph is unchanged, and that the ids are still free for the next write. - Before: `AssertionError: a node id repeated was accepted; it must be refused`. - After: passes. - Flow suites (release): `test_effects_wire` 15/15, `test_effects_shapes` 22/22, `test_effects_opcodes` 12/12, `test_effects_batch` 4/4, `test_effects_commands` 7/7. - `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except the known macOS `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). `fmt` and `clippy` are clean on the touched file. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Closes #3247. Refuses a `GRAPH.EFFECT CREATE_NODE` record that repeats a node id instead of silently creating one node, matching the refusal `CREATE_EDGE` has had since #2846. - Rejects the buffer with `bulk node create got N ids of which only M are distinct; an id names one node` and applies nothing. - Adds a Rust unit test and a flow test covering the refusal, no resync, unchanged graph, and freed ids for the next write. Written for commit ad9d88b3b1ff3a550bbc1858dcd998dc8559a0a9. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: validate the clauses that follow a procedure CALL
pulls.body: Closes #3279 ## Problem The `Call` arm of `QueryIR::inner_validate` (`graph/src/parser/ast.rs`) checked the procedure's own arguments and then returned `Ok(())`. It never validated the clauses after the `CALL`, so none of the usual checks ran there. A trailing `MATCH` reached the planner as the plan root and panicked in `utilize_node_by_id` (`parent().unwrap()` on `None`), which took the server down. ## Fix End the `Call` arm with `iter.next().map_or(Ok(()), |first| first.inner_validate(iter))`, as every other clause arm does. Graph: `CREATE (:N)`. | query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `CALL db.labels() YIELD label MATCH (n)` | **server crash** | Query cannot conclude with MATCH | same | | `CALL db.labels() YIELD label WITH label MATCH (n)` | **server crash** | Query cannot conclude with MATCH | same | | `CALL db.labels() YIELD label OPTIONAL MATCH (n)` | runs | Query cannot conclude with MATCH | same | | `CALL db.labels() YIELD label UNWIND [1] AS x` | runs | Query cannot conclude with UNWIND | same | | `CALL db.labels() YIELD label CREATE (a)-[:R\|S]->(b)` | creates an edge | Exactly one relationship type … CREATE pattern. | same | | `CALL db.labels() YIELD label MERGE (a)-[:R\|S]->(b)` | runs | Exactly one relationship type … MERGE pattern. | same | | `CALL db.labels() YIELD label MATCH (n) RETURN label, labels(n)` | rows | rows | **C crashes (SIGSEGV)** | ## Tests New flow test `test_procedures.py::test13_clauses_after_call_are_validated`. Before the fix (`main` @ b033aecc6) the server dies: `redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Connection closed by server. … process is not alive`. After the fix: `[PASS]`. pulls.title: fix: AND/OR/XOR type mismatches name the operand's type like C
pulls.body: Closes #3292 ## Problem When an `AND`/`OR`/`XOR` operand was not a boolean at runtime, the error printed the value in Rust's `Debug` form (`Type mismatch: expected Bool but was Int(3)`) and not its type. C, and Rust's own `NOT`, name the type. ## Fix The four messages (the `And`/`Or`/`Xor` arms in `eval.rs` and the vectorized connective in `vector_expr.rs`) now use `Value::name()` and C's wording for projections. | query | Rust `main` | this PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | `UNWIND [3] AS x RETURN x AND true` | `Type mismatch: expected Bool but was Int(3)` | `Type mismatch: expected Boolean or Null but was Integer` | same as this PR | | `UNWIND [3] AS x RETURN x OR false` | `… Bool but was Int(3)` | `… Boolean or Null but was Integer` | same as this PR | | `UNWIND [3] AS x RETURN x XOR true` | `… Bool but was Int(3)` | `… Boolean or Null but was Integer` | same as this PR | | `UNWIND ['a'] AS x RETURN x AND true` | `… Bool but was String("a")` | `… Boolean or Null but was String` | same as this PR | In a `WHERE` filter, C says `expected Boolean but was Integer` without "or Null". The evaluator does not know whether it is running a filter or a projection, so it uses the projection wording that `NOT` already uses. Whether `AND`/`OR` should short-circuit at all is a separate question, tracked in #3293 (needs decision), and this PR does not change it. ## Tests - New e2e test `test_boolean_operator_type_mismatch_names_the_type` covering the four queries above. - Before: `AssertionError: assert 'Type mismatch: expected Boolean or Null but was Integer' in 'Type mismatch: expected Bool but was Int(3)'` - After: passes. `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 132 passed. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except the known `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy reports no warnings in the touched files. - Flow tests (RLTest, release): `test_filters` 9/9, `test_query_validation` 51/51. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the error messages in AND/OR/XOR runtime type checks so they name the offending operand's type instead of printing its Rust `Debug` form. Messages now read `Type mismatch: expected Boolean or Null but was Integer` instead of `Type mismatch: expected Bool but was Int(3)`, matching C's wording and what `NOT` already emits. - Applies to the four scalar/vectorized connective paths in `eval.rs` and `vector_expr.rs`. - Since the evaluator can't tell a filter from a projection, WHERE clauses also get the "or Null" wording, which differs from C's filter message. - Leaves the separate short-circuit question (#3293) unchanged. - Adds an e2e test covering the four operator/operand combinations. Written for commit 1ef929506e53efd26cebe36409199f1e0dd03e8f. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: reject a query that ends with WITH
pulls.body: Closes #3271 ## Problem `QueryIR::inner_validate` (`graph/src/parser/ast.rs`) handled `With` in the same arm as `Return`, so it accepted `WITH` as the last clause of a query or of a `CALL { … }` body. `MATCH (n) WITH n` returned the projection as the result set, and `CREATE (a) WITH a` ran its write. ## Fix Give `With` its own arm, which returns `Query cannot conclude with WITH (must be a RETURN clause, an update clause, a procedure call or a non-returning subquery)` when no clause follows. This is the same shape the `Match` and `Unwind` arms already use, and the same message as C. | query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (n) WITH n` | returns every node | cannot conclude with WITH | cannot conclude with WITH | | `UNWIND [1] AS x WITH x` | `[[1]]` | error | error | | `WITH 1 AS x` | `[[1]]` | error | error | | `CREATE (a) WITH a` | creates the node | error, nothing created | error | | `MATCH (n) CALL { WITH n MATCH (m) WITH m } RETURN 1` | runs | error | error | | `MATCH (n) CALL { WITH n } RETURN 1` | runs | error | error | | `WITH 1 AS x RETURN x`, `MATCH (n) CALL { WITH n CREATE (:X) } RETURN 1` | run | run | run | A trailing `WITH` after a procedure `CALL` is still accepted until #3279 is fixed, because nothing after a `CALL` is validated yet. ## Tests New flow test `test_query_validation.py::test52_query_cannot_conclude_with_with`. Before the fix (`main` @ b033aecc6): ``` ❌ (FAIL): False == True [MATCH (n) WITH n] ❌ (FAIL): False == True [UNWIND [1] AS x WITH x] ❌ (FAIL): False == True [WITH 1 AS x] ❌ (FAIL): False == True [CREATE (a) WITH a] ❌ (FAIL): False == True [MATCH (n) CALL { WITH n MATCH (m) WITH m } RETURN 1] ❌ (FAIL): False == True [MATCH (n) CALL { WITH n } RETURN 1] ❌ (FAIL): [[1]] == [[0]] ``` After: `[PASS]`. Also run: the whole flow suite (124 files, without replication/persistency/defrag/bulk/cluster). Everything passes except `test_effects_ddl::test02_a_drop_during_validation_is_not_resurrected`, which fails on `main` too. Also: TCK (`TCK_DONE`: 2456 scenarios passed, 0 failed), `tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py` (131 passed), `cargo test -p graph --lib` (only the known macOS failure `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, #2922), `cargo fmt --check`, and no clippy warnings in the touched code. Validation-only change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes query validation so a query or `CALL { … }` body can no longer end with `WITH`, matching the behavior C already has. - Previously, `MATCH (n) WITH n` returned the projection as the result set and `CREATE (a) WITH a` ran its write; both now error with "Query cannot conclude with WITH". - Adds a flow test covering rejected and still-valid queries, including confirming a rejected `CREATE` did not execute. pulls.title: fix: an inline write no longer fails while a queued write is matching
pulls.body: Closes #3093 ## Problem A queued write claimed `MvccGraph`'s write slot (a CAS) as soon as it started, while it was still a reader matching without the GIL. An inline writer that ran in that window (`MULTI/EXEC`, Lua, `GRAPH.EFFECT`, anything on the main thread) took the GIL and the write lock, found the slot taken, and failed with `another write is in progress, retry the query`. Its write was lost. It could not wait instead, because the queued writer cannot escalate until the inline writer releases the GIL. C commits the inline write. ## Fix This is option A from the issue: claim the slot at escalation. - `MvccGraph::fork` makes a private version without claiming the slot. `MvccGraph::claim(fork)` claims it and checks that the fork still extends the committed version (`Claim::Busy` / `Claim::Stale`). `write()` is unchanged (claim + fork) for writers that already hold the write lock. - `QuerySession::write_version` hands a reader session an unclaimed fork. A writer session claims immediately. `upgrade_to_write` claims the fork right after escalating, under the GIL and the write lock. So the slot is only ever held by a thread that holds the write lock, and an inline writer never finds it taken. - If an inline writer committed while the query was matching, the claim reports `Stale`. At that point nothing has been mutated in shared state, no index document has been published, and nothing has been replied, so the query is dropped and run again from the start: - `execute_query_write` (GRAPH.QUERY / GRAPH.PROFILE) loops on a fresh session. - `GRAPH.BULK` rebuilds its fork. - `GRAPH.RECORD` (debug) reports the error. - `abandon_write` and `finish_write` release the slot only if this session claimed it (`QuerySession::release_slot`). `MULTI; GRAPH.QUERY mr "CREATE (:M)"; EXEC` sent 0.3 s after a queued `UNWIND range(1,40000000) AS x WITH count(x) AS c CREATE (:N {c:c})` (release build): | | MULTI reply | final counts | |---|---|---| | Rust before (`main` @ b033aecc6) | `another write is in progress, retry the query` (2/2 runs) | `N=1, Seed=1`, **M missing** | | Rust after | `Labels added: 1, Nodes created: 1` (3/3 runs) | `M=1, N=1, Seed=1` | | C (`bin/macos-arm64v8-release`) | `Labels added: 1, Nodes created: 1` | `M=1, N=1, Seed=1` (C also crashed on 2 of 3 runs of this race, a separate C bug, as noted in the issue) | The queued write still commits exactly once (`N=1`). ## Tests - New flow test `test_multi_exec.py::test_write_while_queued_write_matches`. It runs MULTI while a queued write is matching and asserts that the inline write commits, that the queued write commits exactly once, and that the two really overlapped. - Before: `FAIL True == False [another write is in progress, retry the query]` and `[['N', 1], ['Seed', 1]] == [['M', 1], ['N', 1], ['Seed', 1]]`. - After: PASS. - `tests/test_concurrency.py::_multi_write` no longer swallows `another write is in progress`. A MULTI write under concurrent queued-write load must now succeed. - New unit test `mvcc_graph::tests::a_fork_is_claimed_late_and_refused_once_stale`. - Also run: - `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` (no new warnings in touched code). - `cargo test --release -p graph --lib` (497 passed). - Flow suites, all pass: `test_multi_exec`, `test_bulk_insertion`, `test_concurrent_query`, `test_constraint`, `test_multi_writer`, `test_pause_replication_race`, `test_effects_commit`, `test_replication`. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py tests/test_mvcc.py tests/test_concurrency.py` (145 passed). Not hot-path: a queued write makes the same single `new_version()` as before. Only the CAS moves, from the start of the query to escalation. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #3093, where an inline write (e.g., inside MULTI/EXEC) failed with "another write is in progress" and lost its changes when it ran while a queued write was still matching. A queued write now builds into an unclaimed fork and claims the MVCC write slot only when it escalates under the write lock, so an inline writer never finds the slot taken. If an inline writer commits during matching, the queued write discards its fork and re-runs from the start. **Behavior** - GRAPH.RECORD returns a retryable error on a stale fork instead of retrying. - The write slot is only held by threads that hold the write lock. Written for commit ad2925117a40fdb47325867c5e9238c0d4feb0e0. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: reject a relationship variable repeated in a named-path CREATE or a MERGE
pulls.body: Closes #3287 ## Problem A relationship variable repeated inside one `CREATE` or `MERGE` pattern was dropped instead of rejected whenever the pattern had a path variable, and in every `MERGE`. The query created one edge where it wrote two. `CREATE ... RETURN p, q` also returned a `q` whose edge did not connect its nodes. `parse_pattern` checked the result of `QueryGraph::add_relationship` in four places, with different rules. The named-path and `allShortestPaths` branches only errored for `MATCH`, and the plain-path branch only for `MATCH` and `CREATE`. ## Fix All four call sites now go through a new `Parser::add_pattern_relationship`. It turns a repeat into the clause's error for every clause, using C's wording for `MERGE`. | Query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `CREATE p=(a)-[r:R]->(b), q=(c)-[r:R]->(d) RETURN p, q` | 4 nodes, 1 rel; `q = [(2), [0], (3)]` | `The bound variable 'r' can't be redeclared in a CREATE clause` | ``Variable `r` already declared`` | | `MERGE (a)-[r:R]->(b)-[r:R]->(c)` | 3 nodes, 1 rel | `The bound variable 'r' can't be redeclared in a MERGE clause` | same | | `MERGE p=(a)-[r:R]->(b)-[r:R]->(c)` | `Variable a not found` | `The bound variable 'r' can't be redeclared in a MERGE clause` | same | | `CREATE ()-[r:R]->()-[r:R]->()` | redeclared error | unchanged | error | ## Tests - `parser::cypher::tests::repeated_relationship_variable_is_rejected` covers six shapes (CREATE/MERGE/MATCH, with and without a path variable). Against the `main` parser it fails on the first silent shape (`CREATE p=..., q=...`: `left: None`). With this PR it passes. - Flow: `test_create_clause::test02_edge_reuse` gets the two named-path CREATE shapes, and `test_graph_merge::test31b_relationship_alias_redeclared` is new. On the `main` module they fail (`test_create_clause.py:58`, `test_graph_merge.py:633`). With this PR they pass: test_create_clause 8/8, test_graph_merge 39/39, test_graph_create 10/10, test_query_validation 51/51, test_path_filter 19/19. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 496 passed. The one failure is `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, which already fails on macOS (#2922). - `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. - `cargo fmt --check` is clean, and clippy reports nothing in touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Rejects a relationship variable repeated inside one `CREATE` or `MERGE` pattern instead of silently dropping the repeat. Closes #3287. - Previously, named-path `CREATE` patterns and all `MERGE` patterns created one edge where the query wrote two; only plain-path `MATCH` and `CREATE` raised an error. - All four `parse_pattern` call sites now route through `add_pattern_relationship`, which errors for every clause with a clause-specific message, with `MERGE` matching C's wording. - Adds unit and flow tests covering plain and named path shapes for `CREATE`, `MERGE`, and `MATCH`. Written for commit 9e3c117ac09b2a5b65441d5a614f576e452fbc5f. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: a deleted node keeps labels set or removed earlier in the same query
pulls.body: Closes #3245 ## Problem The project rule for Rust is that a node deleted by a query keeps all its details for the rest of the query. `DeleteOp` snapshotted a committed node's labels with `g.get_node_label_ids(id)`, which reads the committed label matrix. The attributes beside them already came from the pending view. So labels the same query set or removed before the `DELETE` were lost, and `labels(n)` / `n:L` answered from the committed labels. Both snapshot sites had this: `delete_nodes_bulk` (`DELETE n`) and `delete_entity` (`DELETE `, e.g. `coalesce(n)` or a path). ## Fix A new `staged_label_ids` overlays the query's staged adds/removes (`Pending::staged_node_labels`, which `update_node_labels` now uses too) on the committed label ids, and both snapshot sites use it. The snapshot is still collected straight into the `HashSet` that `DeletedNode` holds, so there is no extra allocation per node. | Query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (n:A) SET n:C DELETE n RETURN labels(n), n:C` | `[A], false` | `[A, C], true` | `[], false` | | `MATCH (n:A) REMOVE n:A DELETE n RETURN labels(n), n:A` | `[A], true` | `[], false` | `[], false` | | same two with `DELETE coalesce(n)` | `[A], false` / `[A], true` | `[A, C], true` / `[], false` | `[], false` | C returns no labels at all for a deleted node. The "after" column follows the Rust rule (a deleted entity keeps all its details), not C. ## Tests - New flow test `test_access_del_entity.py:testAccessDelNode.test10_deleted_node_keeps_labels_staged_in_the_same_query`. It covers both delete paths (`n` and `coalesce(n)`), a staged `SET` and a staged `REMOVE`, and checks that nothing staged on the deleted node reaches the graph. - Before the fix: 6 assertion failures, e.g. `['A'] == ['A', 'C']` and `[['B', 'A'], True, True] == [['B'], False, True]`, on both paths. - After: passes. - Flow suites (release): `test_access_del_entity` 19/19, `test_results` 18/18, `test_graph_deletion` 45/45, `test_index_delete` 14/14, `test_label_update` 6/6, `test_mix_labels` 9/9, `test_multi_label` 12/12, `test_effects_batch` 4/4. - `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except the known macOS `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). `fmt` and `clippy` are clean on the touched files. - Cost, measured on `MATCH (n:A) DELETE n RETURN count(labels(n))` over 200k `:A:B` nodes, which takes the snapshot path (median of 7 runs; the machine was at load ~20-45, so the numbers are noisy): | build | run 1 | run 2 | best single run | |---|---|---|---| | `main` | 209 ms | 158 ms | 154 ms | | this PR | 173 ms | 163 ms | 157 ms | | C | 120 ms | | 116 ms | No measurable change from `main`. The gap to C is older than this PR, and C keeps no labels for a deleted node. Separate and older than this PR: `DeletedNode.labels` is a `std::collections::HashSet`, so the *order* of a deleted node's labels is random between runs (`['B', 'A']` vs `['A', 'B']` in the failure output above). That is why the test sorts them. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes deleted nodes losing labels that were set or removed earlier in the same query. The snapshot now overlays the query's staged label changes on the committed labels, so `labels(n)` and `n:L` reflect the node's state at the `DELETE`. - Uses a new `staged_label_ids` helper that reuses the same staging logic as live nodes; applied to both the bulk `DELETE n` and per-entity `DELETE ` paths without extra allocation per node. - Adds a flow test covering both delete paths and staged `SET`/`REMOVE` cases, ensuring staged changes don't leak into the graph. Written for commit 156912daa326add51baeee8e8081feb69644eb86. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: virtual keys of one graph can no longer share a name
pulls.body: Closes #3284 ## Problem `uuid_v4` names the virtual keys that a large graph is split into during an RDB save. It mixed the clock and a per-process counter as `a = t ^ seq` and derived every printed field from `a`. Two calls whose clock and counter changed in the same bits got the same name (`4 ^ 2 == 5 ^ 3`). The second `vkey_map.insert` then replaced the first virtual key, and that slice of the graph was missing from the save. ## Fix The mixing now lives in `const fn uuid_fields(t, seq)`, and the clock and the counter go in separate fields. The first three fields come from `t`, and the last 48 bits come from `seq * K + C` with `K` odd, which is a bijection modulo 2^48. Two calls in one process therefore always get different names, whatever the clock does, and the clock still separates names across restarts. The name keeps its UUID shape and its `{graph}graph_` key format. | calls | Rust `main` | this PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | `t=4, seq=2` vs `t=5, seq=3` | same name | different names | random UUID (`UUID_New`), no collision | | same `t`, consecutive `seq` | different | different | different | ## Tests This crate's unit tests cannot run outside Redis, because its global allocator is Redis's (`cargo test -p falkordb-rs` aborts with "the Redis Allocator isn't available"). The regression check is therefore a compile-time `const` assertion next to the function, and it runs in every build: - Before the fix, with the old `t ^ seq` mixing extracted unchanged into `uuid_fields`: `error[E0080]: evaluation panicked: virtual key names collide for (t=4, seq=2) and (t=5, seq=3)` - After: the build succeeds. The collision was not reproduced live because it depends on timing. On macOS the clock has microsecond resolution, so consecutive calls cannot collide there. On Linux, two calls exactly 1 ns apart can. - Flow tests (RLTest, release): `test_encode_decode` 19/19 (multi-key saves), `test_rdb_load` 2/2, `test_graph_copy` 9/9, `test_replication_states` 1/1. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy reports no warnings in `redis_type.rs`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a collision in virtual key naming that could drop a slice of a graph from RDB saves. `uuid_v4` mixed the clock and the call counter with XOR, so two calls whose clock and counter shifted in the same bits produced identical names, and the second virtual key replaced the first. The clock and counter now occupy separate fields, and a compile-time assertion prevents the colliding pair. Written for commit 55d4ca549c968200037e367d664cce185e74850a. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: CowBTree rejects DOC_BYTES widths it cannot read back
pulls.body: Closes #3238 ## Problem `CowBTree`'s const assert accepted `DOC_BYTES ∈ 1..=8`, but the doc field is read back with `read_width`, which loads only 1/2/4/8 bytes and treats any other width as 8. `CowBTree::<256, 256, 3>` compiled and panicked on its second insert. Latent: the only production instantiation (numeric index) uses `DOC_BYTES = 8`. Different from the two CowBTree bugs in #2893 / #2897; found by the Lean model of #2278 (`LeafAosD.docBytes3_*`). ## Fix The smaller of the two options in the issue: a `const fn is_read_width(width) -> bool { matches!(width, 1 | 2 | 4 | 8) }` next to `read_width`, used by the three const asserts (`Default`, `new`, `from_sorted`), so the accepted set is defined by the reader. Supporting 3/5/6/7 would need a variable-length load in the hot read path for no current user. Compile-time only; no runtime code changes. | `CowBTree::<256, 256, 3>::new()` then two `insert`s | Result | |---|---| | Rust before | compiles; 2nd insert panics — debug: `assertion left == right failed` (`mod.rs:98`); release: `range end index 16 out of range for slice of length 11` (`mod.rs:99`) | | Rust after | compile error: `DOC_BYTES must be 1, 2, 4 or 8: it is the AoS doc field width, read back with read_width, which loads only those widths` | | C | n/a (no equivalent structure) | ## Tests - `doc_bytes_accepts_exactly_the_readable_widths`: `is_read_width` over `0..=16` accepts exactly `[1, 2, 4, 8]`, and `read_width` round-trips each accepted width. pulls.title: fix: CowBTree remove_batch never leaves a one-child non-root branch
pulls.body: Closes #3237 ## Problem `CowBTree::remove_batch` repairs under-full children one level at a time (`merge_underfull`). A branch that ends with a single child cannot repair it — it has no sibling — so it reports its own underflow to its parent. If the parent also ends with one child, the grandparent merges it with a neighbour via `Node::combine`, which concatenates the two child lists; the one-child branch lands in the merged node and nothing re-examines it. A later `remove` that drains its lone leaf leaves an empty non-root leaf, and the next `insert_batch` panics in `Node::min`. Any `BRANCH_MAX >= 4`. Since #2350 the numeric index calls `remove_batch` on commit, but at the production fan-out (256/256) the shape needs a height-3 tree, so this was reproduced as a unit test, not a live query. Different from the two CowBTree bugs in #2893 / #2897; found by the Lean model of #2278 (`BugsBatch.lean`). ## Fix `merge_underfull` (batch path only) now, after each combine, re-runs itself over the children of the node(s) the combine produced (`Node::merge_underfull_below`, a no-op unless one of them is under-full) and re-checks the produced node. The single-key `rebalance` path is unchanged. | `CowBTree::<2, 4>`: 96 keys, `remove_batch(33..64)`, `remove(32)`, `insert_batch([(0,1),(95,1)])` | Result | |---|---| | Rust before | `check_invariants`: "branch must have >= 2 children: 1"; then `insert_batch` panics: `range end index 8 out of range for slice of length 0` (`mod.rs:83`) | | Rust after | well-formed after every step, contents correct | | C | n/a (no equivalent structure) | `remove_batch` timing (`CowBTree<256,256>`, 4M entries, release, median of 31) is within machine noise: main vs fix, two interleaved rounds each — scattered 2/3: 150.8 / 73.2 ms vs 69.6 / 152.5 ms; middle half: 36.1 / 22.8 ms vs 19.0 / 51.9 ms; 1k range: 0.025 / 0.025 ms vs 0.014 / 0.014 ms. ## Tests - `remove_batch_never_leaves_a_single_child_branch` — the exact repro. - `remove_batch_keeps_the_tree_well_formed_for_any_window` — every contiguous drain window at `<2,4>`, `<2,5>`, `<2,8>`, `<4,4>`, then a `remove` + `insert_batch`, checking invariants and contents. Before the fix (main @ b033aecc6): both FAILED (`tests.rs:1347` "branch must have >= 2 children"). After: `cargo test -p graph --lib cow_btree` 35 passed; `cargo test -p graph --lib` 497 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, #2922). `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py` 131 passed; flow `test_index_updates`, `test_index_delete`, `test_edge_index_updates`, `test_index_scans` all pass. fmt / clippy clean. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `CowBTree::remove_batch` leaving a one-child non-root branch that corrupted the tree: a later `remove` emptied its lone leaf, and the next `insert_batch` panicked in `Node::min`. The batch path now re-runs under-full repair on the children of every node a merge produces and re-checks the result; the single-key `rebalance` path is unchanged. Adds the exact repro and a sweep across drain windows and fan-outs that checks invariants and contents after each step, and shows batch-removal timing on a 4M-entry tree stays within machine noise. Written for commit 56c39c3dbc6924f7a1eede9d31832233b9f6a989. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: OPTIONAL MATCH with a filter inside CALL {} no longer fails with "Variable n not found"
pulls.body: Closes #2728 ## Problem `MATCH (x:A:B) CALL { OPTIONAL MATCH (n:A:B {id:3}) RETURN n.id AS nid } RETURN x.id, nid` fails with `Variable n not found`. C returns `[1,3],[2,3],[3,3]`. The query in #2728 (`Variable n1 not found`) fails for the same reason. `push_filters_down` (`graph/src/planner/optimizer/push_filters_down.rs:214-242`) handles a filter in the right branch of an `Apply` by walking up to the nearest `Apply` and adding its left branch's variables to the set the filter may be pushed under. The walk stepped over `Optional`, so the filter on `n` in the CALL body's `Optional` reached the outer `Apply` and inherited the outer query's variables (`x`). Variable sets here are ids only, and ids are per scope, so the body's `n` and the outer `x` share an id. The filter was then pushed below `n`'s scan onto its `Argument`, where `n` is unbound: ``` Optional Project Argument Node By Label Scan | (n:A:B) Filter <- n.id = 3, below the scan of n Argument ``` ## Fix The walk stops at the nearest `Apply` or `Optional`, since both feed their left branch's rows to the right branch through `Argument`. When that left branch is a `Project`/`Aggregate`, such as a CALL body's import, it inherits only the variables that operator names (`branch_output_variables`). The filter now stays above the scan: ``` Optional Project Argument Filter Node By Label Scan | (n:A:B) Argument ``` Setup: `UNWIND range(1,3) AS i CREATE (:A:B {id: i})` | query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (x:A:B) CALL { OPTIONAL MATCH (n:A:B {id:3}) RETURN n.id AS nid } RETURN x.id, nid` | `Variable n not found` | `[1,3],[2,3],[3,3]` | `[1,3],[2,3],[3,3]` | | `MATCH (x:A:B) CALL { WITH x OPTIONAL MATCH (n:A:B) WHERE n.id = x.id + 1 RETURN n.id AS nid } RETURN x.id, nid` | `[1,2],[2,3],[3,null]` | same | same | | query from #2728 (empty graph) | `Variable n1 not found` | no rows, 1 node created | no rows, 1 node created | ## Tests New `tests/test_e2e.py::test_call_optional_match_filter_not_pushed_with_outer_variable_ids` covers both queries in the table and the query from #2728. - before (origin/main b033aecc6 build): `ResponseError: Variable n not found`, FAILED - after: passed Other checks (release build, private ports): - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. The one failure, `test_load_csv`, fails the same way on main because the local import folder `/var/lib/FalkorDB/import/` is missing. - TCK (`TCK_DONE=tck_done.txt`): passed - Flow: `test_call_subquery` 56/56, `test_optional_match` 27/27, `test_filters` 9/9, `test_foreach` 19/19, `test_inline_pattern_attributes` 21/21, `test_multi_pattern` 7/7, `test_path_filter` 19/19, `test_relation_patterns` 13/13, `test_reversed_patterns` 1/1, `test_union` 10/10, `test_with_clause` 14/14, `test_graph_merge` 38/38 - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 495 passed. The 1 failure is the known macOS-only `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). - `cargo fmt --check` passes, and `cargo clippy -p graph --all-targets` reports no warnings in `push_filters_down.rs`. This change is optimizer-only and does not touch the runtime. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `OPTIONAL MATCH` with a filter inside a `CALL {}` body so the query no longer fails with "Variable n not found". **Bug Fixes** - `push_filters_down` now stops its ancestor walk at the nearest `Apply` or `Optional`, since both feed left-branch rows to the right through `Argument`. - When that left branch is a `Project`/`Aggregate` (a `CALL {}` import), only the variables it names are inherited, so body variables no longer collide with outer variables that share the same id. - The filter now stays above the body's scan instead of being pushed onto its `Argument` where the variable is unbound. - Added an e2e test covering the failing queries from #2728 and the regression cases; the change is optimizer-only and does not touch the runtime. Written for commit 39cac5dddcbdea1ce25db6d75f2a91f2c771f97b. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: dbms.functions unions and the fulltext.drop error are spelled like C
pulls.body: Part of #3272 (items 1 and 2; items 3–6 need a decision and are left open there). ## Problem - `type_to_dbms_string` (`graph/src/runtime/functions/procedures.rs`) joined `Type::Union` members in the order each signature declares them; C always uses its fixed type order. - `Graph::drop_index` (`graph/src/graph/graph.rs`) always printed `(attrs)` in its "no such index" error, so `db.idx.fulltext.drop('L')` said `:L()`. ## Fix - Flatten a union's members and sort them by C's type order (the same list Rust already used to spell `Any`, now a shared `DBMS_TYPE_ORDER` const). - Omit the parentheses when no attribute is named. | | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `point` return type | `Point or Null` | `Null or Point` | `Null or Point` | | `distance` arguments | `[Point or Null, Point or Null]` | `[Null or Point, Null or Point]` | same as after | | `tofloat` arguments | `[String, Float, Integer, or Null]` | `[String, Integer, Float, or Null]` | same as after | | `vecf32` / `vec.cosineDistance` / `vec.euclideanDistance` | `Vectorf32 or Null` | `Null or Vectorf32` | `Null or Vectorf32` | | `CALL db.idx.fulltext.drop('Nope')` | `Unable to drop index on :Nope(): no such index.` | `… :Nope: no such index.` | `… :Nope: no such index.` | Across the 99 function names both engines list, rows that differ from C drop from 16 to 10; the remaining 10 are real signature differences, listed in #3272. ## Tests - New flow tests `tests/flow/test_procedures.py::test13_function_union_type_order`, `test14_fulltext_drop_missing_index_message`. - Before (module built from `main`): both FAIL (`'Point or Null'…`, `':NoSuchLabel()'`). - After: `test_procedures.py` 14/14, `test_index_create.py` 18/18, `test_index_delete.py` 14/14, `test_fulltext_query.py` 5/5 pass. - `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p graph --all-targets` adds no warnings in touched code; `cargo test -p graph --lib` 495 pass (only the known macOS `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, #2922). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes two mismatches with C's behavior: `dbms.functions()` now spells union types in C's fixed type order (e.g. "Null or Point" instead of "Point or Null"), and `db.idx.fulltext.drop` no longer prints empty parentheses in the "no such index" error when no attribute is named. Part of #3272. - Unions are flattened and sorted against a shared `DBMS_TYPE_ORDER` constant. - Adds flow tests for both the ordering and the error message. Written for commit b3717ac872164029982cdf3f37f85642fe528e34. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: effects payloads of 4 GiB or more ship uncompressed instead of with a truncated length
pulls.body: Closes #3276 ## Problem `maybe_compress` wrote the frame's `plain_len` and `comp_len` with `as u32`. With `EFFECTS_COMPRESSION` enabled, a payload of 4 GiB or more declared a truncated length, for example 5 for 4 GiB + 5. The replica uses that length as the ceiling for `zstd::bulk::decompress`, so it rejected the frame, never applied the write, and looped on forced resyncs. ## Fix The 12-byte prefix is now built by `frame_prefix`, which narrows both lengths with `u32::try_from` and returns `None` when either does not fit. `maybe_compress` then leaves the payload uncompressed, and an uncompressed payload has no length field to overflow. It also returns early when the plaintext alone is already too long, so a 4 GiB payload is not compressed only to be discarded. Payloads under 4 GiB produce the same bytes as before. | plaintext | Rust `main` | this PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | < 4 GiB | compressed, `plain_len` exact | same bytes | no v3 / compression | | 4 GiB + 5 | compressed, declares `plain_len = 5`, replica refuses | shipped uncompressed, applies | no v3 / compression | ## Tests - New unit test `effects::v3::records::tests::a_frame_whose_lengths_do_not_fit_u32_is_not_written`. It builds the prefix from the lengths alone and allocates nothing large. - Before the fix (the same `as u32` logic, extracted unchanged into `frame_prefix`): `left: Some([5, 0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 0, 0, ...]) right: None` - After: `ok` - `cargo test -p graph --lib effects`: 197 passed, including the existing compression round-trip tests. Full `cargo test -p graph --lib` passes except the known `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy reports no warnings in the touched file. - Flow tests (RLTest, release): `test_effects_wire` 14/14 (covers compressed payloads), `test_effects_values` 9/9, `test_replication` 2/2. `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes effects payloads of 4 GiB or more shipping with a truncated compressed-frame length. `maybe_compress` narrowed the frame's `plain_len` and `comp_len` with `as u32`, so a 4 GiB + 5 byte payload declared a length of 5; the replica takes that declared length as its decompress ceiling, rejects the frame, and loops on forced resyncs. - The 12-byte prefix is now built by `frame_prefix`, which refuses lengths that don't fit `u32` and leaves such payloads uncompressed. Compression is skipped when the plaintext alone already exceeds `u32`. - Payloads under 4 GiB produce the same bytes as before. - New unit test builds the prefix from its lengths alone, without allocating the 4 GiB payload. Written for commit a735fa87f86174a520723bafeeb77b95c14a7c35. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: a deleted edge no longer keeps its type after a constraint registers a new type
pulls.body: Closes #3244 ## Problem `Graph::get_type_id_mut` registered a relationship type and its tensor but did not call `resize()`, so `relationship_type_matrix` (edges x types) stayed one column short. `get_relationship_matrix_mut` and `get_label_id_mut` both resize for this reason. Its callers that register a type with no edge are `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE ... RELATIONSHIP ` on the primary and `ADD_SCHEMA` in effects apply on a replica. After that, edge deletes (`delete_relationships`, `delete_implicit_edges`) built a removal mask `relationship_cap x relationship_types.len()` that the narrower matrix refused with `GrB_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`. Only a `debug_assert` checks it, so in release the deleted edge kept its type, and the edge that reused its id read back with the old type. ## Fix Call `self.resize()` in `get_type_id_mut` after registering the type. `resize` costs a few comparisons when nothing changed, and this runs once per type ever. The one change covers both the primary and the replica path. ``` CREATE (:N)-[:A]->(:N) GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE g MANDATORY RELATIONSHIP B PROPERTIES 1 x MATCH ()-[r]->() DELETE r MATCH (a), (b) WHERE id(a) = 0 AND id(b) = 1 CREATE (a)-[:C]->(b) MATCH ()-[r]->() RETURN id(r), type(r) ``` | | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | primary `type(r)` | `A` | `C` | `C` | | replica `type(r)` | `A` | `C` | n/a (C cannot read v3 effects) | ## Tests - New flow test `test_effects_ddl.py:testEffects_01_ConstraintAsEffect.test04_a_type_registered_by_a_constraint_does_not_stick_to_deleted_edges` runs the repro on a primary/replica pair and checks `type(r)` and the `:A` count on both sides. - Before the fix: fails twice, `[[0, 'A']] == [[0, 'C']]`, once for the primary and once for the replica. - After: passes. - Flow suites (release): `test_constraint.py` 26/26, `test_effects_topology.py` 3/3, `test_effects_opcodes.py` 12/12, `test_effects_ddl.py` 18/19. The one failure is `testEffects_06_ConstraintSettlingRaces.test02` (`[[1]] == [[2]]`). It also fails on `main` with the class run alone, and the test's own comment records it as a known intermittent failure. - `RELEASE=1 pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except the known macOS `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). `cargo fmt --check` is clean, with no clippy warnings in the touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #3244: a deleted edge no longer keeps its type after a constraint registers a new type. `get_type_id_mut` registered a relationship type and its tensor but didn't resize `relationship_type_matrix`, so a type registered with no edge (a `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT` on the primary, an `ADD_SCHEMA` on a replica) left the edge×type matrix one column short. The next edge delete then built a removal mask the narrower matrix rejected — only a `debug_assert` caught the mismatch — so in release builds the deleted edge kept its type and the edge that reused its id read back the old type. The fix routes every type registration through `register_relationship_type`, a single helper that pushes the type name, inserts its tensor, and always calls `resize()`. Both `get_type_id_mut` and `get_relationship_matrix_mut` now go through it, so no registration site can skip the resize. `resize` costs a few comparisons when nothing changed and runs once per type. The change covers the primary and replica paths, and the new flow test runs the repro against both. Written for commit 5733f785611bbb41133ce8aa290be7fa9cd497e8. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Relationship types remain consistent across graph updates and constraints, including on replicas. When a deleted edge’s ID is reused for a different relationship type, the edge is associated only with its current type; stale associations are no longer retained on the master or replicas. This keeps relationship information accurate after edge changes.

pulls.body: Closes #3273 ## Problem `Index::create_rs_index` allocated the RediSearch index options (`RediSearch_CreateIndexOptions`, an `rm_calloc`), then hit early returns that skipped `RediSearch_FreeIndexOptions`: a stopword, language or label with a NUL byte (`CString::new(...)?`), and `Language is not supported`. Related: #2449 (language validated only when the spec is created) touches the same function and is not changed here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #3273: a refused fulltext `CREATE INDEX` no longer leaks the RediSearch options block. **Bug Fixes** - Moves `CString` conversions before the options allocation so early returns cannot leak it. - Frees the options block on the unsupported-language error path; behavior and error messages are unchanged. - Adds a flow test that verifies 10,000 refused statements grow `used_memory` by under 200 KB. pulls.title: fix: accept a list or map subscript as a WHERE predicate
pulls.body: Closes #3261 ## Problem `Binder::expr_may_return_boolean` put `ExprIR::GetElement` with the node kinds that can never be boolean, so any subscript used as a predicate (`WHERE n.flags[0]`, `WHERE true AND l[0]`, `WHERE m['a']`) failed with `Expected boolean predicate` before the query ran. C accepts these and checks the element's type at runtime. ## Fix Move `GetElement` to the "may be boolean" arm next to `Property`, `Variable` and `Parameter`. `GetElements` (a slice, always a list) is still rejected. | query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (n:N) WHERE n.flags[0] RETURN count(n)` | Expected boolean predicate | 1 | 1 | | `MATCH (n:N) WHERE NOT n.flags[0] RETURN count(n)` | Expected boolean predicate | 1 | 1 | | `WITH [true] AS l WHERE true AND l[0] RETURN 1` | Expected boolean predicate | 1 row | 1 row | | `WITH {a: true} AS m WHERE m['a'] RETURN 1` | Expected boolean predicate | 1 row | 1 row | | `WITH [null] AS l WHERE l[0] RETURN count(*)` | Expected boolean predicate | 0 | 0 | | `WITH [1] AS l WHERE l[0] RETURN 1` | Expected boolean predicate | Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer | same | | `WITH [true] AS l WHERE l[0..1] RETURN 1` | Expected boolean predicate | Expected boolean predicate | same | (graph: `CREATE (:N {flags: [true, false]}), (:N {flags: [false]}), (:N)`) One difference is left. C constant-folds a subscript of a literal (`WHERE [1][0]`) and rejects it as `Expected boolean predicate` at compile time. Rust now gives the runtime `Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer`. Both are errors. `test_reduce.py::test_nested_reduction` asserted the compile-time message for `WHERE [x IN [0] | reduce(...)][0]`. C gives `Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer` for that query, so the assertion now matches C. ## Tests New flow test `test_filters.py::test10_subscript_as_predicate`. Before the fix (`main` @ b033aecc6) it fails with `redis.exceptions.ResponseError: Expected boolean predicate`. After the fix: `[PASS]`.
