pulls.title: fix: nested lists in an effects payload can no longer reserve memory quadratic in its size
pulls.body: Closes #3266 ## Problem The v3 `SIValue` decoder checks a nested `T_ARRAY`'s child count only against the bytes left after it, and ignores the siblings that its ancestor frames still owe. Every level of `[[[…` can therefore claim the whole remainder, and each level then calls `ThinVec::with_capacity` for that claim. The reservations add up to the square of the payload. Any client can send `GRAPH.EFFECT`, and a 1 MB payload pushed `redis-server` to a 2.3 GB peak RSS before the decode failed at the end of the buffer. ## Fix `Value::decode` keeps `owed`, the number of children the open frames still need beyond the one being read now (`Σ (left − 1)`). A new list must fit `n + owed` values in the remaining bytes. Its own children and the siblings it would otherwise take bytes from are disjoint byte ranges, so the total capacity reserved across the stack stays at or below `remaining / 4`, which is linear in the payload. Legitimate values are unaffected, because their claims are always backed by real bytes. Peak RSS of `redis-server` after one hostile `GRAPH.EFFECT` (repro script in #3266, fresh server per row, `/usr/bin/time -l`): | payload | Rust `main` | this PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | none (idle) | 23.6 MB | 23.6 MB | – | | 256 KB | 566 MB, fails at EOF | 24.7 MB, refused at once (`ImplausibleCount`) | no v3 decoder | | 1 MB | 2.31 GB, 1.34 s | 25.5 MB, under 10 ms | no v3 decoder | ## Tests - New unit test `effects::v3::value::tests::nested_lists_cannot_each_claim_the_whole_remaining_buffer`, which uses 1,000 levels, each claiming the most its trailing bytes allow. - Before the fix: `FAILED … expected the claim to be refused up front, got UnexpectedEof { want: 4, have: 0 }` - After: `ok`. The payload is refused at the second level. - `cargo test -p graph --lib effects`: 197 passed, including the 5,000-deep round trip and the nested-list round trip. - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except the known `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy reports no warnings in the touched file. - Flow tests (RLTest, release): `test_effects_values` 9/9, `test_effects_wire` 14/14, `test_effects_shapes` 22/22, `test_effects_opcodes` 12/12, `test_replication` 2/2. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents a DoS vector where a 1 MB `GRAPH.EFFECT` payload could push `redis-server` to 2.3 GB RSS by reserving memory quadratically. `Value::decode` now tracks how many children the open frames still owe and checks each nested list's count against that total, so capacity reservations stay linear in the payload size. Written for commit d86f3b56049b8c9cac6f506fa18bf98d9b790166. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: keep an earlier MATCH … WHERE / UNWIND under a variable-length traverse
pulls.body: Refs #2972. This is the variable-length shape of that bug. #3099 fixes the fixed-length `CondTraverse` shape and closes the issue. This PR fixes the separate `CondVarLenTraverse` code path, so it does not close #2972. ## Problem `MATCH (a) WHERE a.v=1 MATCH (a)-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2})` returned rows for every `a`, not only for `a.v = 1`. `plan_query` stitches the first clause, `Filter(AllNodeScan a)`, under the second clause's `CondVarLenTraverse`. `select_var_len_scan_node` (`graph/src/planner/optimizer/select_scan_node.rs`) reverses a leaf traverse when `to` is the more selective end. `planner_scan_alias` looks through `Filter` wrappers, so the stitched clause was taken for the planner's own scan of `from`. The leaf rewrite then pruned it and pushed a bare scan of `b`, keeping only an `Argument` leaf. The non-leaf branch above it already refused a `Filter` wrapper; the leaf branch did not. Anything planned below the scan was dropped too, such as an earlier `UNWIND`. ``` Project Conditional Variable Length Traverse | (a)-[_anon_0*1..2]->(b) Filter Node By Label Scan | (b:B) <- a.v = 1 is gone ``` ## Fix The leaf rewrite now runs only when the subtree is the planner's own scan: no `Filter` wrapper, and nothing under the scan except an `Argument` leaf, which is the only thing it carries over. Otherwise the planner's direction is kept. `IncludePending` (MERGE) is still rebuilt as before. Setup: `CREATE (a1 {v:1})-[:R]->(:B {w:2}), (a2 {v:0})-[:R]->(:B {w:2}), (a3 {v:0})-[:R]->(:X)-[:R]->(:B {w:2})` | query | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (a) WHERE a.v=1 MATCH (a)-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2}) RETURN a.v, b.w` | `[1,2],[0,2],[null,2],[0,2]` | `[1,2]` | `[1,2]` | | `UNWIND [1,2] AS i MATCH (a) WHERE a.v = 1 MATCH (a)-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2}) RETURN count(*)` | 4 | 2 | 2 | | `UNWIND [1,2] AS i MATCH (a)-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2}) RETURN count(*)` | 4 | 8 | 8 | | `MATCH (a {v:0})-[*1..2]->(b:B {w:2}) RETURN count(*)` (single clause, still scans `b:B`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | ## Tests New `tests/test_e2e.py::test_var_len_traverse_keeps_earlier_clause_below_it` covers the WHERE, WHERE + UNWIND, and UNWIND shapes. It also checks that a single MATCH still starts from the selective end (plan unchanged: `Node By Label Scan | (b:B)`). - before (origin/main b033aecc6 build): `assert [[1, 2], [0, ...e, 2], [0, 2]] == [[1, 2]]`, FAILED - after: passed Other checks (release build, private ports): - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. The one failure, `test_load_csv`, fails the same way on main because the local import folder `/var/lib/FalkorDB/import/` is missing. - Flow: `test_variable_length_traversals` 18/18, `test_varlength_traversal` 9/9, `test_traversal_construction` 16/16, `test_graph_merge` 38/38, `test_optional_match` 27/27, `test_call_subquery` 56/56, `test_path_filter` 19/19, `test_bidirectional_traversals` 12/12, `test_path` 8/8 - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 495 passed. The 1 failure is the known macOS-only `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). - `cargo fmt --check` passes, and `cargo clippy -p graph --all-targets` reports no warnings in `select_scan_node.rs`. This change is optimizer-only. Plans change only for queries that had an earlier clause under the traverse, and those now keep it, as C does. It touches the same file as #3099 and #3046, in a different function (`select_var_len_scan_node`). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes variable-length traversals dropping an earlier `MATCH ... WHERE` filter or `UNWIND` when the planner reversed the traversal to scan the more selective endpoint. - The leaf rewrite now runs only when the subtree below the scan is the planner's own scan (no `Filter` wrapper, only an `Argument` leaf); otherwise the original direction is kept. - Adds e2e tests covering the `WHERE`, `UNWIND`, and combined shapes, and confirms a single-clause traversal still scans the selective end. Written for commit 583a8846fff7f0383cb5f207eac91ad3dfd277b3. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: give graphs loaded from an RDB the configured CACHE_SIZE
pulls.body: Closes #3251 ## Problem `src/redis_type.rs` hard-coded `DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE = 25` and passed it to `rdb_load_graph` in `graph_rdb_load` and `graphmeta_rdb_load`, and to the multi-key placeholder graph. So a graph loaded from an RDB (restart, `DEBUG RELOAD`, a replica's full sync) always had a 25-entry plan cache, whatever `CACHE_SIZE` the module was loaded with. Graphs created at run-time honour it. ## Fix The load callbacks run on the main thread, so `io_cache_size` takes the context Redis attaches to the IO handle (`RedisModule_GetContextFromIO`) and reads `CONFIGURATION_CACHE_SIZE` with it, the way `create_virtual_keys` already reads `VKEY_MAX_ENTITY_COUNT`. The constant is gone. `CACHE_SIZE 1`, `DEBUG RELOAD`, then `RETURN 1`, `RETURN 2`, `RETURN 1`: | | `main` | This PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | `Cached execution` | 0, 0, **1** | 0, 0, 0 | 0, 0, 0 | ## Tests - New flow test `test_cache.testCache.test_15_cache_size_survives_rdb_load` (`CACHE_SIZE 1`, reload, check a second query evicts the first). - Before: `True == False` FAIL at the last `RETURN 1`. - After: pass. - Flow (RLTest, release): `test_cache` 15/15, `test_encode_decode` 19/19 (multi-key load path, `VKEY_MAX_ENTITY_COUNT 10`), `test_persistency` 11/11, `test_rdb_load` 2/2, `test_replication` 2/2. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. `cargo fmt --check` clean; `clippy --all-targets` has no warnings in touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes graphs loaded from an RDB (restart, `DEBUG RELOAD`, or replica full sync) so they use the configured `CACHE_SIZE` instead of the previously hard-coded default of 25. Load callbacks run on the main thread, so they now read the configured value through the context Redis attaches to the IO handle, matching how graphs created at runtime behave. - Adds a flow test that reloads with `CACHE_SIZE 1` and verifies a second query evicts the first from the cache. - Closes #3251. pulls.title: fix: NOT over a pattern predicate drops rows where the predicate is null
pulls.body: Closes #3241 ## Problem `Planner::expr_to_plan` planned `NOT (complex)` as `AntiSemiApply(input, plan(inner))`. The inner plan passes a row only when the inner predicate is `true`, so `AntiSemiApply` passed every row where it was not `true`, including the rows where it is `null`. `NOT null` is `null` and should drop the row. ## Fix When `NOT` wraps an `AND`, `OR` or `NOT` (under any parentheses), push it down with De Morgan before planning (`push_not_down`, `graph/src/planner/mod.rs`). These identities hold in three-valued logic. The leaves become `NOT pattern`, planned as `AntiSemiApply` (a pattern is never `null`), or `NOT scalar`, planned as an ordinary `Filter`. Other operators (`XOR`) keep the existing path. Graph: `CREATE (:N {v: 0}), (:N), (:N {v: 5}), (:N)-[:R]->(:M)`, query `MATCH (a:N) WHERE RETURN count(a)`: | predicate | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `NOT (a.v > 1 OR (a)-->())` | 2 | 1 | 1 | | `NOT (a.v > 1 AND (a)-->())` | 4 | 3 | 3 | | `NOT (NOT (a.v > 1 OR (a)-->()))` | 2 | 2 | 2 | | `NOT (a.v = 0 OR NOT (a)-->())` | 1 | 0 | 0 | | `NOT ((a)-->() OR NOT (a.v < 3 AND (a)<--()))` | 0 | 0 | 0 | ## Tests New flow test `test_path_filter.py::test19_negated_pattern_predicate_drops_null_rows`. Before the fix (`main` @ b033aecc6): ``` ❌ (FAIL): [[2]] == [[1]] [NOT (a.v > 1 OR (a)-->())] ❌ (FAIL): [[4]] == [[3]] [NOT (a.v > 1 AND (a)-->())] ❌ (FAIL): [[1]] == [[0]] [NOT (a.v = 0 OR NOT (a)-->())] ``` After: `[PASS]`. Also run: `test_path_filter` (20/20) and every flow suite that uses `NOT` (30 suites, all pass except `test_defrag::test_frag_ratio`, which fails on `main` too); `tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py` (131 passed); `cargo test -p graph --lib` (only the known macOS failure `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, #2922); `cargo fmt --check`; no clippy warnings in the touched code. Planner-only change, no runtime hot path touched. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `NOT` over a pattern predicate returning rows where the negated predicate is `null`. `NOT null` is `null`, so those rows should be dropped, but the planner's `AntiSemiApply` over the inner predicate kept every row where the inner predicate was not `true`, including the `null` ones. - Pushes `NOT` down to the leaves with De Morgan when the wrapped expression is `AND`, `OR`, or `NOT` (under any parentheses), which holds in three-valued logic. - Leaves become `NOT pattern`, planned as `AntiSemiApply` (patterns are never `null`), or `NOT scalar`, planned as a regular `Filter`. - Adds a flow test covering mixed pattern and scalar predicates. Written for commit 020cd2d5b583fdf4a7a8d52a09deccb9c496dfd6. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix: refuse an unknown vector similarityFunction at any dimension; GRAPH.MEMORY errors match C
pulls.body: Closes #3256 ## Problem - `similarityFunction` was only checked in `Index::register_fields`, inside `if dimension > 0`. So `CREATE VECTOR INDEX … OPTIONS {dimension:0, similarityFunction:'bogus'}` created an index with `similarityFunction: bogus`, and with a non-zero dimension the refusal had a different message than C's. - `GRAPH.MEMORY` sent its own error strings: `ERR SAMPLES must be …` (C sends no `ERR ` prefix), and different texts for a wrong `USAGE`/`SAMPLES` keyword. ## Fix - `map_to_index_options` (`graph/src/runtime/runtime.rs`) refuses an unknown name at parse time with C's `Invalid vector index configuration` prefix. `ip` is still accepted (Rust supports it; C does not). - `graph_memory` (`src/commands/memory.rs`) sends C's three error lines, from `Graph_Memory` in `cmd_memory.c`. | Command | `main` | This PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | `CREATE VECTOR INDEX … {dimension:0, similarityFunction:'bogus'}` | `Indices created: 1` | `Invalid vector index configuration: unknown similarityFunction 'bogus', …` | `Invalid vector index configuration` | | `CREATE VECTOR INDEX … {dimension:3, similarityFunction:'bogus'}` | `Unknown similarity function 'bogus', …` | `Invalid vector index configuration: unknown similarityFunction 'bogus', …` | `Invalid vector index configuration` | | `CREATE VECTOR INDEX … {dimension:0, similarityFunction:'euclidean'}` | created | created | created | | `GRAPH.MEMORY USAGE g SAMPLES -1` (raw) | `-ERR SAMPLES must be a non-negative integer` | `-SAMPLES must be a non-negative integer` | same as this PR | | `GRAPH.MEMORY USAGE g FOO 3` | `-ERR expected SAMPLES keyword` | `-ERR unknown subcommand 'FOO'. expecting GRAPH.MEMORY USAGE SAMPLES ` | same as this PR | | `GRAPH.MEMORY FOO g` | `-ERR unknown subcommand. Try …` | `-ERR unknown subcommand 'FOO'. expecting GRAPH.MEMORY USAGE ` | same as this PR | Not changed: fulltext `OPTIONS {weight:1, foo:1}` is still refused, as #3091 decided (C accepts it only through a loop bug). ## Tests - `test_index_create.py::test19_index_options_validation`: two bogus-function cases (dimension 2 and 0) must be refused, and `{dimension:0, similarityFunction:'cosine'}` must be accepted. - `test_memory_usage.py::test_invalid_call`: checks the three raw RESP error lines (redis-py strips a leading `ERR `, so the test reads the socket). - Before the fix both fail (`'-ERR SAMPLES must be …' == '-SAMPLES must be …'`, `False == True` for the dimension-0 statement). After: pass. The memory test and the new vector cases also pass on the C module. - Flow (RLTest, release): `test_memory_usage` 16/16, `test_index_create` 18/18, `test_index_delete` 14/14, `test_undo_log` 22/22, `test_index_scans` 38/38. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 495 passed, 1 failed (`cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, pre-existing on macOS, #2922). `cargo fmt --check` and clippy clean on the touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Aligned vector index and `GRAPH.MEMORY` error handling with the C module so malformed commands are refused consistently at any dimension. Previously, an unknown `similarityFunction` was only rejected when the dimension was non-zero, so `{dimension:0, similarityFunction:'bogus'}` silently created an index. Now `map_to_index_options` refuses unknown names at parse time with C's `Invalid vector index configuration` prefix, while still accepting `ip` as a Rust extension. `GRAPH.MEMORY` now sends C's error lines byte for byte: the SAMPLES error no longer carries the `ERR ` prefix, and wrong-keyword errors report the offending subcommand instead of a generic message. Written for commit 2a1198f533d4dfb54c270f88b86759646a21e462. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Vector index creation now accepts `euclidean`, `cosine`, and `ip` similarity function names regardless of capitalization, and rejects unsupported names. * Memory command errors for unknown subcommands and unexpected keywords now use consistent, compatible formatting. Invalid sample-count errors no longer include the `ERR ` prefix. * Vector indexes with zero dimensions can now be created using the `cosine` similarity function.

pulls.title: fix: reject an ORDER BY aggregate whose constants differ from the projection's (max(x % 4.0) vs max(x % 3))
pulls.body: Closes #3236 ## Problem `replace_agg_subtrees` binds an ORDER BY aggregate to a projected aggregate when `raw_exprs_structurally_equal` says the two trees match. Its node comparison `expr_ir_eq` compared constant values only for same-type pairs. Every other pair fell back to comparing the `ExprIR` variant, so `Constant(Int(3))` equalled `Constant(Float(4.0))`, `Constant(String("3"))` and `Constant(Null)`. The same fallback ignored the payloads of `Quantifier`, `ListComprehension`, `Reduce`, `Case`, `ShortestPath` and `CompiledRegex`. `RETURN … max(n.v % 3) AS m ORDER BY max(n.v % 4.0)` therefore sorted by `m` instead of failing as it does in C. Open PR #3011 reuses `raw_exprs_structurally_equal` for non-aggregate ORDER BY expressions, where the same bug would bind `ORDER BY n.v % 4.0` to a projected `n.v % 3`. This fix covers that path too. ## Fix `expr_ir_eq` compares constants with `Value`'s `==` (Cypher equality). This is what C's `AR_EXP_Equals` does with `SIValue_Compare`: `3` still matches `3.0`, as in C. It also compares the payload of every variant that has one. Graph-pattern variants (`Pattern`, `PatternComprehension`, `NestedPlan`) keep the variant-only comparison: their anonymous elements get a fresh name per occurrence, so comparing the patterns would reject identical copies that C accepts. Setup: `UNWIND range(1,6) AS i CREATE (:N {g: i % 2, v: i})`, query `MATCH (n:N) RETURN n.g AS g, max(n.v % 3) AS m ORDER BY ` | `` | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `max(n.v % 4.0)` | rows, sorted by `m` | `failed to map aggregation expression` | `failed to map aggregation expression within ORDER BY clause, please use alias` | | `max(n.v % '3')` | rows, sorted by `m` | error | error | | `max(coalesce(n.x, null))` vs projected `max(coalesce(n.x, 7))` | rows | error | error | | `max(n.v % 3.0)` | rows `[0,2],[1,2]` | same | same | | `max(n.v % 3)` | rows `[0,2],[1,2]` | same | same | ## Tests New `tests/test_e2e.py::test_order_by_aggregate_matches_projection_only_on_equal_constants`: - before (origin/main b033aecc6 build): `AssertionError: Expected an error`, FAILED - after: passed Every case was also checked against the C module on a live server. Other checks (release build, private ports): - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. The one failure, `test_load_csv`, fails the same way on main because the local import folder `/var/lib/FalkorDB/import/` is missing. - Flow: `test_order_by` 9/9, `test_aggregation` 15/15, `test_with_clause` 14/14, `test_comprehension_functions` 25/25, `test_reduce` 14/14, `test_shortest_path` 7/7 - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 495 passed. The 1 failure is the known macOS-only `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922). - `cargo fmt --check` passes, and `cargo clippy -p graph --all-targets` reports no warnings in `binder.rs`. This change is planner-only and runs at bind time, so the runtime is not affected. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the binding of ORDER BY aggregate expressions to projected aggregates so mismatched constants and payloads no longer pass as equal. Previously, `expr_ir_eq` compared only the `ExprIR` variant when types or payloads differed, so `max(n.v % 4.0)` matched a projected `max(n.v % 3)` and the query sorted by the wrong expression instead of failing. Constants are now compared by value equality—`3` still matches `3.0`, as in C—and the payloads of `Quantifier`, `ListComprehension`, `Reduce`, `Case`, `ShortestPath`, and `CompiledRegex` are compared too. - Added `tests/test_e2e.py::test_order_by_aggregate_matches_projection_only_on_equal_constants` covering mismatched and matching constants. Written for commit 9bcf4727d7a9ad3516c29f9c64576add14d039c8. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Fixed aggregate sorting so `ORDER BY` correctly matches aggregates in the selected output when their constant values are equal, including equivalent integer and decimal values. * Sorting still reports an error when the aggregate expressions do not match.

pulls.title: fix: graph.traverse reports the start node when it has a self-loop
pulls.body: Closes #3240 ## Problem `js_traverse_impl` (`graph/src/udf/js_classes.rs`) seeded its BFS `visited` set with the start node, so when the start node is its own neighbour (a self-loop) it was never emitted. ## Fix Do not pre-mark the start node. It is reported once, when an edge reaches it. At the default depth 1 that only changes self-loops; with `maxDepth > 1` a start node on a cycle is reported once at the depth it is reached. `CREATE (a {id:0})-[:R]->(a), (a)-[:R]->(:B {id:1})`, `graph.traverse([a], {direction: d})[0]` ids: | direction | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | outgoing | `[1]` | `[0, 1]` | `[0, 1]` | | incoming | `[]` | `[0]` | `[0]` | | both | `[1]` | `[0, 1]` | `[0, 1]` | Independent of #3084 (self-loop *edge* reported twice in `collect_edges`); the two touch different lines of the same file. ## Tests - New flow test `tests/flow/test_udf.py::test_udf_javascript.test_traverse_self_loop_reports_start_node`. - Before (module built from `main`): FAIL (`[1] == [0, 1]`, `[] == [0]`, `[1] == [0, 1]`). - After: `tests/flow/test_udf.py` 47/47 pass. - `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p graph --all-targets` clean; `cargo test -p graph --lib` 495 pass (only the known macOS `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, #2922); `tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py` 131 pass. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `graph.traverse` so the start node is reported when it has a self-loop. The BFS pre-marked the start node as visited, so a self-loop edge to it was never emitted. It is now reported once, when an edge reaches it, matching C's behavior. At the default depth 1 only self-loops are affected; with `maxDepth > 1` a start node on a cycle is reported once at the depth it is reached. - Bug Fixes - Removes the pre-marking of the start node in the traversal's visited set. - Adds a flow test covering outgoing, incoming, and both directions with a self-loop. Written for commit 9e1e2747767a2a57d72f7c7c3687d10292d3ad63. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Graph traversal now includes the starting node in results when a self-loop or a return edge reaches it, across supported traversal directions.

pulls.title: fix: reload an index on an attribute named `range:x` under that name
pulls.body: Closes #3239 ## Problem Since #2459 the RDB encoder writes each index field's bare attribute name, as C does. The decoder (`decode_index_field`, `src/serializers/mod.rs`) still stripped a `range:` / `vector:` prefix from the name it read, a leftover from before that change. An attribute literally called `range:x` (or `vector:v`) therefore came back after `DEBUG RELOAD` / restart as an index on `x`, and the index stopped serving `n.`range:x``. All released Rust versions (6.0.0+) already write bare names, so no released RDB carries a prefix. ## Fix Use the name as read. The prefixed RediSearch field name is still built by `create_index_sync` when the index is rebuilt. | After `CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.`range:x`)` + `DEBUG RELOAD` | `main` | This PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | `db.indexes()` properties | `[x]` | `[range:x]` | `[range:x]` | | `MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.`range:x` = 1` plan | Label Scan + Filter | Index Scan | Index Scan | ## Tests - New flow test `test_encode_decode.test_19_index_on_attribute_named_like_a_field_prefix` (range index on `range:x`, vector index on `vector:v`, reload, check names and that the index still serves the query). - Before: `['v', 'x'] == ['range:x', 'vector:v']` FAIL, and `'Aggregate / Filter / Node By Label Scan' should contain 'Index Scan'` FAIL. - After: pass. - Flow (RLTest, release): `test_encode_decode` 20/20, `test_rdb_load` 2/2, `test_index_create` 18/18, `test_vecsim` 12/12, `test_constraint` 26/26, `test_graph_copy` 9/9, `test_persistency` 11/11. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. `cargo fmt --check` clean; `clippy --all-targets` has no warnings in touched code. ## Release note RDBs written by pre-6.0 development builds of the Rust engine (before #2459) stored index fields under their RediSearch names (`range:age`). They now load with the index on an attribute of that literal name, which is left unused; re-create those range/vector indexes. Every 6.0.x release, and C, write the bare attribute name and are unaffected. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes RDB reload so an index on an attribute literally named `range:x` or `vector:v` comes back under that name. The decoder in `src/serializers/mod.rs` still stripped `range:`/`vector:` prefixes that the encoder stopped writing in #2459, so such an attribute came back as an index on `x` and stopped serving queries. **Bug Fixes** - Read the index field name verbatim; the prefixed RediSearch field name is still built when the index is rebuilt. - Adds a flow test covering range and vector indexes on prefixed attribute names after `DEBUG RELOAD`, checking the name and that the index still serves the query. Written for commit a9f12a0d95a3e070ab36e54771f6802335db30f8. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Indexes on attributes beginning with `range:` or `vector:` now retain their full names when listed and after an RDB reload. * Queries using a reloaded range index on an attribute beginning with `range:` now work correctly.

pulls.title: fix: shrinking a tensor drops the multi-edge ids of pairs it cuts off
pulls.body: Closes #3246 ## Problem `Tensor::resize` to smaller dimensions resized `m`, `dp`, `dm` and `mt`, but not `me`. `me` is keyed by `compound_key(src, dst)` and is `ME_DIM` rows whatever the node count, so a resize never reaches it. A multi-edge pair outside the new bounds lost its `MULTI_EDGE` sentinel but kept its ids: `iter_edges` still returned them and `edge_count` still counted them. Latent: the only caller that can shrink (`rebuild_derived_matrices` after an RDB load) resizes to `node_cap`, which covers every node id, so Cypher cannot reach it today. ## Fix In the shrink branch, collect the `me` entries whose `compound_key_inverse` falls outside `nrows x ncols` and remove them. One pass over `me`, on a shrink only; the grow path is unchanged. `Tensor::new(8, 8)` with multi pairs (0,1) and (5,6) and single pair (1,2), then `resize(4, 4)`: | | Rust before | Rust after | C | |---|---|---|---| | `iter_edges()` | `(0,1,10) (0,1,11) (1,2,12) (5,6,20) (5,6,21) (5,6,22)` | `(0,1,10) (0,1,11) (1,2,12)` | n/a (no shrink path) | | `edge_count()` | 5 | 3 | n/a | | `multi_pairs()` | 2 | 1 | n/a | ## Tests - New unit test `graph::graphblas::tensor::tests::shrinking_drops_the_multi_edge_ids_of_pairs_it_cuts_off`. - Before the fix: `FAILED … a pair outside the shrunk tensor kept its multi-edge ids` (left had `(5,6,20) (5,6,21) (5,6,22)`). - After: `ok`. - `cargo test -p graph --lib tensor`: 18 passed. `cargo test -p graph --lib`: all pass except the known macOS failure `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` (#2922); `list_literals_parse_in_linear_time` failed once under load and passes on rerun. - `cargo fmt --check` clean; no clippy warnings in `tensor.rs`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `Tensor::resize` so shrinking drops the multi-edge ids of pairs that fall outside the new bounds. `me` is keyed by pair rather than sized by node count, so the shrink resizes never reached it: a cut-off multi pair kept its ids and stayed visible to `iter_edges` and `edge_count` with no forward entry leading to it. **Notes** - Removes the orphaned entries in one pass over `me`, only on the shrink path. - The bug is currently latent: the only shrink caller resizes to `node_cap`, which covers every node id. Written for commit defb47224b05c9b7c2bf2415109c73233ed8b8d1. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Resizing a graph to smaller dimensions now removes multi-edge IDs for pairs that fall outside the new bounds, keeping edge counts consistent.

pulls.title: fix: a range index beside a fulltext index on the same attribute answers queries
pulls.body: Closes #3248 ## Problem An attribute keeps one RediSearch field per index type, in creation order. Every query-node builder in `graph/src/index/mod.rs` (numeric/string range, numeric/string equality, point, array-contains) took the attribute's first field, whatever its type. After `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.s)` then `CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.s)`, the numeric/tag/geo nodes targeted the fulltext field, so every range-index lookup on `n.s` returned no rows (nodes and relationships alike). ## Fix A `range_field(key)` helper returns the attribute's `IndexType::Range` field; the six sites use it instead of `.first()`. | Query (fulltext index created before the range index) | `main` | This PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | `MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.s = 'foo' RETURN n.s` | `[]` | `foo` | `foo` | | `MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.s > 'c' RETURN n.s` | `[]` | `dog`, `foo` | `dog`, `foo` | | `MATCH (n:L {s:'bar'}) RETURN n.s` | `[]` | `bar` | `bar` | | `MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.s IN ['foo','dog'] RETURN n.s` | `[]` | `dog`, `foo` | `dog`, `foo` | | `MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.v >= 2 RETURN n.s` | `[]` | `bar`, `dog` | `bar`, `dog` | ## Tests - New flow tests `test_index_scans.py::test_42_range_index_beside_fulltext_index` (nodes) and `test_edge_index_scans.py::test29_range_index_beside_fulltext_index` (relationships): string and numeric equality, range, inline map and `IN`, plus a fulltext query on the same attribute. - Before the fix: both fail, every lookup `[] == [...]`. - After: 2/2 pass. They also pass on the C module. - Flow suites (RLTest, release): `test_index_scans` 39/39, `test_edge_index_scans` 31/31, `test_index_create` 18/18, `test_index_updates` 11/11, `test_edge_index_updates` 6/6, `test_index_delete` 14/14, `test_fulltext_query` 5/5. - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed. `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 495 passed, 1 failed (`cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored`, pre-existing on macOS, #2922). `cargo fmt --check` and clippy clean on the touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes range-index lookups (numeric/string equality, range, geo, tag, array-contains) returning empty results when an attribute also has a fulltext index. Query-node builders were targeting the attribute's first field regardless of its index type, so a fulltext index created first made every range lookup miss. Adds a `range_field(key)` helper that selects the `IndexType::Range` field and uses it in all six query-node builders in `graph/src/index/mod.rs`. Closes #3248. **Tests** - New flow tests for nodes and relationships cover string/numeric equality, range, inline map, and `IN` queries on an attribute with both index types. - Verified that fulltext queries on the same attribute still return rows. Written for commit 847b4a8930f622e59e8074993e73862edc36b34f. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Queries now select the appropriate range index when an attribute also has a full-text or vector index, improving results for equality, range, pattern, `IN`, geo-point, and array-contains queries. * Queries return no results when an attribute has no suitable range index. * **Tests** * Added coverage for queries using range and full-text indexes on the same attributes.

pulls.title: fix: a refused GRAPH.EFFECT buffer no longer keeps its index DDL
pulls.body: Closes #3023 ## Problem When `GRAPH.EFFECT` refuses a buffer, `MvccGraph::rollback` drops the private version. Index DDL survived that rollback. The `Indexer` map is shared by every MVCC version, so a `CREATE_INDEX` or `DROP_INDEX` that ran before the refusing record stayed applied, while everything else in the buffer was rolled back. ## Fix This implements option 1 from the issue. `apply_effects` still verifies each `CREATE_INDEX` / `DROP_INDEX` record in place: schema and attribute ids, label, index type. It then queues the statement instead of running it. The queue runs in record order after all records have applied and `Graph::validate` has passed, before `commit_index`. If a data record refuses the buffer, no DDL has run yet. Deferring the DDL created a problem with population. `docs` only collects documents for indexes that already exist, so an entity the buffer writes now has to reach a newly created index through population. Population reads the **committed** graph, and that graph lacks the buffer's writes until `MvccGraph::commit` publishes the version. To handle this, `populate_index` takes an optional `published_at` version, and the first batch reschedules until the committed graph reaches it. This uses the same 1 ms reschedule as the existing "graph not yet committed" path. The apply path uses the new `Graph::create_index_populated_at` / `drop_index_populated_at`, which pass `Some(g.version)`. `create_index` / `drop_index` pass `None`, so the primary's `CREATE INDEX` / `DROP INDEX` behave as before. Without the gate, a 50k-node buffer had 0 of its nodes in the index. The same race already exists on `main` when an entity comes before its `CREATE_INDEX` in a buffer, and the new test hits it. | Case (client-sent `GRAPH.EFFECT`) | `main` | This PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | `[CREATE_INDEX A(zz), CREATE_NODE 0]`, node 0 live → refused | `db.indexes()` lists `A [zz]` | `db.indexes()` empty | n/a: C cannot read v3 (logs `GRAPH.EFFECT version mismatch expected version <= 2 got: 3` and exits) | | `[DROP_INDEX A(zz), CREATE_NODE 0]` on an indexed graph → refused | index gone | index still there, still answers `n.zz = 1` | n/a | | `[CREATE_NODE ×50000 :F, CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX F(body)]` → accepted | 0 of 50000 indexed | 50000 indexed | n/a | | same, index record first | 50000 | 50000 | n/a | One case remains, also noted in a comment in `apply_effects`. If a deferred DDL statement is refused itself (index already exists, drop of a missing index), the DDL statements before it in the same buffer stay applied. A refusal by any data record is now fully undone. Covering that last case needs option 2 (undo log) or option 3 (per-version `Indexer`). ## Tests New class `testEffects_07_RefusedBufferIndexDDL` in `tests/flow/test_effects_ddl.py`. The payloads are captured from the replica's MONITOR feed for a statement run on a source graph with the same schema numbering, then spliced with a `CREATE_NODE 0` that the target refuses as already live. - `test01_a_refused_create_index_is_not_kept` - `main`: FAIL, `db.indexes()` = `[['A', ['zz'], …]] == []` - this PR: PASS - `test02_a_refused_drop_index_is_not_kept` - `main`: FAIL, `[] == [['A', ['zz'], …]]` - this PR: PASS - `test03_an_accepted_buffer_indexes_what_it_created` (both record orders, 50k nodes) - `main`: FAIL, `[[0]] == [[50000]]` (node first) - this PR with the deferral but **without** the population gate: FAIL in both orders - this PR: PASS Other runs (release build, RLTest): - `test_effects_{batch,commands,commit,ddl,opcodes,shapes,topology,values,wire}`: 4/7/4/21/12/22/3/9/14, all pass - `test_index_{create,delete,scans,updates}`: 18/14/38/11, all pass - `test_replication` 2/2, `test_replication_states` 1/1, `test_aof` 1/1 - `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py`: 131 passed - `cargo test -p graph --lib`: 495 passed. The 1 failure is the known `cap_at_or_above_batch_size_is_ignored` on macOS (#2922). - `cargo fmt --check` is clean, and `clippy -p graph --all-targets` adds no warnings in touched code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #3023: a refused `GRAPH.EFFECT` buffer no longer keeps its index DDL. Index DDL is now verified in place but queued and run only after all records apply and `Graph::validate` passes, in record order. - Background index population now waits for the buffer's version to be committed, so entities the buffer wrote reach indexes the same buffer created. Without this gate, a 50k-node buffer indexed 0 of its nodes. - Deferred index DDL and index commits run through the shared `commit_index_docs` path after validation. - The primary's `CREATE INDEX` / `DROP INDEX` path is unchanged. - Adds tests for refused `CREATE_INDEX` / `DROP_INDEX` and for accepted buffers indexing what they created in both record orders. **Remaining gap**: a DDL statement that is itself refused still leaves the DDL statements before it applied. Covering that needs an undo log or a per-version index map. Written for commit 4642405ba7b664f1ba1a8fc31f87f5847c86236c. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Index creation and removal are now applied only when the corresponding batch of changes is accepted, preventing refused batches from leaving index changes behind. * Accepted batches apply index changes consistently whether index creation is recorded before or after node creation. * Background index population waits until the relevant graph version is available, improving consistency of indexed results.

pulls.title: fix: slow log no longer panics on a multi-byte character at byte 2048
pulls.body: Closes #3233 ## Problem The slow log sliced the query and parameter text at byte 2048 (`entry_hash` and `truncate` in `src/slow_log.rs`). Slicing a `&str` inside a multi-byte character panics, so a query (or `CYPHER` parameter string) longer than 2048 bytes that ran past the 10 ms threshold, with a character straddling byte 2048, killed the server: ``` FalkorDB panic: panicked at src/slow_log.rs:49:10: end byte index 2048 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'é' (bytes 2047..2049 of string) ``` ## Fix A `prefix` helper returns the longest prefix of at most 2048 bytes that ends on a char boundary (`str::floor_char_boundary`, already used in the lexer). `entry_hash` hashes that prefix and `truncate` stores it plus `...`. Nothing else in `src/` slices text by a byte limit unsafely: `telemetry.rs` cuts by `char_indices`, `divergence_guard.rs::clip` walks to a boundary, and the `graph_core.rs` slices are at NUL / params offsets. Query: 2050 bytes, `é` at bytes 2047..2049, `UNWIND range(1, 2000000) …` so it is logged. | | `main` | This PR | C | |---|---|---|---| | query answers | no, server panics and exits | yes | yes | | `GRAPH.SLOWLOG` query text | — | 2047 bytes + `...` (2050 bytes, valid UTF-8) | 2048 bytes + `...` (2051 bytes, ends `\xc3...`: half of `é`, invalid UTF-8) | | same with the character in a `CYPHER p='…'` prefix | panics at `slow_log.rs:32` | params 2047 bytes + `...` | 2048 bytes + `...`, invalid UTF-8 | The stored text differs from C only where C stores a broken character; we drop the whole character (up to 3 bytes fewer) and keep the reply valid UTF-8. Matching C byte for byte would mean storing and returning non-UTF-8 bytes. Unchanged: C also appends `...` to text that is exactly 2048 bytes long, which Rust did not do before and still does not. ## Tests - New flow test `test_slowlog.py::test07_truncate_on_char_boundary`: for `é`, `€` and `😀` straddling byte 2048, in the query text and in the parameters, it checks the server answers and `GRAPH.SLOWLOG` holds both entries, cut before the character. - Before the fix (release build of `main`): fails, `Connection closed by server`, the server process is gone. - After: passes; `test_slowlog.py` 7/7. - No Rust unit test: the `falkordb-rs` crate's test binary aborts at start (`the Redis Allocator isn't available`), since the module's global allocator is Redis's, so `src/` has no runnable unit tests. - `cargo fmt --check` clean, no clippy warnings in `slow_log.rs`, `cargo test -p graph --lib` 495 passed (only the known #2922 failure), `pytest tests/test_e2e.py tests/test_functions.py` 131 passed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a server panic when the slow log truncated a query or `CYPHER` parameter string longer than 2048 bytes whose multi-byte character straddled byte 2048; slicing the `&str` at that byte panicked and took down the server. Truncation and the dedup hash now cut at the nearest character boundary at or below 2048 bytes via `str::floor_char_boundary`, so the whole character is dropped and stored text stays valid UTF-8. This differs from C only where C stores a broken character; otherwise behavior matches, including not appending `...` to text that is exactly 2048 bytes. Adds a flow test covering `é`, `€`, and `😀` straddling byte 2048 in both the query text and the parameters. Closes #3233. Written for commit be7a3ae20320f44c8025faad721a2cb1c84920da. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Slow-log entries now truncate long query text and CYPHER parameter values at valid character boundaries, preventing multibyte characters from being split or corrupted. * Truncated values end with an ellipsis. Long queries containing multibyte characters are also handled safely when generating query hashes.

Updates `libc` from 0.2.189 to 0.2.190
Release notes

Sourced from libc's releases.

0.2.190

There is now a single config for enabling 64-bit time_t: libc_unstable_time64. This can be set unconditionally; it opts in to 64-bit time_t on the following platforms that use 32-bit by default:

  • 32-bit Linux-GNU
  • 32-bit Linux-uClibc
  • 32-bit Linux-musl. Note that setting this flag also enables some other changes that happend in musl v1.2.
  • 32-bit Windows-GNU
  • ESP-IDF (all targets with this environment are 32-bit)

Most other 32-bit platforms are either already using 64-bit time_t, or are considered legacy and will not be gaining support from their upstream maintainers.

You can enable this using RUSTFLAGS:

RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=libc_unstable_time64' cargo ...

Note that there may still be some changes to features gated by this config option, hence "unstable" in its name. In the near future we will rename it to just libc_time64. Until then, please test it out and report any bugs you find!

Support

  • Add initial support for HelenOS (#4355)

Added

We are slowly filling out the Default implementations, to reduce the need for mem::zeroed() in user code:

  • Unix: Implement Default for a number of structs, especially on Apple platforms (#5576)
  • Linux, NetBSD: Give statvfs a Default impl (#5583)
  • Linux: Add Default to a linux/can.rs structs (#5257)

Other additions:

  • Expose the libc_unstable_time64 cfg (#5411)
  • Android, Glibc: Add pthread_gettid_np (#5359)
  • Android: Add RTLD_NEXT (#5323)
  • Android: Add reuseport BPF socket options (#5366)
  • Apple: Add TCP header flags, options and SACK limits (#5358)

pulls.title: fix(runtime): keep grouping keys bound after accumulator unbind (#3150)
pulls.body:
In `AggregateOp::next`, internal aggregate accumulator variables are unbound so they don't leak to downstream operators. The binder can assign an accumulator the same slot ID as a grouping key or an aggregate output (slot ID reuse across scopes). When that slot held a NULL grouping key, unbinding it left the column unbound, `BatchBuilder::finish` emitted `Column::Unbound`, and `src/reply.rs` panicked on `value_at().unwrap()`.

## Changes

- `graph/src/runtime/ops/aggregate.rs`: unbind accumulator slots right after the aggregate outputs are evaluated, then write the pre-projection values, the grouping keys (`acc.merge(&key)`) and the aggregate outputs, in that order. Every slot an accumulator shares is written after the unbind, so NULL keys survive. Accumulators that collide with nothing stay unbound as before.
- This also fixes a key-ordering bug in an earlier revision of this PR, where a per-key re-bind loop mixed input-scope and output-scope slot IDs (`WITH 1 AS a, 2 AS b RETURN b AS x, a AS y, count(*)` returned `x=1`).
- `src/reply.rs`: `value_at().unwrap_or(Value::Null)` as defense in depth, so one bad column can't take down the server.

## Tests

- `test10_null_preceding_aggregate`: the #3150 cases (`RETURN null AS x, count(1)`, `collect`, missing property before an aggregate).
- `test11_null_key_after_aggregate`: NULL key after an aggregate through a `WITH ... AS hops` slot (plain, variable-length path, `algo.SSpaths`), cases that already passed, grouping-key ordering, and the OPTIONAL MATCH + `collect()` shape from the issue thread.
- `TEST="tests/flow/test_null_handling" ./flow.sh`: 11/11 pass locally. test11 fails on the previous revision of this branch.
- Aggregation, WITH and OPTIONAL MATCH flow files pass; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` are clean.

Fixes #3150

pulls.title: perf(constraint): look UNIQUE keys up in the supporting index
pulls.body: ## What this PR does UNIQUE enforcement looks the keys of a commit up in the constraint's supporting range index. It no longer scans the label once per affected entity. The second commit checks only the entities whose key or membership the commit can change. This applies to every commit that touches an entity under a UNIQUE constraint. MANDATORY constraints do not change. Fixes #2995. It is an alternative to #2997, and keeps the one-pass check of #2997 as its fallback. ## Why we need this On `main`, a UNIQUE check costs one pass over the whole label per affected entity (#2995). A write of one entity costs O(label size). A batch of k rows costs O(k x label size). - One `CREATE` takes 20.9 ms at 100,000 nodes and 0.76 ms at 1,000 nodes. - A `SET` of an unconstrained property costs the same, because every touched entity is checked. - Loading 30,000 nodes in three 10,000-row queries takes 111 s. ## Merge order The index lookup is exact only while the index holds every entity with its current values. Two open bugs break that on `main`, so this PR depends on #3086 and #3098: - #3069, fixed by #3086: a field added to an index during its population stays empty while the index reports OPERATIONAL. - #3095, fixed by #3098: a population batch can overwrite a newer document or add a deleted entity back. Without them, a lookup can miss an existing key, and a duplicate gets in. `test_effects_ddl.py::testEffects_06_ConstraintSettlingRaces::test01` shows it: it fails on this PR alone and passes with #3086 and #3098 under it. Merge this PR after both. ## Root cause Line numbers are for `main` at `ec2448f`. - `Pending::enforce_constraints` (`graph/src/runtime/pending.rs:1258`) calls `check_node_constraint` (`:1355`) and `check_edge_constraint` (`:1425`). - For each affected entity, `check_node_constraint` builds a map of the composite keys of the whole label (`:1397`, loop at `:1400`). `check_edge_constraint` does the same per relationship type (`:1470`, loop at `:1473`). - The check runs for every touched entity, including entities whose constrained properties the commit did not change. ## The fix - The commit keys every entity it checks into one map. Two entities of the commit with one key fail at once. - The other entities are looked up in the supporting range index, 1,024 keys per RediSearch query. The query is a union of rows, and each row is an intersection of one exact match per property. - Each hit is read back from the graph and compared by the same composite key. A hit that matches only as `f64` does not count. Neither does the stale document of an entity that this commit changed, deleted or unlabelled. - The lookup runs only while the index is OPERATIONAL, and only for values that the index stores exactly. These are booleans, integers up to 2^53, finite floats, and non-empty strings below the 4,096-byte tag limit. - In every other case, one pass over the label checks all keys of the commit at once, as #2997 does. The pass also runs when a commit carries more keys than a quarter of the graph's entities. - Debug builds run both checks and assert that they agree. - The second commit skips the UNIQUE check for an entity whose key cannot change. A new duplicate needs at least one entity that the commit created, gave the label, or set a constrained property on. ## Behavior change - A duplicate pair that already exists no longer fails an unrelated `SET` on one of its entities. Such a pair can exist when two equal keys are written while the constraint is still validating. - A `SET` of a constrained property is still checked against every other member, with the full composite key. A swap is judged by the full keys of both entities. - C FalkorDB and #2997 still reject that unrelated `SET`. ## Tests New flow tests, class `testUniqueConstraintIndexLookup` in `tests/flow/test_constraint.py`: - `test01_bulk_load`: 20,000 nodes in one query under UNIQUE, within 10 s. Stock `main` fails it: 47.97 s. - `test02_node_duplicates`: duplicates of an existing node, within one query, by `SET`, by `MERGE`, by a new label. It checks 1, 500 and 10,000 keys, which covers the lookup and the label pass. Swaps, reuse of a freed value in one query, and `'10'` against `10` must pass. - `test03_edge_duplicates`: the same cases for relationships. - `test04_partial_composite_change`: a `SET` of one property of a composite key is judged by the whole key. Flow set of 34 files, services mode, with a replica for the files that need one: | Build | Passed | Failed | |---|---|---| | Stock `main` | 515 of 515 | none | | This PR alone | 518 of 519 | `test_effects_ddl` class 06 `test01`: "a duplicate must be rejected" | | This PR on #3086 and #3098 | 521 of 521 | none | | The same, debug assertions on | 521 of 521 | none; the lookup and the label pass agreed on every check | | The same, plus the open-scan PR | 522 of 522 | none | ## Measurements Write latency on a label of 1k, 10k, 30k and 100k nodes with UNIQUE `(id)`. The nodes were loaded first, then the index and the constraint were created. Medians of 30 single writes and of 5 batches, in ms: | Write | Stock `main` | This PR | This PR on #3086 and #3098 | |---|---|---|---| | One `CREATE` | 0.76, 2.16, 4.93, 20.9 | 0.41, 0.33, 0.38, 0.29 | 0.39, 0.28, 0.33, 0.29 | | `MATCH` by id, then `SET` of another property | 0.48, 1.86, 4.84, 19.5 | 0.33, 0.18, 0.21, 0.29 | 0.26, 0.25, 0.22, 0.37 | | One `UNWIND` of 100 `CREATE` | 17.3, 155, 469, 1,850 | 0.48, 0.47, 0.75, 0.66 | 0.71, 0.64, 0.48, 0.57 | The same writes, with the constraint created before the load of 10k-row queries. Stock `main` timed out on the 100k load: one 10k-row query ran over 120 s. The cells for the patched builds give the median of 3 runs: | Write | Stock `main` | This PR | This PR on #3086 and #3098 | |---|---|---|---| | One `CREATE` | 0.69, 2.03, 6.36, timed out | 0.42, 0.34, 0.38, 0.38 | 0.42, 0.49, 0.44, 0.33 | | `MATCH` by id, then `SET` of another property | 0.45, 1.92, 6.00, timed out | 0.26, 0.36, 0.29, 0.25 | 0.31, 0.33, 0.40, 0.25 | | One `UNWIND` of 100 `CREATE` | 18.4, 140, 476, timed out | 0.77, 0.58, 0.71, 0.58 | 0.60, 0.66, 0.79, 0.72 | Without a constraint, stock `main` takes 0.24 to 0.37 ms for one `CREATE` at every size. Bulk load under UNIQUE, in 10k-row queries: | Nodes | Stock `main` | This PR | This PR on #3086 and #3098 | |---|---|---|---| | 30,000 | 111 s: 16.8, 34.0 and 60.3 s per query | 0.08 s | 0.06 s | | 100,000 | not run | 0.26 s | 0.21 s | A `CALL {}` subquery sets `n.y` on each row of an index scan. A second client runs `RESTORE` every 100 ms, and a third sends PING every 20 ms. Both builds carry the open-scan PR (`fix/index-scan-read-locks-across-commit`): without it, this shape deadlocks against `RESTORE` on `main`. Two runs of 15 s each: | Scan | `main` with the open-scan PR | The same, plus #3086, #3098 and this PR | |---|---|---| | 3,000 nodes, UNIQUE on the scanned key: CALL p50; PING p99 | 1,038 and 1,084 ms; 1,196 and 1,214 ms | 9.2 and 12.0 ms; 13.0 and 16.8 ms | | 20,000 nodes, UNIQUE | the query times out at 30 s; one PING waits 30.0 s | 63 and 84 ms; 63 and 143 ms | | 20,000 nodes, no constraint, for reference | 49 and 76 ms; 41 and 99 ms | 66 and 71 ms; 58 and 93 ms | Environment: Apple silicon, Docker linux/arm64 VM with 15 CPUs and 12 GB. Release `falkordb.so` from each branch, built with the builder stage of `build/runtime/Dockerfile`, in the `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` image (Redis 8.10.2). Module arguments: `TIMEOUT_DEFAULT 30000 TIMEOUT_MAX 60000 RESULTSET_SIZE -1 MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES 200 NODE_CREATION_BUFFER 1024 CACHE_SIZE 10 QUERY_MEM_CAPACITY 268435456 ASYNC_DELETE no THREAD_COUNT 4`. Redis arguments: `--maxmemory 6gb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --save '' --appendonly no`. Each run started a new server. Other containers on the host used about 2 of the 15 CPUs. ## Repro On stock `main`, each write to a large label with a UNIQUE constraint costs a full pass over the label: ``` redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0, 99999) AS i CREATE (:Node {id: 'k' + toString(i)})" redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:Node) ON (n.id)" redis-cli GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE g UNIQUE NODE Node PROPERTIES 1 id # wait until CALL db.constraints() reports OPERATIONAL redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1, 100) AS j CREATE (:Node {id: 'new' + toString(j)})" ``` The last query takes about 1.8 s on stock `main` and under 1 ms with this PR. ## Not covered - Some values always take the label pass: lists, points, temporal values, NaN and infinities. Integers above 2^53 do too, and so do empty strings and strings of 4,096 encoded bytes or more. - A UNIQUE write during an index population takes the label pass, because the index is not OPERATIONAL. - The switch point, a quarter of the entities, comes from one measurement: about 0.4 µs per key lookup against 0.1 µs per scanned entity. - The key equality of the tag stays as it is: `1` and `1.0` are two keys (#2774). - The open-scan PR (`fix/index-scan-read-locks-across-commit`) replaces `IndexResultsIter::new` and `EdgeTripleIter::new`. The second of the two PRs to merge changes the two calls here to `IndexResultsIter::open(iter, index, node_result)` and `IndexResultsIter::open(iter, index, edge_result)`. ## Commits - `perf(constraint): look UNIQUE keys up in the supporting index` - `perf(constraint): check UNIQUE only for entities whose key can change` --- ## Summary by cubic UNIQUE constraint enforcement now looks up a commit's keys in the supporting range index instead of scanning the whole label once per affected entity. This cuts write latency on large labels from O(label size) to O(keys) per commit and skips the check for entities whose key or membership the commit cannot change. **Behavior change** - An unrelated `SET` on an entity no longer triggers a label scan, so a pre-existing duplicate pair no longer fails it. - The check still runs on every entity whose key or membership the commit can change; swaps and partial composite changes are judged by the full key. - The index lookup only applies when the index is fully populated and the values are stored exactly; otherwise the label is scanned as before. **Merge order** - Requires #3086 and #3098 to be exact: without them the lookup can miss existing keys during index population. Written for commit 0d93649961063a935d54135971c9f59e567c3e04. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(index): read the pending count without the pending-slots mutex
pulls.body: ## What this PR does `Index::pending_count` now reads an atomic copy of the current-generation pending count. Every change of that count under the pending-slots mutex also stores it in the atomic. The other pending-slot functions do not change. This applies to every build. Only the readers of `pending_count` change: the RDB encoder, `CALL db.indexes()` and the planner's index checks. ## Why we need this A BGSAVE child can block forever on the pending-slots mutex of an index. BGSAVE then never finishes, and a replica that needs a full sync waits for it. Each later BGSAVE fails with `Background save already in progress`. The hang needs a fork while another thread holds the mutex. That window is short, so the hang is rare. When it occurs, nothing recovers from it without a restart. ## Root cause Line numbers are for `main` at `ec2448f`. - The RDB encoder runs in the BGSAVE child. `Schema::from_graph` (`src/serializers/mod.rs:708`) calls `Indexer::index_info` (`graph/src/index/indexer.rs:793`), which reads `pending_count` of every index (`:805`). - `Index::pending_count` locks `pending_slots`, a `parking_lot::Mutex` (`graph/src/index/mod.rs:2164`). - Other threads take that mutex all the time. Population workers take it for every ticket (`increment_pending_for_generation` at `:2110`, `try_decrement_pending_for_generation` at `:2128`). Query threads take it when the planner checks an index (`graph/src/index/indexer.rs:445`, `:459`). - `fork` copies only the calling thread. A mutex that another thread holds at that moment stays locked in the child, and no thread can release it. The code already states the intent. `index_info` says "Lock-free snapshot: safe to call from a BGSAVE fork child" (`indexer.rs:794-795`). `graph_rdb_save` bypasses the graph `RwLock` for the same reason (`src/redis_type.rs:190-191`). ## The fix - `Index` gets `current_pending: Arc`. Clones of the `Index` share it, as they share `pending_slots`. - `bump_id`, `increment_pending_for_generation` and `try_decrement_pending_for_generation` store the new current-generation count into it while they hold the mutex. - `pending_count` loads it with `Ordering::Relaxed` and takes no lock. The count is a status value, and no reader orders other memory accesses on it. ## Tests - No new flow test. A test would need a fork at the instant another thread holds the mutex, which a flow test cannot arrange. - The flow set of 34 files ran in services mode, with a replica for the files that need one. Stock `main` and this branch both passed 515 of 515 tests. ## Measurements | Check | Stock `main` | This PR | |---|---|---| | BGSAVE while one thread holds the pending-slots mutex (fault injection, below) | the child blocks in `futex_wait`; `rdb_bgsave_in_progress:1` after 30 s | BGSAVE finishes at once | | 2,600 BGSAVE runs while 8 clients loop `CALL db.indexes()` on 64 or 256 indexes | 2,600 of 2,600 finish | not run | - The second row shows that load alone rarely opens the window. Each BGSAVE child finished on stock `main`. - In the first row, the stock child has this stack: `RawMutex::lock_slow`, `Indexer::index_info`, `Graph::index_info`, `encode_graph`, `rdb_save_graph_key`, `graph_rdb_save`, `rdbSaveObject`, then Redis's `rdbSaveBackground`. Environment: Apple silicon, Docker linux/arm64 VM with 15 CPUs. Release `falkordb.so` from each branch, built with the builder stage of `build/runtime/Dockerfile`, in the `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` image (Redis 8.10.2). The first row ran with the default module arguments. The second row ran with `TIMEOUT_DEFAULT 30000 TIMEOUT_MAX 60000 RESULTSET_SIZE -1 MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES 200 NODE_CREATION_BUFFER 1024 CACHE_SIZE 10 QUERY_MEM_CAPACITY 268435456 ASYNC_DELETE no THREAD_COUNT 4`: 2,300 runs on all CPUs and 300 runs pinned to one CPU. ## Repro: setup A fork has to land while another thread holds the mutex. This repro makes that certain: it patches one instruction of the running server, so that a population worker spins inside the mutex. The patch runs as root in a sidecar container that shares the server's PID namespace and has `SYS_PTRACE`. On the arm64 build of `ec2448f`, the first instruction after the lock in `Indexer::release_population_ticket` is at offset `0x38c188`: `ldr x8, [x21, #24]`, bytes `a8 0e 40 f9`. On this branch it is at `0x38c1a8`. ## Repro: procedure 1. Find the offset for your `falkordb.so` with `objdump -d`: the first instruction after the lock in `Indexer::release_population_ticket`. 2. Run `redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1, 100) AS i CREATE (:P {v: i})"`. 3. Run the script below with the server's PID and the offset. It writes `b .` (`00 00 00 14`) over that instruction through `/proc//mem`. 4. Run `redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:P) ON (n.v)"`. The population worker spins at the patched instruction with the mutex held. 5. Run `redis-cli BGSAVE`, then `redis-cli INFO persistence` every few seconds. On stock `main`, `rdb_bgsave_in_progress` stays at `1`. With this PR it returns to `0` at once. ```python import sys off = int(sys.argv[2], 16) base = None for line in open(f"/proc/{sys.argv[1]}/maps"): f = line.split() if len(f) >= 6 and f[5].endswith("/falkordb.so") and int(f[2], 16) == 0: base = int(f[0].split("-")[0], 16) break with open(f"/proc/{sys.argv[1]}/mem", "r+b", buffering=0) as mem: mem.seek(base + off) assert mem.read(4) == bytes.fromhex("a80e40f9") mem.seek(base + off) mem.write(bytes.fromhex("00000014")) ``` ## Repro with a debugger On a debug build, a debugger in non-stop mode does the same job. Stop the population thread on a line inside `try_decrement_pending_for_generation`, after the lock. Run BGSAVE while the thread is stopped. --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents a BGSAVE child from hanging forever by making `Index::pending_count` read an atomic copy of the pending count instead of taking the pending-slots mutex. The count is stored in an `Arc` whenever it changes under the mutex; `pending_count` now loads it with relaxed ordering and does not lock. Since `fork` copies only the calling thread, a child can inherit a mutex that remains locked forever; this removes that failure mode from BGSAVE and any other reader of the pending count. Written for commit c3ec97513fd6be9f4383eb21d8be3d6d2da81dd4. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance** * Checking the current amount of pending work now avoids waiting for a bookkeeping lock, which can reduce coordination overhead during index updates. Generation-specific counts and handling of work from older generations remain unchanged, preserving existing count behavior while making this common check more efficient.

pulls.title: fix(index): release open index scans before commit; read the pending count without the mutex
pulls.body:
Fixes #3226

## What this PR does

Two fixes for lock hazards around the indexes that RediSearch backs.

- Before a query takes the GIL to commit, it reads every RediSearch query that it still has open to the end and frees it. The scan then yields the buffered rest as before. `LIMIT` also drops its input once the limit is met, so a `LIMIT k` write frees its scan before the commit and buffers nothing.
- `Index::pending_count` reads an atomic copy of the current-generation pending count. A BGSAVE child then never takes the pending-slots mutex.

This applies to the default build. Queries that hold no open index scan at commit time do not change. Of the pending-slot functions, only the readers of `pending_count` change: the RDB encoder, `CALL db.indexes()` and the planner's index checks.

## Why we need this

On `main`, a write query whose index scan is still open at commit time stops the server or aborts it. Two common shapes keep a scan open: an index scan below `LIMIT`, and an index scan that feeds a `CALL {}` subquery.

- The server stops answering when another client runs a command that needs the RediSearch write lock under the GIL. `RESTORE` of a graph with indexes is one such command. The writer holds the RediSearch read locks and waits for the GIL. The GIL holder waits for the RediSearch write lock.
- The server aborts when the query writes the property that its scan reads. The index write fails the assertion `attempted to upgrade a spec read lock to a write lock`.

A BGSAVE child can also block forever on the pending-slots mutex of an index. BGSAVE then never finishes, and a replica that needs a full sync waits for it. Each later BGSAVE fails with `Background save already in progress`. The window is short, so the hang is rare. When it occurs, nothing recovers from it without a restart.

## Root cause: open index scans at commit

Line numbers are for `main` at `ec2448f`, with `deps/RediSearch` at `ea1a6f4`.

- An open RediSearch iterator holds two read locks. `handleIterCommon` takes the global `RWLOCK` read lock and the spec read lock (`deps/RediSearch/src/redisearch_api.c:904-905`). Only `RediSearch_ResultsIteratorFree` releases them (`:1045`).
- `IndexResultsIter` (`graph/src/index/mod.rs:268`), `EdgeTripleIter` (`:355`) and `ScoredEdgeTripleIter` (`:419`) free the iterator only in `Drop` (`:336`, `:406`, `:472`).
- `LimitOp::next` (`graph/src/runtime/ops/limit.rs:49`) keeps its child after the limit is met (`:72`, `:83`). The scan below stays open until the query ends.
- A `CALL {}` subquery commits once per input batch while the outer scan is still open.
- `CommitOp` commits the pending changes (`graph/src/runtime/ops/commit.rs:89`). It then takes the GIL in `upgrade_to_write` (`:96`, `src/query_session.rs:221`, `escalate` at `:242`). Last, it writes the deferred index changes (`commit.rs:103`).
- `IndexSpec_LockWrite` finds the read lock of the same thread on that spec and aborts (`deps/RediSearch/src/spec.c:2304`).

## Root cause: pending count in the BGSAVE child

- The RDB encoder runs in the BGSAVE child. `Schema::from_graph` (`src/serializers/mod.rs:708`) calls `Indexer::index_info` (`graph/src/index/indexer.rs:793`), which reads `pending_count` of every index (`:805`).
- `Index::pending_count` locks `pending_slots`, a `parking_lot::Mutex` (`graph/src/index/mod.rs:2164`).
- Other threads take that mutex all the time. Population workers take it for every ticket (`increment_pending_for_generation` at `:2110`, `try_decrement_pending_for_generation` at `:2128`). Query threads take it when the planner checks an index (`graph/src/index/indexer.rs:445`, `:459`).
- `fork` copies only the calling thread. A mutex that another thread holds at that moment stays locked in the child, and no thread can release it.

The code already states the intent. `index_info` says "Lock-free snapshot: safe to call from a BGSAVE fork child" (`indexer.rs:794-795`). `graph_rdb_save` bypasses the graph `RwLock` for the same reason (`src/redis_type.rs:190-191`).

## The fix

Open index scans:

- Every RediSearch iterator is now an `OpenQuery` behind `Rc<RefCell<..>>`. A weak reference to it goes into the thread-local list `OPEN_QUERIES`.
- `release_open_queries()` reads each open query of the calling thread to its end, buffers the rest of its results and frees the C iterator. The iterator then yields from the buffer.
- A query that reaches its end frees its C iterator at once, not when the operator tree drops it.
- `QuerySession::upgrade_to_write` calls `release_open_queries()` on every call, before it takes the GIL. A writer can open new scans between two commits, and an inline session starts as a writer.
- `abandon_write` calls it before the index resync, which also writes the index.
- `LimitOp` replaces its child with an empty op once the limit is met. The child is never pulled again, and a `CALL {}` subquery builds a new op tree for each input batch.

Pending count:

- `Index` gets `current_pending: Arc<AtomicI32>`. Clones of the `Index` share it, as they share `pending_slots`.
- `bump_id`, `increment_pending_for_generation` and `try_decrement_pending_for_generation` store the new current-generation count into it while they hold the mutex.
- `pending_count` loads it with `Ordering::Relaxed` and takes no lock. The count is a status value, and no reader orders other memory accesses on it.

## Tests

- New flow test `test_index_updates.py::test13_write_to_index_scanned_under_limit`. It writes the scanned property under `LIMIT 10`, then in a `CALL {}` subquery over 2,000 rows. It checks the returned counts and the indexed values. On stock `main`, the server aborts at the first query of the new test.
- The pending count has no new flow test. A test would need a fork at the instant another thread holds the mutex, which a flow test cannot arrange.
- The flow set below ran in services mode, with a replica for the files that need one. Stock `main` passed 515 of 515 tests. With both fixes, this branch passed 516 of 516.
- `test_effects_ddl.py::testEffects_06_ConstraintSettlingRaces::test02` is a known flake that the file documents. In three reruns of that file, the open-scan fix alone passed 3 of 3. Stock `main` failed 2 of 3 with the same assertion.

Flow files: `test_index_scans`, `test_index_updates`, `test_edge_index_scans`, `test_edge_index_updates`, `test_fulltext_query`, `test_call_subquery`, `test_foreach`, `test_graph_merge`, `test_with_clause`, `test_vecsim`, `test_undo_log`, `test_multi_exec`, `test_index_create`, `test_index_delete`, `test_optimizations_plan`, `test_concurrent_query`, `test_results`, `test_order_by`, `test_union`, `test_unwind_clause`, `test_profile`. With a replica: `test_constraint`, `test_ro_query`, `test_replication`, `test_effects_commit`, `test_effects_ddl`, `test_persistency`, `test_graph_deletion`, `test_rdb_load`, `test_stress`, `test_graph_copy`, `test_memory_usage`, `test_pause_replication_race`, `test_replication_states`.

## Measurements

Open index scans:

| Check | Stock `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| One query, `LIMIT 10` SET of the scanned property, 2,000 indexed nodes | server aborts, exit 133, the lock-upgrade assertion | answers 10 |
| One query, `CALL {}` SET of the scanned property, 2,000 rows | server aborts, exit 133, the same assertion | answers 2,000 |
| Writer loop `LIMIT 5 SET n.x` with a `RESTORE` loop, 20 s | PING gets no reply from 0.2 s on; 0 writes and 0 `RESTORE` complete | no stall; 8,625 writes, 7,281 `RESTORE` |
| Same, the writer sets the scanned `n.id` | PING gets no reply from 0.2 s on; 0 writes | no stall; 7,018 writes, 7,290 `RESTORE` |
| Same, a `CALL {}` write per row of a 20,000-node scan | PING gets no reply from 0.2 s on; 0 writes | no stall; 361 writes, 467 `RESTORE` |
| Same, a `CALL {}` SET of the scanned `n.id` over 19,999 rows | server aborts at the first write | no stall; 8,438 writes, 8,396 `RESTORE` |

Pending count:

| Check | Stock `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| BGSAVE while one thread holds the pending-slots mutex (fault injection, below) | the child blocks in `futex_wait`; `rdb_bgsave_in_progress:1` after 30 s | BGSAVE finishes at once |
| 2,600 BGSAVE runs while 8 clients loop `CALL db.indexes()` on 64 or 256 indexes | 2,600 of 2,600 finish | not run |

- The second pending-count row shows that load alone rarely opens the window.
- The stock child blocks with this stack: `RawMutex::lock_slow`, `Indexer::index_info`, `Graph::index_info`, `encode_graph`, `rdb_save_graph_key`, `graph_rdb_save`, `rdbSaveObject`, then Redis's `rdbSaveBackground`.
- The open-scan rows ran on the open-scan commits alone, and the pending-count rows on the pending-count commit alone, each against stock `main`.

Environment:

- Host: Apple silicon, Docker linux/arm64 VM with 15 CPUs and 12 GB. Other containers on the host used about 2 of the 15 CPUs during the runs.
- Build: `cargo build --release` with the builder stage of `build/runtime/Dockerfile`, on `ghcr.io/falkordb/falkordb-build@sha256:b5d954ebaf523da2171bb6306c9348a767963f32e0e1f0a3b1115a66f1e397a7`.
- Runtime: each `falkordb.so` in the `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` image, which runs Redis 8.10.2, the `REDIS_VERSION` that `main` pins.
- Module arguments: the defaults for the single-query rows and the fault-injection row. The loop rows ran with `TIMEOUT_DEFAULT 30000 TIMEOUT_MAX 60000 RESULTSET_SIZE -1 MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES 200 NODE_CREATION_BUFFER 1024 CACHE_SIZE 10 QUERY_MEM_CAPACITY 268435456 ASYNC_DELETE no THREAD_COUNT 4`. The open-scan loop rows also ran Redis with `--maxmemory 6gb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --save '' --appendonly no`.

Method for the open-scan loop rows:

- Each row starts a new server.
- The loop rows use graph `g` with 20,000 `:D {id, x}` nodes and a range index on `:D(id)`.
- Client A loops the write. Client B loops `GRAPH.DELETE r` and `RESTORE r` of a 2,000-node graph with one range index.
- Client C sends PING every 200 ms with a 3 s timeout, and stops the row at the first unanswered PING.

## Repro: open index scans

Run these commands against a stock `main` server. The last command aborts the server.

```
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1, 2000) AS i CREATE (:W {v: i})"
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:W) ON (n.v)"
# wait until this prints OPERATIONAL
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CALL db.indexes() YIELD status RETURN status"
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n:W) WHERE n.v > 0 WITH n LIMIT 10 SET n.v = n.v + 100000 RETURN count(n)"
```

The server log shows `attempted to upgrade a spec read lock to a write lock`. With this PR the query returns 10.

The stall needs a writer and a `RESTORE` loop. On stock `main`, this Python script (redis-py) gets no PING reply within its first second:

```python
import threading, time
import redis
from redis.backoff import NoBackoff
from redis.retry import Retry

r = redis.Redis()
r.flushall()
r.execute_command("GRAPH.QUERY", "g", "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:D) ON (n.id)")
r.execute_command("GRAPH.QUERY", "g", "UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS i CREATE (:D {id: i, x: 0})")
r.execute_command("GRAPH.QUERY", "src", "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:T) ON (n.k)")
r.execute_command("GRAPH.QUERY", "src", "UNWIND range(1, 2000) AS i CREATE (:T {k: i})")
payload = r.dump("src")

def writer():
    c = redis.Redis()
    while True:
        c.execute_command("GRAPH.QUERY", "g", "MATCH (n:D) WHERE n.id > 0 WITH n LIMIT 5 SET n.x = n.x + 1")

def restorer():
    c = redis.Redis()
    while True:
        c.delete("r")
        c.restore("r", 0, payload)

for f in (writer, restorer):
    threading.Thread(target=f, daemon=True).start()
ping = redis.Redis(socket_timeout=2, retry=Retry(NoBackoff(), 0))
for _ in range(100):
    ping.ping()  # raises TimeoutError on stock main
    time.sleep(0.2)
print("no stall")
```

## Repro: pending count, setup

A fork has to land while another thread holds the mutex. This repro makes that certain: it patches one instruction of the running server, so that a population worker spins inside the mutex. The patch runs as root in a sidecar container that shares the server's PID namespace and has `SYS_PTRACE`.

On a debug build, a debugger in non-stop mode does the same job. Stop the population thread on a line inside `try_decrement_pending_for_generation`, after the lock. Run BGSAVE while the thread is stopped.

## Repro: pending count, procedure

1. Find the offset for your `falkordb.so` with `objdump -d`: the first instruction after the lock in `Indexer::release_population_ticket`. On the arm64 build of `ec2448f` it is `0x38c188`: `ldr x8, [x21, #24]`, bytes `a8 0e 40 f9`.
2. Run `redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1, 100) AS i CREATE (:P {v: i})"`.
3. Run the script below with the server's PID and the offset. It writes `b .` (`00 00 00 14`) over that instruction through `/proc/<pid>/mem`.
4. Run `redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:P) ON (n.v)"`. The population worker spins at the patched instruction with the mutex held.
5. Run `redis-cli BGSAVE`, then `redis-cli INFO persistence` every few seconds.

On stock `main`, `rdb_bgsave_in_progress` stays at `1`. With this PR it returns to `0` at once.

```python
import sys
off = int(sys.argv[2], 16)
base = None
for line in open(f"/proc/{sys.argv[1]}/maps"):
    f = line.split()
    if len(f) >= 6 and f[5].endswith("/falkordb.so") and int(f[2], 16) == 0:
        base = int(f[0].split("-")[0], 16)
        break
with open(f"/proc/{sys.argv[1]}/mem", "r+b", buffering=0) as mem:
    mem.seek(base + off)
    assert mem.read(4) == bytes.fromhex("a80e40f9")
    mem.seek(base + off)
    mem.write(bytes.fromhex("00000014"))
```

## Notes

- Memory and time: each scan that is open at commit time keeps its remaining results in a buffer until the operator drops it. That is 8 bytes per node id and 24 bytes per edge, plus 8 bytes per result for a scored query. The first commit also pays for reading the rest of the scan.
- The list of open queries is per thread. A query creates its scans and commits on one thread, the worker or the main thread of an inline session.
- The test is numbered `test13` because open PR #3098 adds `test12` to the same file.
- This PR and #3098 both change `bump_id`. The second of the two to merge keeps both lines.

## Commits

- `fix(index): release open index scans before a query becomes a writer`
- `perf(runtime): drop LIMIT's input once the limit is met`
- `fix(index): read the pending count without the pending-slots mutex`
- `docs(index): state that pending_count reads a lock-free copy`

pulls.body: resolve: #3183 --- ## Summary by cubic 4.22.1 patch release: truncated, corrupt, or malformed RDB payloads now fail the load cleanly instead of crashing the server or silently building partial graphs, and `RESTORE ... REPLACE` no longer decodes into a live graph of the same name. **Bug Fixes** - Declares `REDISMODULE_OPTIONS_HANDLE_IO_ERRORS` so Redis passes short reads (diskless-replication stream drops, truncated RESTORE/MIGRATE payloads, cut dump files) to the decoders instead of panicking; the partial graph is torn down. - Decoders check serialized counts, ids, strings, matrices, indexes, and constraints against the payload framing; violations set a sticky error that aborts the load and logs `Failed loading graph key '': `. - `RESTORE ...
